# VisualCore — Fully Specified, Desktop-Driven iOS Graphics Suite

**Edition:** 2026-11-10, revised for **Claude Code in the Claude Desktop app**  
**Primary execution surface:** Claude Desktop → **Code** tab → **local folder** on the project Mac  
**Scope:** reusable VisualCore framework, existing ProjectM-iOS reference integration, VisualCore Showcase, **25 independent iOS/iPadOS applications**, complete simulator/unit testing, and a **single contiguous, sequenced three-device qualification campaign**  
**Inputs preserved:** original VisualCore README, AppsBrainstorm, all 25 app manuals and indexes, original ProjectM-iOS `CLAUDE.md`, owner-provided `devices.md`, and the previous CLI-oriented runbook (historical only)  
**Companion file:** the separately supplied root **`CLAUDE.md`** in this deliverable; use both files together.

> **Start here; do not run historical commands from the appendices.** The first sections of this README are the updated controlling implementation specification. The remainder preserves complete source documents without deleting an app feature, algorithm, file layout, test requirement or prior lesson. Historical CLI instructions are archived solely to prevent loss of context: **do not execute `claude -p`, `claude --print`, a Claude Agent SDK runner, or the old Python supervisor.** Claude itself runs in the Desktop **Code** tab, and Python runs only deterministic build, audit, ledger and Apple-tool operations.

> **Execution boundary:** the user has delegated normal engineering decisions and wants no routine dialogue. That does not constitute authority to manufacture Apple signing credentials, grant permissions in someone else's name, unlock hardware, enroll in paid agreements, purchase apps, disable safety checks, change D3's OS, or publish to App Store Connect. Desktop Auto mode reduces routine prompts but may still require approvals; account quotas, app restarts, background scheduling, security gates and device locks can interrupt a run. The workflow checkpoints progress and resumes in a new Desktop session or configured local scheduled task; it cannot guarantee a single never-ending agent session.

## 1. Authoritative architecture and design corrections

### 1.1 Mission

Build **one engineering system** that serves 25 distinct, fully functioning products, instead of 25 disconnected demo scenes or copies of ProjectM. The framework must support correct GPU resource ownership, portable scene/effect interfaces, strong native iOS accessibility, testable numerical behavior and sustainable performance. Build an independent Showcase to prove the API. Retain ProjectM-iOS as a pinned integration reference and avoid entangling new apps with its proprietary-to-the-engine preset and visualizer abstractions.

**Mandatory dependency direction:**

```text
   25 application targets             VisualCore Showcase
       |    native SwiftUI/UIKit UI, product models and feature logic  |
       +---------------------+---------------------------------------+
                             v
                 App-specific rendering adapters
                             v
       VisualCore public APIs (life cycle, input, scenes,
       geometry, resources, shader pipeline, effects, metrics)
                             v
     source-audited EGL/OpenGL ES/ANGLE host integration boundary
                             v
           owner's ANGLE implementation --> Metal backend --> GPU

     External/projectm-ios (pinned, authoritative reference checkout)
       ├── its own Vendor/projectM (owner fork, ios branch)
       ├── its own Vendor/angle (owner fork, ios branch)
       └── reference tests, RendererLab/CaptureLab lessons

     ProjectM engine and presets are *not* required by unrelated apps.
```

The existing architecture is **not** a blank-slate renderer. ANGLE already translates the applicable OpenGL ES workflow to Metal in ProjectM-iOS. The new architecture therefore reuses the proven rendering integration rather than "factoring out ANGLE" as though the fork itself were a reusable Swift scene library. First audit the Objective-C++ glue, EGL display/context/surface lifecycle, thread affinity, ownership, license, exports, build scripts, CMake/XcodeGen, supported OS targets and binary linking. Establish a clean integration seam **around** that working implementation, potentially via a packageable adapter or XCFramework. Do not assume that moving files into SwiftPM magically makes the integration portable across process/target boundaries. Make the narrowest tracked upstream-ready patch only if actually required, and never silently mutate the pinned reference checkout.

### 1.2 Canonical decisions that supersede older advice

| ID | New controlling decision | Engineering effect |
|---|---|---|
| VC-001 | **Claude Desktop Code is the sole AI execution surface.** | No `claude` CLI launches, no `claude -p` and no model-calling Python supervisor. Desktop local sessions and optional **native local scheduled tasks** carry the work. |
| VC-002 | **Implement everything before physical devices.** | Host/unit/integration and simulator checks run during development. No `devicectl install/launch`, on-device XCTest or real-device benchmark until `IMPLEMENTATION-LOCK` passes for all 25 apps. |
| VC-003 | **One contiguous device campaign, three devices, fixed order D1 → D2 → D3.** | Device runbook processes all 25 apps on D1, then D2, then D3, storing 75 app-device rows and separate specialized scenarios. |
| VC-004 | **D3 must remain on iPadOS 26.5.** | Do not update, erase/restore or replace the D3 OS; it is the sole iOS 26 compatibility fixture. |
| VC-005 | One **development monorepo**, 25 separately shippable app targets. | Atomic cross-app API and regression changes. Older standalone-repo layouts are preserved as design options, not the unattended execution plan. |
| VC-006 | ProjectM reference checkout pinned/read-only by default. | No invisible submodule relocation/updates. The owner's ProjectM and ANGLE forks remain authoritative. |
| VC-007 | Existing ANGLE Metal backend remains canonical. | No unnecessary second renderer; shared wrapper reflects audited actual symbols, ownership and behavior. |
| VC-008 | Public, app-neutral VisualCore surface; no ProjectM engine dependency in 25 app targets. | Test dependency graph and link symbols, both source and built products. |
| VC-009 | Spec Kit Claude skills execute **inside Desktop conversation**. | `specify` CLI may initialize templates; `.claude/skills/speckit-*` used by Desktop model. Disable optional runtime events that would invoke Claude CLI. |
| VC-010 | Python is allowed only for deterministic provisioning, validation, project generation, reports and Apple tools. | No Python subprocess or API wrapper is allowed to invoke the Claude agent. |
| VC-011 | Durable file-backed stage ledger with independent check evidence. | A prose assertion never marks an app, phase, performance criterion or physical-device row passed. |
| VC-012 | Native app UI remains SwiftUI/UIKit with accessible controls. | GPU for graphics; platform UI for navigation, VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, permissions, display controls. |
| VC-013 | Scientific/render models are deterministic and versioned. | Numerical stability, reference measurements, atomic persistence, format validation and replay fixtures. |
| VC-014 | StoreKit is tested with local configurations/fake entitlement paths. | No live purchases, real Ask to Buy automation, credentials or agreements. |
| VC-015 | No App Store submission/purchase/remote publication based on this document alone. | Implementation and local testing are authorized work; releases and external administrative actions remain explicit owner gates. |
| VC-016 | Historical ProjectM milestones are engineering **reference evidence**, not new suite results. | Never copy ProjectM's passes into new apps' evidence; rerun appropriately. |
| VC-017 | Enforce narrow, public Apple APIs and feature truthfulness. | No private API, dlsym/dlopen, ReplayKit capture workarounds, assumed universal system audio or invented live wallpaper capability. |
| VC-018 | Prioritize feature fidelity over passing superficial smoke tests. | Each archived manual contributes distinct MVP, UX, algorithms, data formats, file layout, failure cases and acceptance criteria, all traced to code and tests. |
| VC-019 | Owner-device and human security boundaries remain real. | Developer Mode, signing/certificates, first-time OS permission prompts, device unlock, Store agreements must already be provisioned or be reported as blocked. |
| VC-020 | Cross-device results are named and versioned. | Report exact OS, build, model ID, hardware UDID kept private, Xcode build, revision, test run ID, thermal and latency metadata. |

### 1.3 Rules for conflicting material

Use this priority: **(1)** actual Apple/platform/tool observations and applicable security rules; **(2)** this updated canonical README and root CLAUDE.md; **(3)** generated project Spec Kit constitution and versioned ADRs, where not in conflict; **(4)** the detailed archived original visual-core architecture, app manuals, AppsBrainstorm and ProjectM lessons; **(5)** generated source code. Within archive-only product questions, the app-specific guide wins over a generic brainstorming description. Do not discard requirements merely because an archived source's command syntax is obsolete. Instead migrate requirement content and put obsolete mechanism under a documented compatibility note.

### 1.4 What "unattended" means here

The Desktop agent should never ask for ordinary code-organization, naming, minor API or task order decisions; it should choose the simplest defensible solution, write an ADR and proceed. **Auto** permission mode processes routine tool calls through its classifier; it does not override external permissions. Local Desktop scheduled tasks can create a fresh session against the same folder if configured, but they run only while Desktop is open and the computer is awake. No agent is guaranteed to finish a 25-app suite within a single uninterrupted context or account budget. Checkpointing is the strategy, not a fictional promise of unlimited unattended time.

## 2. Exact delivered scope and complete 25-app portfolio

### 2.1 Core deliverables

- An app-neutral VisualCore package hierarchy with documented stable APIs, threading/lifecycle contracts, compatibility checks and test fixtures.
- The audited existing ANGLE/EGL/OpenGL ES → Metal reference integration, repackaged minimally where possible; a separate ProjectM reference integration and regression suite.
- A reusable VisualCore Showcase with representative standalone effects and live lifecycle/context-loss diagnostics.
- All **25 app targets**, each complete through its individual seven-phase guide including MVP feature set, native UI, shaders/scene or simulation logic, persisted projects/presets as applicable, help/onboarding, privacy/accessibility, test fixtures and useful export/output.
- Complete versioned Spec Kit specifications, plans, contracts, tasks, acceptance fixtures, decisions, requirement-to-test traceability and a full portfolio test/release matrix.
- CI for source/docs/compliance and host/SIM builds, plus a separate macOS physical-device test harness that is dormant until implementation lock and operator provisioning.
- Actual machine-readable source/hardware/check evidence. Release status remains explicitly incomplete if any required criterion is not verified.

However, deterministic gate IDs are indexed by the original 01–25 roster; the Desktop controller can apply a dependency-aware wave order *only if* the gate manifest and helper are updated together before work begins. **Default, simpler unattended ordering:** foundation → app 01 through app 25, ensuring an unambiguous stable resume state. This does not change the wave-specific implementation decisions in the underlying manuals.

### 2.3 App success standards

Every app must be a meaningful product, not a colored rectangle with a title. Each app gets independent identity, real working feature controls, at least its guide's documented core interaction and persistence, deterministic demo/sample data, stress and error scenarios, screenshot and accessibility fixtures and documented supported/non-supported platform features. A native target that compiles but lacks core UI/engine integration fails the implementation lock.

## 3. Claude Desktop: bootstrap, permissions, and autonomous continuation

### 3.1 Choose the right execution surface

1. Use the **macOS project Mac** that owns Xcode and the three paired devices. Install and sign in to **Claude Desktop**. Open **Code** (not ordinary Chat; not a cloud-only repository environment); choose the **local VisualCore project folder**.
2. Add both generated files at repository root, named **`README.md`** and **`CLAUDE.md`**. Start with one Code session, *Worktree off for the integration controller*, and a model capable of long-form coding. The direct session can run Python, Git, Spec Kit CLI for setup, `xcodebuild` and Apple tools through its terminal tool; it does **not** launch `claude` as an executable.
3. Choose **Auto** permission mode when available and trusted. Current Claude Desktop documents Manual, Accept edits, Plan, Auto and Bypass. **Auto** is the preferred unattended-safe tradeoff: routine actions are classified, but exceptional calls may prompt. **Never select Bypass as a default**, particularly on the owner's signed Mac. If Auto is unavailable, document the mode limitation; Accept edits alone may still prompt for shell/test commands.
4. Trust the local folder and grant limited appropriate tool approvals before starting the long run. Provision Apple signing and Git access separately, without committing tokens or teams. Use no computer-use UI automation to bypass prompts/trust dialogs.
5. Prevent Mac idle sleep for local runs, leave Claude Desktop open, and monitor storage/thermal/disk. The app's native **Scheduled tasks** can resume from a checkpoint if the initial session finishes or the user wants recurring progress (Section 16). Local tasks start fresh Code sessions and require the Mac to be awake with Desktop open; they are not an external CLI bridge. Select a schedule supported by the installed UI; a normal hourly schedule is a reasonable choice.

**Published documentation:** [Claude Code Desktop](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop), [Desktop scheduled tasks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-scheduled-tasks), [Claude Code settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings), and [Spec Kit's Claude integration](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html). Tool versions, permissions and setting keys may change; inspect installed documentation before relying on a behavior.

### 3.2 Desktop sessions versus the old Python supervisor

The **old approach** spawned 186 external `claude -p` subprocesses with `dontAsk`. This is obsolete and expressly superseded. The **new approach**:

- Claude Desktop's Code session is the single AI worker and executes a **read → spec → implement → verify → checkpoint → next** loop via its own tools;
- `Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py` is **deterministic only** and cannot invoke Claude or call an LLM. It verifies original source hashes, extracts archived manuals for manageable context windows, writes a 263-gate JSON ledger, checks actual evidence file presence, executes and hashes real host/device test commands through `run-check`/`seal`, and refuses device gates before implementation lock;
- Native **local scheduled tasks** or an explicitly resumed Desktop Code session can read the ledger and continue the next gate, without guessing from the last chat's words;
- A lock directory prevents two integration sessions from racing on the same state/build output. Analytical subagents can work in isolated worktrees; the primary writer controls spec/project files, `project.yml`, build tools, `.specify` and integration commits;
- failed or blocked checks remain failed or blocked, not silently auto-approved;
- no Python code pretends to provide Desktop's model inference API, session reactivation, or permission grants.

### 3.3 Scope of standing delegation

The instruction to continue unattended authorizes routine engineering judgment: local source modifications, repository-local docs/specs, new test fixtures, small commits, build/test commands and retry repairs. It does **not** silently authorize pushing to the new repository's `origin/main`; the original ProjectM guide's push authorization applied to its original repository. Do not reset a dirty checkout, delete the ANGLE dependency tree, upgrade D3, modify signing teams/certificates/profiles, accept paid agreements, purchase products, create App Store Connect IAP records, or submit applications. Record these as `BLOCKED_OWNER_ACTION` when absolutely necessary.

### 3.4 Session/checkpoint protocol

Each fresh Desktop session, including a scheduled task, does the following:

```bash
# Run INSIDE Claude Desktop Code's tools/terminal, not an external Claude CLI:
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py validate
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py status
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py next
```

Acquire a stable integration lease such as:

```bash
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py claim --owner desktop-local-session-001
```

Choose a unique owner string per new session, never guess that an existing lock is stale. Reclaim a genuinely abandoned lock only after verifying no other Desktop session is active. Complete a bounded gate, attach evidence, and call `record` (Section 17), then repeat. Release the lease at the session's end:

```bash
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py release --owner desktop-local-session-001
```

To reduce token pressure, the session **never loads the entire 1.6 MB source archive into the conversation**. Read controlling chapters and the *one relevant extracted* `.autonomy/context/apps/<nn>-<name>.md`; the bootstrap extracts all complete manuals and checks hashes. `CLAUDE.md` stays concise enough to load at session start.

Use XcodeGen `project.yml` and an ignored generated `.xcodeproj` when compatible with the original ProjectM toolchain; pin XcodeGen version and SHA-256. Do not generate 25 incompatible, manually edited `.xcodeproj` files. Keep third-party dependency sources pinned as submodules under the owning reference. Do not commit large shader caches, build artifacts, Apple's derived data, binary preview videos, device container dumps or generated indexes. App-specific file diagrams in all 25 manuals remain the detailed implementation source, not a duplicate common layout to be imposed blindly.

### 4.1 Module contracts that must be proven with code

The following are conceptual names and must be reconciled against the actual engine symbols:

- **Renderer host:** create/destroy/make-current EGL surfaces; capability checks; framebuffer and presentation contracts; orientation/viewport changes; foreground/background; background audio restrictions; coherent error handling.
- **Resource allocator:** explicit per-frame budgets; ownership and reusable pools; first-frame shader compilation; context-loss recreation; deterministic GL state hygiene; test counters.
- **Effect pipeline:** render passes with explicit inputs/outputs/color space/resolution, graph cycle detection, compositing/sampling conventions, dependency ordering and shader timeouts/quotas.
- **Input and scenes:** native gesture translation; reproducible camera, coordinate and units; fixed-step simulation separate from frame presentation; domain logic testable with a fake clock.
- **Audio:** microphone, in-app playback, and system capture only when official iOS-version/API permissions and diagnostics permit; `CaptureManager`/normalizer lessons from ProjectM preserved; no lock-wait syscalls or allocations on realtime callback and no false source claims.
- **Persistence:** version-tagged models, checksummed import where useful, migration tests, atomic writes and failures that do not erase previous user work.
- **Accessibility:** native VoiceOver fields, native text/controls, Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing, touch target sizes, color differentiation, comfort mode and fallback for inaccessible graphics.
- **Diagnostics:** measured startup stages, first frame, on-time refresh slots, CPU/GPU/memory, thermal state, asset load, permission reasons and device provenance.

### 4.2 One writer, many reviewers

Allow research/review/test-fixture subagents as needed but no more than **10 across the entire workload**. Agents produce scratch reports or isolated worktrees; **one writer per repo file** merges changes. `tasks.md`, `spec.md`, contracts, `project.yml` and key bridge source are owned by the integration session. Avoid concurrent Xcode builds and all physical-device jobs on a single Mac. Prefer sequential compilation while expensive ANGLE builds run; if running subagents, do not assume an agent report proves a task. Inspect diff and rerun tests before checking the task off.

## 5. Strict implementation-first schedule and stage gates

### 5.1 The only permitted macro-sequence

```text
CAMPAIGN I — COMPLETE IMPLEMENTATION (NO PHYSICAL DEVICES)
  F00–F09   : VisualCore audit, architecture, integration, packages,
              diagnostics, Showcase, reference regression, documentation
  A01-P00..P06 : Generative Art Studio, all seven phases
  A02-P00..P06 : Fluid Art Playground, all seven phases
  ...
  A25-P00..P06 : Effects Composer, all seven phases
  HOST-AUDIT : full clean Xcode build; all target/host/unit/integration/
               simulator tests, docs, source map, licensing/security scans
  IMPLEMENTATION-LOCK : machine-verifiable 25/25 complete implementation
                      and 25/25 verified build + unit + simulator artifact rows

CAMPAIGN II — ALL PHYSICAL-DEVICE TESTS, IN ONE ORDERED BLOCK
  D1-A01 ... D1-A25  : all 25 apps, iPhone 15 iOS 27.0.1
  D2-A01 ... D2-A25  : all 25 apps, iPad Pro M5 iPadOS 27.2
  D3-A01 ... D3-A25  : all 25 apps, iPad A16 iPadOS 26.5
  DEVICE-RECONCILE   : targeted fixes + repeat all impacted on-device tests
  SUITE-FINAL        : independent audit of true evidence, final report
```

**Hard constraint:** `scripts/run_device_campaign.py`, or any direct `xcrun devicectl device install`/`device process launch` or physical `xcodebuild test`, must call `python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py guard-device` **and exit nonzero** unless the implementation lock is confirmed. A physical-device build targeting `generic/platform=iOS` without connecting/installing is permitted as a *compilation check* in Campaign I; **that is not a device test**. Automated simulators also remain permitted in Campaign I. There is no early "smoke test on D1" exception, even if graphics risk is higher without early hardware proof: honor the requested all-implementation-first sequence and compensate with ANGLE host unit/simulator/generic-device compilation and reference evidence.

### 5.2 Ten foundation gates (F00–F09)

| Gate | Implement | Exit evidence before next gate |
|---|---|---|
| F00 | Unmodified ProjectM reference audit; verify owner fork pins, licenses, build scripts, ANGLE size and project toolchain; inventory devices **without testing** | audit report, actual symbol/build graph, pinned refs, commands and logs |
| F01 | Spec Kit constitution, master architecture contracts, ADRs, source-to-requirement mapping, repo layout and standards | validated constitution, real Spec Kit artifacts, source hash report |
| F02 | Package/bridge the existing ANGLE EGL context/surface loop; lifecycle and platform capability negotiation | independent minimal GLES scene rendering on simulator, native build artifacts |
| F03 | GPU resources/shaders, safe caches, color-space, viewport/texture/FBO lifecycle and memory quotas | shader fixtures, tests, resource leak/cycle checks and simulator run |
| F04 | Shared effects/graph/passes, deterministic control and cross-pass error recovery | multi-pass effect fixtures, cycle reject tests, simulator previews |
| F05 | Touch/animation/camera/scene and deterministic simulation helpers | replay/resize/background CPU tests and simulator UI checks |
| F06 | Full VisualCore Showcase with native accessible UI and multiple true renderer capabilities | Showcase Xcode scheme, functioning scenes and tests |
| F07 | ProjectM reference adapter/regression suite without changing engine semantics | reference build/regression logs; any upstream patch formally tracked |
| F08 | Second independent consumer test (not ProjectM), plus optional audio feature bridge | real modular dependency proof, crash/relaunch/teardown tests |
| F09 | Framework stabilization, public interfaces, doc sites, privacy/licensing/CI, automation harness skeleton | clean CI and simulator/generic-iOS builds; all foundation acceptance |

Original foundation Phase 0–9 detailed prompts, commands, and architecture diagrams are preserved in archived `sources/README.md`. Enforce the stronger current policies above where old text suggests unreviewed source moves or a new backend.

### 5.3 Seven phases for EACH app (175 app gates)

Each `apps/<nn>-<slug>.md` manual contains detailed app-specific tasks. Map its original Phase 00–06 to the following and retain each unique scenario, data fixture, file layout, algorithm and release criterion:

| Phase | Minimum work (all 25 apps) | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| P00 — audit/spec | read full manual; create application constitution alignment, risk, feature contracts, privacy/asset review and app README | requirements with IDs, tests and source-line references |
| P01 — model/shell | domain models, versioning, native UI skeleton, navigation, state persistence, accessible controls | host unit and basic simulator UI tests |
| P02 — real graphics | independent VisualCore adapter, actual ANGLE-scene rendering, lifecycle and frame scheduling | GPU scene evidence in simulator; reproducible fixtures |
| P03 — full MVP | implement **every mandatory** product workflow from app manual (not a toy sample) | feature unit/integration/UI tests with negative cases |
| P04 — rich experience | presets/content, editing/export, undo/migration, onboarding, error handling as defined | stable content parsing and snapshot/export validation |
| P05 — quality | resource quotas, accessibility, privacy, localization readiness, crash/fuzz tests, performance strategy | automated tests, static checks and simulator captures |
| P06 — implementation complete | app build, all documented MVP criteria, release metadata/tests/fixtures, true failure states and evidence | independent full target and simulator verification; no physical device action |

**Do not create 175 separate branches solely for bookkeeping.** Use feature specs or bounded tasks that fit the actual Spec Kit installation; stage IDs are ledger checkpoints and can map to a sensible number of real Spec Kit feature documents. Each feature uses unique requirement (FR), success criterion (SC), risk (R) and task (T) identifiers, with doc validation catching duplicates.

### 5.4 Implementation lock: stricter than file counts

Before authorizing device campaign Claude must:

1. Discover actual project/workspace and Xcode schemes; emit `docs/verification/full-suite-implementation.json` containing **exactly 25 unique app_slug values**, actual scheme and bundle ID, manifest status pass, and existing build, host/unit test and simulator `.xcresult` artifacts per app.
2. Run a fresh aggregate `xcodebuild` build of all 25 app targets, Showcase and referenced packages on the pinned toolchain; run host/SIM tests, Xcode project generation, native `.xcframework` link checks, app capability reviews, source/docs/compliance checks, full asset indexing, shader fixtures and every required P06 acceptance check. Reject any skipped mandatory test.
3. Inspect outputs to ensure real apps have nonplaceholder functionality. Enforce no ProjectM engine dependency in new app symbols, no private APIs, no signing credentials in Git, no debug automation code in shipping Release, stable deployment target suitable for D3 and no dynamic-loading capture hacks.
4. Produce `docs/verification/implementation-lock-report.md`, including real commands, exit statuses, Xcode/SDK and commit hash, substantive unimplemented-feature audit, app-by-app requirements, known platform limits and build artifacts.
5. Mark `IMPLEMENTATION-LOCK` with a file-backed JSON evidence record. The embedded helper validates the 25 app artifact paths and refuses device runs without a passed lock and all **185** preceding implementation gates.

At this point *implementation is complete but hardware qualification is untested*. Only now start D1 physical-device tests. If one app fails lock, fix that app and rerun cross-app regressions; don't prematurely run any device test.

### 5.5 Repair during device qualification

After lock, the code base is functionally frozen except for **targeted** repairs that unblock genuine device-specific defects. Record the failing test first, use smallest reproducible patch, rerun affected app's source/simulator checks and *all affected real devices*, and append fresh evidence instead of overwriting historical failed attempts. A shared-bridge change invalidates prior device rows affected by that change; mark them stale and rerun before final certification. Do not quietly add post-MVP features during physical qualification. Preserve lock history; document any change to the certified revision and reconcile it at `DEVICE-RECONCILE`.

## 6. Spec Kit operation entirely within Desktop Code

### 6.1 Install/init without invoking Claude CLI

On the project Mac, use Spec Kit's own CLI only as a **scaffolding** tool. It is not the Claude Code CLI. Inspect existing directories first and preserve the supplied root CLAUDE.md.

```bash
python3 --version
git --version
uv --version
specify version
specify check
specify init --help
# ONLY when .specify has not already been set up and the current directory is the project:
specify init --here --force --non-interactive \
  --integration claude --script py --ignore-agent-tools \
  --integration-options="--events false"
# If .specify already exists but the Claude skill integration is missing:
specify integration install claude --script py --integration-options="--events false"
# Examine installed skill files (no guessing):
find .claude/skills -maxdepth 2 -name SKILL.md -print
```

`--ignore-agent-tools` avoids an unnecessary requirement to install the standalone Claude CLI executable merely to use **Desktop Code**. `--events false` is important because current Spec Kit's Claude **runtime workflow dispatch** can call `claude -p` when events are enabled; this workflow deliberately does not use that dispatch. Preserve model-invocable skills; do **not** select `--no-model-invocation`. If a particular installed Spec Kit version changed these flags or adapter semantics, inspect `specify init --help` and the local skill files, choose an equivalent direct Desktop-safe path, and record the version-specific decision. **Never use `--force` blindly to overwrite established files.** Initialize only after the new repo's preflight/backup is clean.

The supported Spec Kit initialization source is [official documentation](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/reference/core.html); [Claude integration](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html). The old README's `--ai claude` and dotted slash commands are obsolete for the specified current skills integration.

### 6.2 Invoke skills in the Desktop conversation, not terminal subprocesses

In the **Claude Desktop Code prompt field**, model-invocable commands use the names actually installed in `.claude/skills`, normally:

```text
/speckit-constitution
/speckit-specify
/speckit-clarify
/speckit-plan
/speckit-checklist
/speckit-tasks
/speckit-analyze
/speckit-implement
/speckit-converge
```

Some skills may not be in the installed core or extension; use `find .claude/skills ...` and inspect `SKILL.md` to confirm. A missing `/speckit-converge`, for example, is handled by an explicit independent acceptance sweep rather than a fabricated tool call. Spec Kit-generated files are the source of stage feature IDs and tests, not magic evidence that code runs.

**Protocol for each feature/phase** (repeat intelligently across 10 framework stages and each of 25 app manuals):

1. **`/speckit-specify`** — provide product-specific scope/requirements/nonfunctional constraints, link to exact archived source manual paths and acceptance matrix; identify platform capability limits upfront.
2. **`/speckit-clarify`** — choose routine defaults under owner delegation, record options/reasons; do not claim to have accepted owner signing or App Store decisions.
3. **`/speckit-plan`** — real source audit, ABI/render context, package graph, task-level milestones, actual Xcode targets, tests first where practical; no invented APIs.
4. **`/speckit-checklist`** — privacy/security/portability/completeness, testability and device-environment distinctions; if not installed, implement equivalent versioned review doc.
5. **`/speckit-tasks`** — small bounded tasks with dependencies, unique IDs, `device` vs `host` labels, and real acceptance commands; no blanket "done" tasks.
6. **`/speckit-analyze`** — detect and repair spec/plan/tasks inconsistency and manual-to-implementation omissions before implementation.
7. **`/speckit-implement`** — write real code/fixtures; do not stop at planning or scaffolding. Host/SIM tests are allowed. Stop early only for a true external blocker.
8. **`/speckit-converge`**, if installed, plus independent compiler/test validation and a diff review — mark tasks done only with `— Verified YYYY-MM-DD: <command>, <fixture>, <result>`.
9. Generate evidence JSON for the stage and invoke the deterministic `record` command only on a genuine successful check; commit bounded verified work and proceed to the next unlocked stage.

### 6.3 Example app-specific prompt format

> Build **App 08 Oscilloscope Studio**, stage `A08-P03`, after reading `.autonomy/context/apps/08-oscilloscope-studio.md` in full and the applicable VisualCore audio/rendering package contracts. Invoke the installed Spec Kit skills from **this Desktop Code session**, not `claude` subprocesses. Implement the manual's complete waveform/timebase/trigger MVP, calibration behavior, permission/route state, saved projects and error handling; use synthetic/audio fixture signals for host/SIM unit tests. Never claim generic Spotify/Apple Music capture. Create real tests for signal timing, clipping, trigger and frame-display coherence. Produce logs and a stage evidence JSON with actual commands and exits, record the gate, and continue to the next gate. Do not run any physical-device operation before `IMPLEMENTATION-LOCK`.

Every other app's full manual defines its equivalent specialized prompt; do not replace it with the oscilloscope template.

## 7. Shared renderer and ProjectM integration engineering

### 7.1 Preserve proven internals and fork provenance

From the owner's original ProjectM-iOS agent guide (source archive): `Vendor/projectM` belongs to `Coastrnaut/projectm` on `ios` branch; engine changes become isolated upstream-ready commits logged in `docs/projectm-patches.md`. `Vendor/angle` belongs to `Coastrnaut/angle` on `ios` branch and may include a ~12 GB `gclient sync` working dependency tree. Preserve the existing runtime topology and fork identity. The older guide recorded the owner fork ProjectM revision `c88894e` during a specific November 2026 milestone, and ProjectM 1.0 had a separate App Store upload state. These are **historical** milestones; discover the actual submodule revision at checkout, do not reset or declare new successes from old tests.

Never run `git clean -fdx` within these dependency trees. Before editing the host bridge, locate actual source headers, C++/Objective-C++ boundaries, EGL current-context rules, frame presentation, build settings and feature flags in the pinned checkout. Build `projectm` and ANGLE XCFrameworks with the owning project's actual scripts (historically `python3 scripts/build_projectm_xcframework.py` and `python3 scripts/build_angle_xcframework.py`) rather than drafting a second build system from scratch.

### 7.2 Correct render/context lifecycle

Enforce explicit state transitions: `uninitialized → surfaceReady → active → suspended → surfaceInvalid → reinitialized → destroyed`, with recoverable errors for unsupported runtime/capability, EGL allocation, context loss, background transition, orientation and app memory pressure. Track GPU handles against owning EGL context/generation. GPU lifetime and Swift task lifetime are not the same. Test reentrancy, pauses, resize/rebuild, rapid scene changes, background/foreground, color/scale and app termination with real native surfaces in simulator; defer all real-device sweeps until the campaign.

### 7.3 Rendering independence and content

VisualCore APIs represent snapshots, frame-time, GLES-compatible draw and effects contracts. New apps own their shader code, domain models and assets until cross-app reuse is established with independent evidence. No ProjectM plugin ABI/preset loader should leak into the common APIs. Test static link maps and exported symbols to prove isolation; use compile-time feature flags only when actually supported by the owner forks. Keep metadata, copyright, licenses and content provenance for every shader/asset that enters an App Store bundle.

### 7.4 Performance lessons from original ProjectM tests

Do not repeat known mistakes: async network product requests should not block a local entitlement/library UI; use `async let` for independent startup operations. Pre-sort large build-time indexes so Swift's runtime sort is cheap; the original guide recorded a D1 index-load improvement **157 ms → 106 ms** under that specific optimization. Shader compilation on the first frame can dominate preset-switch time; measure **load** separately from **first rendered frame**. The original preset-switch metric SC-104 was borderline (**96%** of samples passing after **92%** on an earlier 50-ish sample run, against 95% target); test at least **200** independent samples for percentage gates. These are prior observations, not quantitative targets automatically achieved by new apps.

## 8. Product engineering, data, accessibility, security and release policy

### 8.1 Domain correctness

- **Fluid, particle, ray, physics, fractal, solar/orbital and general simulation apps:** use deterministic fixed-step updates, explicit units/camera conventions, reference fixtures, overflow and NaN/Infinity policies, saved reproducible seed/configuration, bounded iteration count; compare against independent CPU/reference formulas.
- **Waveform, audio and music apps:** source selection and authorization exposed natively, correctly labeled `unavailable`, permission denial, route and interruptions; lock-free/no-allocation real-time audio processing, bounded FFT buffer/latency and secure non-retention of captured audio by default. Do not infer broader system capture from ProjectM's limited device experiment.
- **Anatomy, molecular and astronomy apps:** licensed validated datasets, source/revision notes, uncertainty when necessary, a content accuracy review independent from shader realism. Anatomy is education, not personal diagnosis or treatment.
- **Shader Studio, Visual Programming Lab and Effects Composer:** untrusted code/graphs/resources are bounded; reject cycles/invalid file paths, limit GPU passes, texture memory, compilation/runs, handle loss gracefully and validate import/export version migrations.
- **Living Wallpapers, Ambient Clock, Aurora and zen/ambient apps:** use actual iOS APIs for exported animation/video or still art; never claim the system supports a third-party always-running animated home screen. Respect battery, brightness, Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing and thermal comfort.

### 8.2 Native UX/accessibility

SwiftUI/UIKit owns screen/navigation labels, accessible controls, configuration/help and privacy prompts; GPU owns image output. Implement native Dynamic Type, VoiceOver labels, actionable automation IDs, iPhone/iPad layouts, landscape/portrait behavior as appropriate, Reduce Motion, Reduce Flashing, non-color-only state cues and meaningful empty/permission-denied/error states. Reuse the original ProjectM accessibility and flashing tests as a *method*, not proof.

### 8.3 StoreKit and privacy test discipline

Use StoreKit 2 with `Transaction.currentEntitlements` and `Transaction.updates` where an app truly sells content; never persist an invented unlock bool. Local `.storekit` configurations must not contain a synced `_applicationInternalID`. The app hosting unit tests must switch to a fake store on `XCTestConfigurationFilePath`, avoiding product requests before `SKTestSession` initializes. UI tests unrelated to buying run with a fixed fake entitlement (`-uitestUnlocked NO` was the original example); no actual Ask to Buy flow or Apple Account sign-in in automation. Split the `pending` transaction handler into pure testable code and drive test purchases through `SKTestSession` APIs.

Each app's built product must have a checked `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`, required-reason API inventory, purpose strings, asset attributions, cryptography export declaration such as `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption` if applicable, truthful privacy policy/report and a review notes draft. These do not authorize app publication. Check actual dependency graph and compiled/bundled product; a checked-in manifest alone does not prove compliance.

### 8.4 Compliance and owner-only actions

Public Apple APIs only. The original ProjectM compliance script forbade private APIs, `dlopen`/`dlsym`, ReplayKit capture workarounds and networking in its own app, and its CI enforced it. Port the appropriate constraints with testable scanners; do not assume the no-network rule applies to every potential new product without a threat/privacy analysis. No use of arbitrary background audio capture, unsupported Screen Recording entitlements or circumvented OS prompts. Device and account permissions remain owner-provisioned. Record LGPL/other license analysis for actual binary usage and compile flags; don't blindly relicense copied content.

## 9. Dedicated Apple build-host environment

### 9.1 Known owner Mac reference (historical, must reverify)

The original owner guide reported the project Mac at **Xcode 27.2 (27B52)**, iOS SDK 27.2, **Swift 6.4.2**, **XcodeGen 2.46.0**, **CMake 4.4.5**, and available iOS **27.2** and **26.5 (23F77)** simulators. The original GitHub Actions CI used a mainstream macOS image for iOS 26.5 plus an `xcode-27` preview image for 27.2, weak-linking capability checks where needed. These are a **recorded reference**, not a guarantee that today's host still has those versions; verify and pin rather than upgrade blindly. App and weak-linked ScreenCaptureKit code paths differ with SDK and OS availability; check actual system capabilities on runtime, not compiler-only tests.

### 9.2 Preflight commands in Desktop's integrated terminal

```bash
pwd
xcode-select -p
xcodebuild -version
xcrun swift --version
xcrun simctl list -j devices available
xcrun devicectl list devices --json-output .autonomy/reports/device-discovery.json
xcrun xcresulttool help get test-results summary
xcodegen --version
cmake --version
python3 --version
git --version
specify version
```

No `claude --version`/`claude -p`: **Claude Code itself is already running inside Desktop**. A terminal preflight may inspect Spec Kit's independent `specify` tool, but do not install the Claude CLI as a backend. On macOS, a full Xcode application and selected developer directory are required, not just Command Line Tools. Validate `xcodebuild -showdestinations`, signing/provisioning visibility and the three device hardware model identifiers **without launching tests** during implementation campaign.

For unsigned simulator and generic SDK compiler smoke checks:

```bash
xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -list -json -project <DISCOVERED_PROJECT>.xcodeproj
xcodebuild -project <DISCOVERED_PROJECT>.xcodeproj \
  -scheme <DISCOVERED_APP_SCHEME> -configuration Debug \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
xcodebuild -project <DISCOVERED_PROJECT>.xcodeproj \
  -scheme <DISCOVERED_APP_SCHEME> -configuration Debug \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Replace angle-bracket examples with discovered paths/schemes; **do not copy placeholders into actual scripts**. Run using a Python subprocess with explicit timeout and file-backed stdout/stderr where necessary; don't pipe build logs through `sort`/`tail` and mistake buffering for a hang. Build ProjectM/ANGLE frameworks first with documented scripts; they may consume large disk/time. Run check scripts before every task commit and after changes to dependencies.

### 9.3 User's Windows host and macOS requirement

Windows 11 may host Claude Desktop, source editing and remote orchestration, but Xcode's build, Apple simulator and real-device testing must execute **on the project Mac**. For completely local 25-app CI/device qualification, prefer Claude Desktop **Code** running locally on that Mac. The Code tab supports SSH sessions, but a remote Mac must have full appropriate privileges and reliable connected devices; SSH mode may lack certain Desktop previews and local UI. Avoid unsupported macOS-in-Hyper-V claims or replacing Apple device tests with remote simulation.

Do not infer that they are currently connected/unlocked; `devicectl` must confirm observed device availability and OS before the physical campaign.

| ID | Device | Device name | Part number | OS | Build | Product type/model identifier | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **D1** | **iPhone 15** | `iPhone77` | `MTLV3LL/A` | **iOS 27.0.1** | `24A446` | **`iPhone15,4`** | Primary reference iPhone; system/app capture candidate, microphone and in-app playback |
| **D2** | **iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)** | `iPad77` | `MDYJ4LL/A` | **iPadOS 27.2** | `24B119` | **`iPad17,3`** | High-performance iPad; system/app capture candidate, microphone and in-app playback |

## 11. Single batched physical-device campaign — D1, then D2, then D3

### 11.1 Freeze the implementation first

`python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py guard-device` **must pass** before any real-device install, launch, XCTest, performance run or manual qualification. Build and sign all app variants against discovered schemes and approved signing settings, but do not touch a physical device during the implementation campaign. Record a new device-campaign run ID, git revision and Xcode/SDK fingerprint; a shared-code patch during the campaign invalidates all previously measured affected apps and requires retesting.

### 11.2 Deterministic campaign schedule (75 mandatory rows)

```
D1: iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 — TEST 01→25 in order, one device/app at a time
  D1-A01 D1-A02 D1-A03 ... D1-A25
  For each app: install → launch → UI functional → renderer/lifecycle →
  app-specific checks → privacy/accessibility → calibrated performance →
  export reports → stop app → inspect .xcresult → record row → next app

D2: iPad Pro 13-inch M5, iPadOS 27.2 — TEST 01→25 in same order
  D2-A01 ... D2-A25 (additional large display/multitasking/resolution checks)

D3: iPad A16, iPadOS 26.5 — TEST 01→25 in same order
  D3-A01 ... D3-A25 (OS fallback, smaller compute/memory budget, audio fallback)

DEVICE-RECONCILE: run necessary targeted repeat checks, link attempts,
  certify that shared fixes did not invalidate earlier evidence.
SUITE-FINAL: report 25/25 compiled, 25/25 SIM-tested and 75/75 actual
  device/app certifications, or precise incomplete/blocked state.
```

The fixed order optimizes device setup/cooling, prevents simultaneous Xcode/device contention and makes failures reproducible. A specialized scenario may be `not_applicable` only if the product lacks that capability on that OS/device; **the entire app-device row remains mandatory**. For example, the iOS 26 System/App Capture mode is *correctly unavailable* on D3, but the music app itself still must install, launch, render and pass microphone/in-app playback fallback tests.

### 11.3 Concrete Apple tool commands (discover and verify current syntax)

```bash
# 1. Enumerate all owner devices. Do not guess UDIDs.
xcrun devicectl list devices --json-output .autonomy/reports/devices-before.json

# 2. Discover scheme/destination/actual team provisioning for each app.
xcodebuild -showdestinations \
  -project <ACTUAL_PROJECT>.xcodeproj -scheme <ACTUAL_SCHEME>

# 3. Device XCTest, with unique output and explicit timeouts.
xcodebuild test -project <ACTUAL_PROJECT>.xcodeproj \
  -scheme <ACTUAL_UI_TEST_SCHEME> -configuration Debug \
  -destination 'platform=iOS,id=<HARDWARE_UDID_FROM_DEVICECTL>' \
  -test-timeouts-enabled YES -default-test-execution-time-allowance 180 \
  -resultBundlePath .autonomy/xcresults/<RUN>/<D1|D2|D3>-<APP>.xcresult

# 4. Inspect the actual XCTest bundle; do not rely on stdout's success claim.
xcrun xcresulttool get test-results summary --path <ACTUAL_XCRESULT> --format json

# 5. For deterministic in-app stress modes, use devicectl's documented API.
xcrun devicectl device install app --device <ACTUAL_DEVICECTL_ID> <SIGNED_APP_PATH>
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device <ACTUAL_DEVICECTL_ID> \
  --terminate-existing --environment-variables '{"VISUALCORE_AUTORUN":"stress"}' \
  <ACTUAL_BUNDLE_ID>

# 6. Collect explicit app-owned report files, then terminate/clean up.
xcrun devicectl device info files --domain-type appDataContainer \
  --domain-identifier <ACTUAL_BUNDLE_ID> --json-output <REPORT_JSON>
xcrun devicectl device copy from --device <ACTUAL_DEVICECTL_ID> \
  --source Documents/<KNOWN_REPORT>.json --destination <PRIVATE_OUTPUT>
```

These are **templates** based on the original device-testing playbook. The exact `devicectl` subcommand flags must be checked with `xcrun devicectl ... --help` on Xcode 27.2 (or actual pinned toolchain); do not assume a sample invocation is correct. In particular the test destination needs **hardware UDID**, not the `devicectl` device ID. The example typo `<HARDWARE_UDID_FROM_DEVICECTL>` is descriptive only; in final scripts use the correct `devicectl` discovery object. Use proper file-backed log capture rather than piping through `tail`/`sort`.

### 11.4 In-app automation runner and testability

Each app must expose a private test-only instrumented mode **compiled only in `DEBUG || VISUALCORE_AUTOMATION`**, triggered by `VISUALCORE_AUTORUN=<mode>` in the launch environment. Instrumented **Release** builds with the automation condition are valid performance builds; *shipping Release* builds must have no automation code/symbols. Check with `nm -U` and binary diff or symbol scan. An automation mode writes a JSON report to the app's Documents container **and exits**, ensuring the device is free for the next app. Launch tests write one sample per launch, and the first launch after install can be reserved for onboarding. Disable any private automation features in production build and disallow remote injection of test modes.

Potential modes: `cold-launch`, `warm-launch`, `renderer-10m`, `context-recreate`, `rapid-switch`, `export-roundtrip`, `audio-internal`, `mic-consent-denied`, `navigation`, `asset-stress`, `shader-errors`, `snapshot`, `privacy-audit`, `reduce-flashing`. Implement only modes appropriate to each product, all with documented unit and frame definitions. App-specific specialized modes are recorded separately from mandatory app-device row status.

### 11.5 Device locking, system dialogs and true limitations

A launch that returns `Locked` is a real physical prerequisite failure, not a code defect. In the original ProjectM tests, the owner had to unlock D1/D2/D3 and set Auto-Lock to Never during the session. The new script must **not** call `input()` and hang waiting for Return. It should emit `BLOCKED_OWNER_ACTION` with exact device ID and actions needed and leave the gate incomplete. The same applies to first permission prompts, pairing/trust, signing, purchase sheets, system pickers or Airplane Mode toggles. Do not impersonate human authorization or misreport automated tests that did not run.

These are campaign **minimums**, not replacements for the full tests in each original per-app guide. Every row runs on D1, D2 and D3 after implementation lock, with extra OS/device conditions listed; all required modes also need valid host/SIM proofs before the lock.

| 05 Infinite Geometry | scene progression, camera interaction, clipping and geometry snapshot | aspect ratio 15/Pro/A16; no camera jumps |
| 06 VisualCore Music Lab | supported in-app playback, microphone permission/denial, FFT and first-frame metrics | D1/D2 iOS 27 capture only if actually implemented and authorized; D3 capture unavailable |
| 07 Audio Odyssey | music-driven camera/visual scene, safe-motion modes, audio routing/stop | D3 audio fallback, Reduce Motion/Flashing, iPhone comfort |

| 11 Physics Playground | collisions/contact/resume, save/replay, no explosions/NaNs | device FPS affects visuals not numerical simulation |
| 12 Tiny Worlds | procedural scene switching, camera, asset streaming/budget | D3 smaller memory tier; iPad controls |
| 13 Light Maze | levels, ray intersection, exact reflection and win-state reproducibility | touch target differences and high-DPI render accuracy |

| 15 Molecular Explorer | molecule import/parse validation, bond geometry, selection/labels | fast rejection of invalid data and no D3 GPU OOM |

**Common per-app/device minimum:** signed install/launch, native UI flow, actual rendered scene, touch and accessibility, lifecycle pause/resume/resize where applicable, persisted state, saved export, privacy report, 10-minute sustained stress if app class warrants it, frame/memory/thermal trace and actual XCTest `.xcresult`. For performance percent gates gather at least **200 samples**, record IDs and first-frame timings separately from load; have explicit cool-down windows and never infer frames-per-second from a screenshot.

**Audio source compatibility rule from original ProjectM:** before claiming a particular external music app works, capture **ten minutes** of *non-silent* real-device CaptureLab diagnostic output on supported hardware and route it through documented evaluator checks (FR-031). Prior 20.8/22.4-second Spotify-containing diagnostic sessions were preliminary and do not meet the claim criterion. No microphone/system audio capture claim is justified solely by simulator behavior, a successful compile or a permission dialog.

## 13. Measurement, diagnostic artifacts and independent evidence

### 13.1 Evidence report structure

Every gate gets an actual JSON file and command log, for example:

```json
{
  "stage": "A01-P03",
  "status": "pass",
  "revision": "ACTUAL_REPOSITORY_COMMIT",
  "checks": [
    {
      "command": "swift test --package-path Packages/VisualCoreEffects",
      "exit_code": 0,
      "log": ".autonomy/logs/A01-P03.effects-test.log",
      "attestation": ".autonomy/checks/A01-P03.effects-test.json"
    }
  ],
  "artifacts": ["docs/verification/requirements-trace.json"],
  "notes": "Real tests were executed; this JSON must not be prefilled without logs."
}
```

For each physical-device gate, include the app's actual run ID, `device.role`, `device.product_type`, actual `device.hardware_udid` (private artifact), `device.os_version`, `device.is_simulator=false`, `xcresult` directory and `xcresult_summary="Passed"` only after independently executing `xcresulttool`, plus JSON diagnostics and all applicable mode results. The embedded state validator refuses to pass a device gate without the matching model, 26.5 D3 and an existing real `.xcresult` path. The *separate* project `scripts/verify_xcresults.py` should parse test summaries, record test counts, failure metadata, exact destination and attachments; the ledger's structural checks are not themselves proof against malicious/fabricated log contents.

### 13.2 Source, build and runtime provenance

At minimum record: git commit and dirty flag, package/ANGLE/ProjectM submodule pin, source hash manifest, Xcode+Swift+SDK+CMake+XcodeGen version, scheme/configuration/selected destination, code-signing mode, device product type/OS build, timestamp/run ID, status and summarized metrics. Keep huge raw `.xcresult`, app logs and app-container exports in ignored local/CI artifact stores; the versioned report can contain hashes and relative file references without leaking UDIDs. Signable test artifacts are not automatically releasable App Store builds.

### 13.3 Performance methodology

- Use `CADisplayLink` and interval timelines to count refresh misses. Analyze median/p95/p99 frame time, first render, shader compile, CPU/memory and thermal level, not just a hand-reported "60 fps".
- **At least 200 independent measurements** for every percentage threshold. Separate installation first-run onboarding and cache-warm runs. Store per-sample IDs, scenario, input seed, start/end events, stage timings and failure reason.
- D1 is primary reference; D2 high-resolution high-performance iPad; D3 is compatibility and lower-tier budget. Do not set all devices to the same speculative particle/FBO quality if hardware measurements prove otherwise; preserve correct behavior and report adaptive quality.
- Installed size: compare actual thinned archives using `thinning = <thin-for-all-variants>` and each model's "App Thinning Size Report.txt"; do not compare debug simulator sizes to device shipping sizes.
- Check privacy against full app container and allowed UserDefaults keys. Understand that StoreKit may create `SKTransactionUpdatesLastChecked` and Metal caches may create `.pcm` files unrelated to audio; validate provenance before classifying any file, but do not indiscriminately ignore unexpected data.

### 13.4 XCTest and simulator lessons

Use `xcodebuild ... -test-timeouts-enabled YES -default-test-execution-time-allowance 180`, write complete output to a file, avoid `tail` as a live pipe. For a hang inspect the process elapsed time, a simulator screenshot (`xcrun simctl io <udid> screenshot <path>`) and the last "Test Case ... started" log entry. Isolate simulator runtimes between parallel workers, reset microphone permission with `simctl privacy`, and erase a corrupted simulator only after saving required diagnostics. SwiftUI lazy lists create rows only as scrolled into view; test element labels may contain comma-grouped numbers, and toolbars belong to their declaring view. StoreKit host test isolation is critical to avoid Apple Account sign-in popups.

### 13.5 Final reports and status words

`IMPLEMENTED` = actual code/target and functional requirements present. `BUILT` = real compiler successful. `SIMULATOR_VERIFIED` = real simulator tests passed. `DEVICE_VERIFIED` = real signed hardware tests passed with `.xcresult` and mode reports. `READY_FOR_OWNER_RELEASE_REVIEW` = all mandatory checks satisfied but App Store owner actions still pending. `BLOCKED` or `INCOMPLETE` = any required gate not verifiable. Never collapse these into a single green label.

## 14. Autonomous recovery, CI, Git and safety

### 14.1 Git and history

Keep LF via `.gitattributes`. Commit after each verified task/skill with a subject naming feature/IDs and what changed. No co-author trailers or "Generated with Claude Code" in commits. Use user's configured normal Git email, not one invented by the agent. Do not assume blanket approval to `git push` to the new repo because the owner approved it for the separate original ProjectM repo on 2026-11-09. Never reset/clean source trees, rewrite history or remove uncommitted user work. Scope external pushes and PR creations to explicit authorized repo settings; local progress should be fully testable offline.

### 14.2 CI design

A recommended GitHub Actions graph (once GitHub permission is explicitly provided): docs/Spec Kit traceability/compliance on Linux → Linux SwiftPM/CPU model tests → macOS ANGLE/projectM XCFramework cache keyed to Xcode/pins → macOS host unit and simulator UI tests and **generic unsigned device builds** for all apps → preview-Xcode OS/SDK test compilation if the original toolchain still requires it. Use concurrency/cancel-in-progress/timeouts, artifact retention and caching; fetch only submodules needed per job. Do **not** assume free CI minutes on an unrelated or private repo merely because ProjectM was public. The physical-device `device-farm.yml` runs **only on the owner's self-hosted Mac** and only after recorded implementation lock, with D1/D2/D3 attached and paired. CI must not conflate a generic iOS build with a hardware test.

### 14.3 Recovery when Desktop session ends or runs out of context

Do not depend on a conversational summary. The ledger has fixed stage names. A new Desktop Code session reads `CLAUDE.md`, canonical README, `python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py status/next`, and the relevant extracted manual. It then checks Git status, finished evidence and pending Spec Kit tasks. If the prior session stopped mid-gate, repair from the last passing commit and logs, not by marking a gate pass. Optional native scheduled tasks re-enter the same deterministic protocol (Section 16). A persisted `desktop.lock` from a crashed session must be investigated before clearing it. Routine retries are bounded and follow precise failed command logs, with backoff for package/CI service interruptions.

### 14.4 External blockers and false-success prevention

Blocked conditions include unavailable Claude Desktop Auto/permission approval, expired authentication/session quotas, locked devices, missing certificates or Apple team, system picker dialogs, missing proprietary entitlements, unavailable supported SDK, storage exhaustion, unavailable 26.5 D3, or a failed required scientific/third-party license review. Record `blocked` with exact object, observed error, command, timestamp and safe operator action. Continue *independent* work only when it does not violate stage ordering; with strict sequencing a blocked foundation/app gate may necessarily stop the implementation campaign. **Do not silently waive requirements**, mark all future stages green, or present "no human interaction" as authority to bypass Apple and financial trust boundaries.

## 17. Runbook tool extraction and command reference

The single README remains self-contained: Section 19 embeds the complete deterministic Python tool. **Only this small extraction is done from a terminal**, and the terminal is Claude Desktop Code's existing tools or the operator's Mac Terminal, *not* the Claude CLI. The 33 preserved sources and SHA-256 hashes are also inside this README; all individual docs are faithfully extracted to an ignored folder for manageable context.

### 17.1 Extract the deterministic helper without losing source detail

From the new repo root after placing this README and the companion CLAUDE.md:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
text = Path('README.md').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
match = re.search(r'<!-- BEGIN DESKTOP RUNBOOK PYTHON -->\n```python\n(.*?)\n```\n<!-- END DESKTOP RUNBOOK PYTHON -->', text, re.S)
if not match:
    raise SystemExit('Missing embedded Desktop runbook Python block')
target = Path('Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py')
target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
target.write_text(match.group(1) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
print('Extracted:', target)
PY
python3 -m py_compile Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py bootstrap
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py validate
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py status
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py next
```

`bootstrap` creates `.autonomy/context/sources/` and `.autonomy/context/apps/` with byte-exact copies of the **33** archived source documents, and a durable fixed-order state ledger of **263** gates: **10** framework + **175** app phases + **1** implementation lock + **75** physical app/device rows + **1** device reconcile + **1** final suite audit. It refuses corrupt/missing sources, mismatched stage schemas, accidental path traversal or modified extracted files. It never executes a model or silently changes build scripts.

### 17.2 Gate evidence commands

```bash
# Useful read-only commands for every session
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py validate
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py status
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py next

# Explicit test of forbidden premature hardware campaign; expected to fail before lock
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py guard-device

# Run the actual command through the deterministic evidence-capturing helper.
# This is a real host check; replace with the true F00 acceptance commands.
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py run-check \
  --stage F00 --name python-version -- python3 --version

# The helper hashes stdout/stderr and creates an attestation; then seal and record.
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py seal --stage F00
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py record \
  --stage F00 --evidence .autonomy/evidence/F00.json

# For device rows, run real signed XCTest via run-check, verify xcresulttool,
# create an observed device report JSON, then use seal --device-report <actual.json>.

# On a legitimate external blocker, keep the state incomplete and explain it:
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py block \
  --stage F01 --reason 'specific observed external dependency'

# After a real blocker is fixed and a rerun is possible:
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py retry --stage F01

# After the very last gate (all must pass), independently validate archive/evidence:
python3 Tools/python/desktop_runbook.py audit
```

**Evidence schema:** each `record` file has exact `stage`, `status:pass`, at least one `checks` entry with command string, `exit_code:0`, nonempty existing log path and **`run-check` attestation** with matching SHA-256; the helper actually executes each check in a subprocess without a shell, timestamps it and retains failures as historical attempts; per-device `record` additionally requires matching device role/product, observed hardware UDID/OS, `is_simulator:false`, existing `.xcresult`, and independently verified `xcresult_summary:"Passed"`. The helper checks structural integrity; use `scripts/verify_xcresults.py` to truly inspect XCTest outcomes and block false positives. The tool serializes evidence through `next`/`record`, making skipped future phases impossible without tampering.

**Implementation manifest shape, only after real tests:**

```json
{
  "apps": [
    {
      "app_slug": "01-generative-art-studio",
      "status": "pass",
      "scheme": "ACTUAL_SCHEME_FROM_XCODE",
```

The real `apps` array must contain **all 25 distinct slugs**, not just the single schema example, and all artifact paths must exist. Every row needs real success logs plus a working app. A script checking artifact existence alone is insufficient for product completeness; the Desktop agent must independently inspect requirement traces, UI functionality, test results and app implementation.

## 18. Requirement preservation and final acceptance contract

The complete archive below carries **all source content**, not paraphrases: original framework README, AppsBrainstorm, the 25 full original manuals (each ~50–55 KB), original navigation/manifest, **the owner's uploaded ProjectM-iOS agent CLAUDE.md and devices.md**, plus previous CLI supervisor frontmatter for historical record. SHA-256 hashes and lengths are included with each archived block. The deterministic helper validates every archived source before work and extracts individual files for Claude Desktop Code to read. Canonical rules deliberately supersede obsolete CLI-driven actions, but no algorithm/data requirement or owner-reported device fact is discarded.

**In particular, retained lessons include:** the owner's audio-source compatibility FR-031 and FR-032/FR-034 hardware matrix, preprovisioned signing, repo-specific upstream patch process, pinned ANGLE and ProjectM forks, `gclient` disk usage, ELF/Mach-O weak-link checks, CI Xcode-version split, StoreKit 2 test isolation, native accessibility, D3 iOS 26.5 fallback, no audio allocations/locks in realtime callbacks, staged gate/task verification discipline, 200-sample performance methodology, first-frame shader compilation, name/bundle-ID stability, source-specific ProjectM preset counts, no big binaries in Git, and source-based privacy/license review. The archive preserves original historical project task IDs and waiver notes **without** applying those waivers to the new suite.

**The suite is accepted only when:**

- Complete functional VisualCore, Showcase, audited ProjectM bridge and all 25 separate app targets exist, with full guide requirements, source mappings and verified host/SIM/generic-iOS builds;
- all 10 foundation and all 175 implementation phase gates pass real evidence, and the 25-app implementation lock is verified **before** any physical-device test;
- D1 iPhone 15 iOS 27.0.1, D2 iPad Pro M5 iPadOS 27.2 and D3 iPad A16 iPadOS 26.5 each run **all 25 apps**, in exactly that device sequence, with signed physical `.xcresult` and app-mode reports, and D3 is never upgraded;
- the actual product-specific tests, performance and privacy audits pass or have explicit owner-supplied legitimate scope changes, not fabricated agent waivers;
- final output includes a truthful evidence matrix, incomplete blockers where present, size/battery/thermal/compatibility observations and explicit App Store owner-only next steps.

**Do not submit an app to App Store Connect, create purchases or claim general source compatibility merely because development or device tests pass.** Owner actions remain owner actions, and a complete local code suite can still be pending App Review.

The actual pinned local source and toolchain must always override illustrative command strings when they differ.

```python
"""Deterministic, stdlib-only ledger for Claude Code *Desktop* sessions.

"""

CHECKS = STATE_DIR / "checks"
```
