# Audio Odyssey
## iOS application architecture and Spec Kit + Claude Code implementation manual

**Concept #07 of 25** | **Category:** Music and audio | **Proposed app/repository target:** `AudioOdyssey`
**Planning status:** proposed implementation guide; not proof of an existing application or released VisualCore package. **Source:** `AppsBrainstorm.md` catalog item 7; `README.md` VisualCore architecture and Spec Kit strategy.
**Rendering invariant:** reuse the existing ProjectM-proven OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal infrastructure exposed by VisualCore. Never create a duplicate EGL/ANGLE backend or link ProjectM engine internals into this independent app.

---

## 1. Executive summary and source traceability

An audio-reactive journey through procedural tunnels, particle corridors and moving landscapes.

### Original brainstorm concept

> An experience that transforms music into interactive virtual worlds. Users fly through tunnels, landscapes, particle fields, and environments that respond to sound.

**VisualCore capabilities listed in the brainstorm:**
- 3D scene rendering
- Camera systems
- Audio feature integration
- Procedural environments
- Animation and transitions

**Original product opportunity:** An immersive entertainment experience with scene packs and customizable visual journeys.

**Brainstorm initial ranking:** #6 of 25. This is a strategic first-pass judgment, not measured App Store demand or revenue.

**Recommended product hypothesis:** A carefully scoped, offline-capable first release can demonstrate a distinct graphics workload and validate reusable VisualCore APIs. Test this hypothesis with a functioning vertical slice before expanding content or monetization.

## 2. Product contract and scope

### Primary audiences
- Entertainment users wanting immersive visuals
- Creators seeking audio-driven ambient journeys

### End-to-end user journeys
1. **Journey 1:** Select a legally available audio source or demo soundtrack.
2. **Journey 2:** Pick tunnel, landscape or star-corridor journey and start flight.
3. **Journey 3:** Adjust speed/sensitivity, pause scene and switch to low-motion mode.

### Version 0.1 feature contract
1. **Feature 01:** Three distinct procedural environments with controlled camera rail. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
2. **Feature 02:** Audio features mapped to scene geometry/lighting rather than hard cuts. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
3. **Feature 03:** Manual flight speed, camera easing and reduced-motion setting. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
4. **Feature 04:** Microphone/local-app-owned-audio/demo input modes. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
5. **Feature 05:** Save environment + mapping presets. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
6. **Feature 06:** Stable pause/resume and thermal quality downgrade. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.

### Explicit non-goals
- Systemwide capture of third-party protected audio
- VR/headset support in MVP
- Real-time open-world exploration and navigation

### Later-stage ideas, not MVP commitments
- Curated audio journeys and scene packs
- User-controlled path branches
- Compatible spatial audio presentation if justified

## 3. UX blueprint

The first launch should reach a meaningful working graphic or educational interaction without requiring an account. Use SwiftUI for navigation, settings, labels and accessibility; host VisualCore rendering in a verified UIView/UIViewRepresentable integration that owns no duplicate GPU lifecycle.

**Proposed screen inventory** (adapt to the app-specific flows above):
| Screen | Responsibility | Concrete behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Home / gallery | Start without setup | Curated Audio Odyssey example, recent scene and explicit entry point |
| Interactive scene | Primary VisualCore rendering surface | Touch and app-state changes mapped into validated domain commands |
| Inspector | Controls and explanations | Show effective parameter values, reset and valid ranges |
| Library / files | Persistence where relevant | Open, duplicate, save, import/export only via permitted system APIs |
| Settings / help | Quality, accessibility, privacy | Explain input permissions, limitations, credits and renderer fallback |

**Interaction design rules:** screen gestures must have a deterministic domain meaning; rendering can interpolate but cannot silently change persisted state. State-affecting controls should be testable independent of the GPU. All critical feedback must remain legible without bloom, color alone, or animation.

### State transitions to implement
```text
uninitialized → loading-assets → ready → active
                                  ↔ paused / backgrounded
                                  ↘ editing / exporting (if supported)
any GPU state → renderer-lost → recover-resources → ready
any document state → validation-error → recoverable-message
```

Do not upload application/scene state to a server by default. If future features introduce accounts, cloud sync or sharing, write a new privacy and threat-model spec before implementation.

## 4. Architecture: VisualCore consumer, not renderer fork

```text
AudioOdyssey SwiftUI app (navigation, accessibility, preferences)
    ↓ commands / immutable snapshots
AudioOdysseyCore (domain rules, models, persistence schemas, validation)
    ↓ render-state snapshot; never raw SwiftUI bindings
AudioOdysseyRendering (scene adapter, shaders, asset IDs, pass descriptions)
    ↓ public APIs discovered in the real VisualCore checkout
VisualCore runtime, shaders, effects, scenes, inputs, diagnostics
    ↓ shared EGL/context/render host as audited
Existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal implementation
    ↓
iOS device GPU and display
```

**Ownership policy:** The app owns its content, mathematical rules, domain schema, UI and business logic. VisualCore owns generic graphics infrastructure. `Coastrnaut/projectm-ios` remains VisualCore's pinned reference submodule, not an app dependency. Any VisualCore API needed but not present must be proposed upstream with a test and an API contract; do not stub an imaginary package into production.

### Contracts and threading
- A domain coordinator produces immutable render snapshots or bounded commands; presentation does not mutate simulation truth.
- The VisualCore render host controls the EGL context, resource lifetime, presentation and the required render thread/queue; all GL work obeys that ownership.
- Native SwiftUI overlays remain separate from shader drawing where legibility, hit-testing and VoiceOver need native controls.
- On scene resize, background, memory warning or renderer reset, reallocate GPU resources from versioned CPU state rather than persisting raw GL handles.
- Shaders are treated as bundled, versioned assets unless the specific product explicitly supports user-authored GLSL with additional guards.

### Application-specific components
- **`JourneyController.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`ProceduralTunnel.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`LandscapeSegments.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`CameraRail.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`AudioJourneyMapper.swift`**: audio acquisition or signal-feature mapping; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`MotionComfort.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`OdysseyRenderer.swift`**: renderer-facing render orchestration and GPU pass bindings; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.

- Keep all feature specs under `specs/` created by Spec Kit; allow its installed release to determine feature numbering and active feature selection.

## 6. Domain model, algorithms and rendering design

### Versioned domain schemas (proposed types)
| Type | Field contract / required invariants |
|---|---|
| `JourneyState` | `JourneyState(worldID, distance, speed, cameraPose, seed, paused)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `WorldDescriptor` | `WorldDescriptor(meshRule, materialIDs, eventMappings, horizonPolicy)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `AudioReactiveEnvelope` | `AudioReactiveEnvelope(low, mid, high, transient, timestamp)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `ComfortSettings` | `ComfortSettings(maxCameraAcceleration, flashLimit, horizonLock)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |

Use explicit units and coordinate spaces in type names or documentation. Reject NaN/Inf, invalid counts, truncated files, unreasonable allocations and unsupported versions where applicable. Canonical storage should be pure data; expensive buffers can be reconstructed.

### Algorithm and correctness decisions
1. Generate a bounded streaming corridor/terrain mesh around camera and retire segments behind viewer.
2. Use smoothed, clamped audio envelopes to alter color, scale and geometry only within stable bounds.
3. Model camera travel on deterministic path; keep world origin rebasing if distance grows.
4. Separate comfort settings from audiovisual defaults to mitigate simulator sickness.

### App-specific render sequence
1. **Stage 1:** Decode permitted audio and create feature envelope.
2. **Stage 2:** Advance deterministic journey timeline and update nearby procedural segments.
3. **Stage 3:** Render terrain/tunnel, audio-reactive materials and particles.
4. **Stage 4:** Composite fog and post effect; present via VisualCore, with reduced-motion camera fallback.

### Rendering lifecycle and frame budget
- Create resources only after VisualCore signals a valid owning EGL context; release/recreate on context loss and size changes.
- Separate fixed-step simulation, event handling, visual animation time and wall time when the product uses more than one.
- Treat device tier as policy data: resolution scale, effect counts, iterations and object count may change; domain correctness and user state may not.
- Validate framebuffer completeness, shader compile/link results, texture format support and GPU resource handles before presenting a frame.
- Record frame pacing, app-owned CPU time, allocation counts and renderer recovery on a real device before selecting release targets.

### Required capability audit against VisualCore
- **3D scene rendering** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Camera systems** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Audio feature integration** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Procedural environments** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Animation and transitions** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.

> **Domain-specific engineering rule:** Do not claim support for arbitrary background music capture; specify app-owned audio files, demo audio, or consented microphone capture.

## 7. Local environment and reproducible bootstrap

**Prerequisites:** macOS and Xcode for iOS build, signing, Simulator and physical-device tests; Git, Python 3, `uv`, and Claude Code CLI. Windows can prepare specifications and source but cannot validate the iOS rendering path without a macOS builder. Follow current vendor instructions for installation; verify tool versions rather than assuming they exist.

**Terminal on macOS — commands to create this app repository:**
```bash
mkdir AudioOdyssey && cd AudioOdyssey
git init -b main
git --version
python3 --version
uv --version
claude --version
uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git
specify version
specify init --help
specify init --here --integration claude --script py
specify check
git status --short
claude
```

Initialize Spec Kit **once** in a newly created repository. In a non-empty existing repo, commit/backup first and inspect `specify init --help`; `--force` may merge/overwrite managed files and must not be run blindly. Never run Spec Kit initialization inside the VisualCore or ProjectM submodule from an app repo.

**Current Claude Code integration:** Spec Kit creates `.claude/skills/speckit-<command>/SKILL.md`; invoke skills in Claude chat using **hyphens**, e.g. `/speckit-specify`, not the dotted spelling used in some generic documentation. Confirm actual skills with `find .claude/skills -name SKILL.md` and Claude `/help` because installed versions can differ. See official [Claude integration](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html).

**Terminal — verify a local VisualCore checkout without assuming package products:**
```bash
test -d ../VisualCore || { echo "Clone or locate the VisualCore repository beside this app first"; exit 1; }
git -C ../VisualCore status --short
find ../VisualCore -name Package.swift -not -path "*/.build/*" -print
git -C ../VisualCore submodule status
```

If `../VisualCore` does not yet provide a consumer package, create an upstream integration feature and stop at a no-op host skeleton. Do not invent `VisualCoreRenderer` product names or fake ANGLE integration code.

**Claude Code chat, at every task boundary:**
```text
Inspect the active Spec Kit tasks file. Implement only the next smallest dependency-complete task group. Before editing, list intended files, known VisualCore API contracts, test commands, and rollback steps. After editing, run tests and report actual results; do not claim device validation without device logs. Stop for review after this group.
```

Do not ask Claude to run all seven phases unattended. Spec Kit artifacts may expose architecture errors or rights/permission issues that materially change the following work. The Git baseline is reviewed per phase; commit evidence and tests in the application repository, and upstream patches separately.

## 11. Domain, renderer and UI verification matrix

| Layer | App-specific test | Evidence / gate |
|---|---|---|
| Pure domain model | Procedural chunks have watertight joins and bounded generation time | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Pure domain model | Camera speed and acceleration respect comfort limits | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Source switching does not reset EGL context | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Demo waveform produces stable and measurable scene response | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Device or end-to-end | Long-duration travel avoids coordinate precision collapse | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Shared render lifecycle | Repeated renderer create, resize, background, resume, context recovery, release | Device log with no stale EGL/GL handles or persistent GPU memory growth |
| App UI and accessibility | First-session flow, disabled states, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver fallback | UI test + human review on representative iPhone and iPad |
| VisualCore regression | If VisualCore changes, ProjectM remains functional at pinned submodule commit | Existing ProjectM build/smoke log; any difference reviewed |

### Implementation-level fixtures
- Fixture 1: Procedural chunks have watertight joins and bounded generation time.
- Fixture 2: Camera speed and acceleration respect comfort limits.
- Fixture 3: Source switching does not reset EGL context.
- Fixture 4: Demo waveform produces stable and measurable scene response.
- Fixture 5: Long-duration travel avoids coordinate precision collapse.

### Simulator and device separation
- CI/simulator: test domain math, model migration, document round trips, permission-denied paths, basic UI and reproducible app builds.
- Physical iPhone/iPad: validate ANGLE Metal path, shader compilation, context loss, high-refresh/low-refresh behavior, thermals, memory, inputs and real audio/device sensor routes if relevant.
- When tests depend on audio, sensors or input permissions, use synthetic fixtures in CI; do not silently substitute test signals for production sources.
- Store exact Xcode, iOS, device, VisualCore revision, ProjectM submodule revision, preset and test duration with performance reports.

## 12. Profiling plan, budgets and graceful fallback

Before specifying absolute fps, startup or memory targets, measure a baseline on the reference app and at least one representative device. Decide thresholds in a separate acceptance ADR; do not publish invented benchmark numbers.

- Measure segment generation, buffer upload time, p95 frame time and long-session energy use.
- Prioritize smooth camera and feature updates over decorative particle count.
- Screen brightness/flash controls must override presets.

**Telemetry only as local diagnostics by default:** record per-pass timing if genuinely supported, present interval, app-side CPU duration, memory and resource counts, scene configuration, chosen quality tier and build IDs. Make collection opt-in if data ever leaves the device. Never label CPU timings as GPU timings.

**Fallback policy:** keep the app usable when expensive shader passes fail or a device is below target capability: reduce resolution/passes, use a simpler scene, preserve user state, and display a recoverable explanation. When no VisualCore render host exists, ship a native UI placeholder only for internal integration testing—not a misleading App Store release.

## 13. Risks, privacy, science/platform constraints and licenses

### App-specific risk register
1. **Risk 1:** Audio input limitations identical to Music Lab—make source UX transparent. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
2. **Risk 2:** Fast camera motion can cause nausea—provide static/low-motion mode. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
3. **Risk 3:** Streaming geometry may stall render thread—build on worker then safely upload at render boundary. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.

### Cross-cutting obligations
- No private iOS APIs, undocumented system-level audio interception, automatic wallpaper changes or unsupported GPU access; test any requested platform capability against current public documentation.
- Apply least-privilege permission prompts, with useful demo/offline behavior for denied permissions. Document Photos, Files, microphone or audio rights only where that app actually needs them.
- Maintain licenses for ANGLE, VisualCore, ProjectM reference code and all bundled shaders, meshes, textures, fonts, datasets, sound and educational copy. Do not assume upstream assets may be redistributed.
- Use clear scientific/educational caveats wherever simulations or graphics are illustrative. Do not market a toy visualization as an instrument, diagnostic tool or accurate predictive model.
- Validate imported data formats, sizes, paths and schema versions; avoid executing untrusted user code except in the specifically constrained Shader Studio design.

### Content and App Store review checklist
- Document why each permission is necessary and the exact UI path requesting it.
- Provide privacy policy and required app data disclosures based on actual telemetry/storage behavior, not sample text.
- Check all media and code redistribution rights, attribution and trademark rules before the storefront submission.
- Keep claims in marketing and screenshots aligned to implemented working features and measured/attributed facts.

## 14. Xcode project, build, and CI commands

After selecting XcodeGen and writing a real `project.yml` during Phase 0/1, these are executable examples **from this app repo**. Scheme and target names must be confirmed with `xcodebuild -list`; do not assume VisualCore has a particular SPM product name.

```bash
# Use XcodeGen only if project.yml was adopted and reviewed
xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -list -project AudioOdyssey.xcodeproj
xcodebuild -project AudioOdyssey.xcodeproj -scheme AudioOdyssey -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
xcrun simctl list devices available
SIMULATOR_UDID="$(python3 scripts/select_simulator.py)"
test -n "$SIMULATOR_UDID" || { echo "No available simulator"; exit 1; }
xcodebuild -project AudioOdyssey.xcodeproj -scheme AudioOdyssey -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIMULATOR_UDID" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test
python3 scripts/check_repo.py
```

If the repo uses an `.xcworkspace`, SwiftPM-generated project or a different scheme, inspect it and replace these paths; the test commands above do not constitute successful execution here. Build/sign/archive and test native ANGLE/Metal rendering on macOS with Xcode and a physical device.

### Minimal Python repository audit script

Create `scripts/check_repo.py` during the first phase. It should verify presence of essential architecture documents and app-owned shaders, then print the pinned VisualCore version using an actual resolved dependency file. Do not automatically download code or modify an upstream checkout.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import sys
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
required = ["CLAUDE.md", "docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md"]
missing = [name for name in required if not (root / name).is_file()]
for path in missing:
    print(f"MISSING: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
if missing:
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("Repository guidance and integration contract are present")
```

### Portable Python 3 simulator selection helper

Save as `scripts/select_simulator.py`; it reads `xcrun simctl` JSON and chooses a booted iOS simulator first, otherwise an available iPhone simulator. This helper does not create or boot a device; select/boot one manually if no compatible runtime is installed.

```python
import json
import subprocess
import sys
output = subprocess.check_output(
    ["xcrun", "simctl", "list", "devices", "available", "-j"], text=True)
data = json.loads(output)
devices = [device for runtime, group in data.get("devices", {}).items()
           if "iOS" in runtime for device in group
           if device.get("isAvailable", True) and "iPhone" in device.get("name", "")]
device = next((d for d in devices if d.get("state") == "Booted"),
              devices[0] if devices else None)
if device is None:
    sys.exit("No available iPhone simulator. Check Xcode runtimes.")
print(device["udid"])
```

### Minimal XcodeGen target layout

For a fresh repo, an initial `project.yml` can be generated with the following app-only starter; replace deployment target and bundle ID with validated project values, then add local package products only after the VisualCore audit.

```yaml
name: AudioOdyssey
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.example.visualcore
targets:
  AudioOdyssey:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    deploymentTarget: "17.0"   # proposal, verify supported OS
    sources:
      - Apps/AudioOdyssey
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.visualcore.audio-odyssey
```

Install XcodeGen through its official distribution if not already available, verify `xcodegen --version`, and run `xcodegen generate` only after this file and target source exist. Avoid storing unreviewed private package tokens in `project.yml` or CI.

### Suggested macOS GitHub Actions job (create after actual build validation)

```yaml
name: iOS CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Verify Python and repository artifacts
        run: python3 scripts/check_repo.py
      - name: Inspect Xcode and app schemes
        run: xcodebuild -list -project AudioOdyssey.xcodeproj
      - name: Build simulator target
        run: xcodebuild -project AudioOdyssey.xcodeproj -scheme AudioOdyssey -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Pin CI action revisions and the Xcode version according to your organization’s supply-chain rules; add simulator unit tests and any authenticated VisualCore package fetch only after configuration is proven to work. CI on macOS does not substitute for physical GPU regression testing.

## 15. Acceptance criteria and definition of done

A first-release candidate is acceptable only when **all** of the following can be demonstrated:

- [ ] MVP-01: Three distinct procedural environments with controlled camera rail.
- [ ] MVP-02: Audio features mapped to scene geometry/lighting rather than hard cuts.
- [ ] MVP-03: Manual flight speed, camera easing and reduced-motion setting.
- [ ] MVP-04: Microphone/local-app-owned-audio/demo input modes.
- [ ] MVP-05: Save environment + mapping presets.
- [ ] MVP-06: Stable pause/resume and thermal quality downgrade.
- [ ] Standalone app uses public audited VisualCore APIs and shared ANGLE/Metal path, not ProjectM-specific engine internals.
- [ ] Render-state serializations are versioned, validated, and safe after background/resume and renderer reset.
- [ ] Native UI is usable with accessibility features; reduced motion and quality controls behave as stated.
- [ ] Domain and integration test cases in §11 pass; unresolved errors are documented, not marked passing.
- [ ] At least one physical device run with recorded build/OS/device metadata validates actual GPU behavior.
- [ ] No unsupported privacy, scientific or platform capability claims remain in the product UI or listing.
- [ ] Bundled third-party code, shaders, assets, educational facts and sounds have reviewed license/source records.
- [ ] Build from a clean macOS checkout succeeds and the final PR contains exact verification commands and results.
- [ ] Any VisualCore changes have their own upstream PR plus before/after ProjectM reference regression evidence.

## 16. Ordered next actions

1. Create a new `AudioOdyssey` app repo and initialize the Claude/Spec Kit Python variant (commands in §7).
2. Perform read-only VisualCore package/render-host inspection; resolve actual public APIs and upstream gaps.
3. Save the constitution and app-specific design decisions in reviewed repository artifacts.
4. Run Phase 00 through all eight quality gates; complete any upstream VisualCore feature as a separate, reviewed change.
5. Implement Phase 01 journey/camera comfort contract as the smallest testable vertical slice.
6. Continue the remaining phases one by one; compare every release claim against the acceptance matrix.
7. Archive evidence from physical device validation and review the release privacy/license checklist.

# Oscilloscope Studio
## iOS application architecture and Spec Kit + Claude Code implementation manual

**Concept #08 of 25** | **Category:** Music and audio | **Proposed app/repository target:** `OscilloscopeStudio`
**Planning status:** proposed implementation guide; not proof of an existing application or released VisualCore package. **Source:** `AppsBrainstorm.md` catalog item 8; `README.md` VisualCore architecture and Spec Kit strategy.
**Rendering invariant:** reuse the existing ProjectM-proven OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal infrastructure exposed by VisualCore. Never create a duplicate EGL/ANGLE backend or link ProjectM engine internals into this independent app.

---

## 1. Executive summary and source traceability

A responsive and technically legible waveform, Lissajous and spectrum display for permitted audio inputs.

### Original brainstorm concept

> A modern interpretation of classic audio oscilloscopes, Lissajous displays, spectrum analyzers, and waveform visualizations.

**VisualCore capabilities listed in the brainstorm:**
- Line rendering
- Waveform buffers
- Real-time data visualization
- Shader effects
- Multiple visualization modes

**Original product opportunity:** A focused tool for audio enthusiasts, musicians, and technically curious users.

**Recommended product hypothesis:** A carefully scoped, offline-capable first release can demonstrate a distinct graphics workload and validate reusable VisualCore APIs. Test this hypothesis with a functioning vertical slice before expanding content or monetization.

## 2. Product contract and scope

### Primary audiences
- Musicians and audio enthusiasts
- Makers exploring signals
- Educators demonstrating time and frequency domains

### End-to-end user journeys
1. **Journey 1:** Grant mic access or open local audio, select waveform mode.
2. **Journey 2:** Adjust gain, trigger level and timebase.
3. **Journey 3:** Switch to XY Lissajous or spectrogram-like display and freeze a frame.

### Version 0.1 feature contract
1. **Feature 01:** Time-domain waveform with adjustable gain/timebase and selectable trigger. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
2. **Feature 02:** Stereo XY/Lissajous view using available stereo input. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
3. **Feature 03:** FFT spectrum mode with calibrated dB-style annotation where valid. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
4. **Feature 04:** Freeze/capture, cursors and touch zoom. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
5. **Feature 05:** Demo synthetic sine/square/sweep generator for tests. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
6. **Feature 06:** Permission-aware audio input state and safe mic monitoring policy. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.

### Explicit non-goals
- Certified calibrated measurement instrument
- Arbitrary system audio interception
- Medical or lab-grade accuracy claims

### Later-stage ideas, not MVP commitments
- CSV export of analyzed sample windows with consent
- Advanced measurements such as THD with calibration caveats
- Additional local supported audio inputs

## 3. UX blueprint

The first launch should reach a meaningful working graphic or educational interaction without requiring an account. Use SwiftUI for navigation, settings, labels and accessibility; host VisualCore rendering in a verified UIView/UIViewRepresentable integration that owns no duplicate GPU lifecycle.

**Proposed screen inventory** (adapt to the app-specific flows above):
| Screen | Responsibility | Concrete behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Home / gallery | Start without setup | Curated Oscilloscope Studio example, recent scene and explicit entry point |
| Interactive scene | Primary VisualCore rendering surface | Touch and app-state changes mapped into validated domain commands |
| Inspector | Controls and explanations | Show effective parameter values, reset and valid ranges |
| Library / files | Persistence where relevant | Open, duplicate, save, import/export only via permitted system APIs |
| Settings / help | Quality, accessibility, privacy | Explain input permissions, limitations, credits and renderer fallback |

**Interaction design rules:** screen gestures must have a deterministic domain meaning; rendering can interpolate but cannot silently change persisted state. State-affecting controls should be testable independent of the GPU. All critical feedback must remain legible without bloom, color alone, or animation.

### State transitions to implement
```text
uninitialized → loading-assets → ready → active
                                  ↔ paused / backgrounded
                                  ↘ editing / exporting (if supported)
any GPU state → renderer-lost → recover-resources → ready
any document state → validation-error → recoverable-message
```

Do not upload application/scene state to a server by default. If future features introduce accounts, cloud sync or sharing, write a new privacy and threat-model spec before implementation.

## 4. Architecture: VisualCore consumer, not renderer fork

```text
OscilloscopeStudio SwiftUI app (navigation, accessibility, preferences)
    ↓ commands / immutable snapshots
OscilloscopeStudioCore (domain rules, models, persistence schemas, validation)
    ↓ render-state snapshot; never raw SwiftUI bindings
OscilloscopeStudioRendering (scene adapter, shaders, asset IDs, pass descriptions)
    ↓ public APIs discovered in the real VisualCore checkout
VisualCore runtime, shaders, effects, scenes, inputs, diagnostics
    ↓ shared EGL/context/render host as audited
Existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal implementation
    ↓
iOS device GPU and display
```

**Ownership policy:** The app owns its content, mathematical rules, domain schema, UI and business logic. VisualCore owns generic graphics infrastructure. `Coastrnaut/projectm-ios` remains VisualCore's pinned reference submodule, not an app dependency. Any VisualCore API needed but not present must be proposed upstream with a test and an API contract; do not stub an imaginary package into production.

### Contracts and threading
- A domain coordinator produces immutable render snapshots or bounded commands; presentation does not mutate simulation truth.
- The VisualCore render host controls the EGL context, resource lifetime, presentation and the required render thread/queue; all GL work obeys that ownership.
- Native SwiftUI overlays remain separate from shader drawing where legibility, hit-testing and VoiceOver need native controls.
- On scene resize, background, memory warning or renderer reset, reallocate GPU resources from versioned CPU state rather than persisting raw GL handles.
- Shaders are treated as bundled, versioned assets unless the specific product explicitly supports user-authored GLSL with additional guards.

### Application-specific components
- **`AudioInput.swift`**: audio acquisition or signal-feature mapping; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`TriggerEngine.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`TimebaseModel.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`ScopeTraceBuilder.swift`**: audio acquisition or signal-feature mapping; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`SpectrumAnalyzer.swift`**: audio acquisition or signal-feature mapping; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`ScopeRenderer.swift`**: renderer-facing render orchestration and GPU pass bindings; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.

## 6. Domain model, algorithms and rendering design

### Versioned domain schemas (proposed types)
| Type | Field contract / required invariants |
|---|---|
| `SignalWindow` | `SignalWindow(sampleRate, channelCount, sampleCount, timestamp)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `ScopeSettings` | `ScopeSettings(mode, triggerLevel, triggerSlope, timebase, gain, channelMode)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `ScopeTrace` | `ScopeTrace(points, channelLabels, min, max)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `SpectrumSettings` | `SpectrumSettings(fftSize, windowFunction, referenceLevel)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |

Use explicit units and coordinate spaces in type names or documentation. Reject NaN/Inf, invalid counts, truncated files, unreasonable allocations and unsupported versions where applicable. Canonical storage should be pure data; expensive buffers can be reconstructed.

### Algorithm and correctness decisions
1. Use ring-buffer snapshots with correct sample-rate accounting and trigger crossing detection.
2. Implement windowed FFT with bin-frequency mapping and correct log-domain zero guards.
3. Resample decimated display points to avoid drawing more geometry than pixels.
4. Separate real measured levels from relative/un-calibrated display values; annotate source limitations.

### App-specific render sequence
1. **Stage 1:** Capture approved PCM samples.
2. **Stage 2:** Prepare triggered time window or spectral frame.
3. **Stage 3:** Convert samples into bounded line/strip vertex buffers.
4. **Stage 4:** Render grid, trace and labels in separate passes; handle freeze without stopping input unnecessarily.

### Rendering lifecycle and frame budget
- Create resources only after VisualCore signals a valid owning EGL context; release/recreate on context loss and size changes.
- Separate fixed-step simulation, event handling, visual animation time and wall time when the product uses more than one.
- Treat device tier as policy data: resolution scale, effect counts, iterations and object count may change; domain correctness and user state may not.
- Validate framebuffer completeness, shader compile/link results, texture format support and GPU resource handles before presenting a frame.
- Record frame pacing, app-owned CPU time, allocation counts and renderer recovery on a real device before selecting release targets.

### Required capability audit against VisualCore
- **Line rendering** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Waveform buffers** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Real-time data visualization** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Shader effects** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Multiple visualization modes** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.

> **Domain-specific engineering rule:** Do not present apparent dB or voltage values as calibrated without a known input reference. Demo waveform is essential for simulator and CI tests.

## 7. Local environment and reproducible bootstrap

**Prerequisites:** macOS and Xcode for iOS build, signing, Simulator and physical-device tests; Git, Python 3, `uv`, and Claude Code CLI. Windows can prepare specifications and source but cannot validate the iOS rendering path without a macOS builder. Follow current vendor instructions for installation; verify tool versions rather than assuming they exist.

**Terminal on macOS — commands to create this app repository:**
```bash
mkdir OscilloscopeStudio && cd OscilloscopeStudio
git init -b main
git --version
python3 --version
uv --version
claude --version
uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git
specify version
specify init --help
specify init --here --integration claude --script py
specify check
git status --short
claude
```

Initialize Spec Kit **once** in a newly created repository. In a non-empty existing repo, commit/backup first and inspect `specify init --help`; `--force` may merge/overwrite managed files and must not be run blindly. Never run Spec Kit initialization inside the VisualCore or ProjectM submodule from an app repo.

**Current Claude Code integration:** Spec Kit creates `.claude/skills/speckit-<command>/SKILL.md`; invoke skills in Claude chat using **hyphens**, e.g. `/speckit-specify`, not the dotted spelling used in some generic documentation. Confirm actual skills with `find .claude/skills -name SKILL.md` and Claude `/help` because installed versions can differ. See official [Claude integration](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html).

**Terminal — verify a local VisualCore checkout without assuming package products:**
```bash
test -d ../VisualCore || { echo "Clone or locate the VisualCore repository beside this app first"; exit 1; }
git -C ../VisualCore status --short
find ../VisualCore -name Package.swift -not -path "*/.build/*" -print
git -C ../VisualCore submodule status
```

If `../VisualCore` does not yet provide a consumer package, create an upstream integration feature and stop at a no-op host skeleton. Do not invent `VisualCoreRenderer` product names or fake ANGLE integration code.

## 9. Implementation phases with **actual Spec Kit / Claude Code commands**

Run the following blocks **inside Claude Code chat**, **not** your shell. Each phase should produce its own `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, tests and reviewable PR; use the actual active feature convention generated by your Spec Kit version. Execute the next phase only after the preceding acceptance checks pass. Slash commands below follow the current Claude skill installation; if your installed integration differs, inspect its generated `.claude/skills/`.

### Phase 00 — Foundation and VisualCore boundary audit

**Deliverable:** Produce read-only repository inventory; map VisualCore package products, EGL host, render thread, shader/resource APIs, Xcode build steps, actual source ownership and baseline ProjectM regression tests. Record open architectural gaps. Do not modify VisualCore or ProjectM.

**Review / acceptance gates:**
- An evidence-backed integration matrix references real files, symbols and package products
- The app can compile an empty SwiftUI shell before custom graphics integration

## 10. Bounded Claude execution and Git workflow

**Terminal:**
```bash
git status --short
git diff --check
git diff --stat
git add -A
git commit -m "feat: complete reviewed implementation phase"
git log -3 --oneline
```

**Claude Code chat, at every task boundary:**
```text
Inspect the active Spec Kit tasks file. Implement only the next smallest dependency-complete task group. Before editing, list intended files, known VisualCore API contracts, test commands, and rollback steps. After editing, run tests and report actual results; do not claim device validation without device logs. Stop for review after this group.
```

Do not ask Claude to run all seven phases unattended. Spec Kit artifacts may expose architecture errors or rights/permission issues that materially change the following work. The Git baseline is reviewed per phase; commit evidence and tests in the application repository, and upstream patches separately.

## 11. Domain, renderer and UI verification matrix

| Layer | App-specific test | Evidence / gate |
|---|---|---|
| Pure domain model | Known sine frequency maps to expected display periods and spectrum bin | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Pure domain model | Trigger detection handles flatline and missing crossing | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Stereo XY view is disabled or clearly marked for mono sources | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | No clipping or false precision in displayed units | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Device or end-to-end | Freeze captures consistent sample metadata | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Shared render lifecycle | Repeated renderer create, resize, background, resume, context recovery, release | Device log with no stale EGL/GL handles or persistent GPU memory growth |
| App UI and accessibility | First-session flow, disabled states, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver fallback | UI test + human review on representative iPhone and iPad |
| VisualCore regression | If VisualCore changes, ProjectM remains functional at pinned submodule commit | Existing ProjectM build/smoke log; any difference reviewed |

### Implementation-level fixtures
- Fixture 1: Known sine frequency maps to expected display periods and spectrum bin.
- Fixture 2: Trigger detection handles flatline and missing crossing.
- Fixture 3: Stereo XY view is disabled or clearly marked for mono sources.
- Fixture 4: No clipping or false precision in displayed units.
- Fixture 5: Freeze captures consistent sample metadata.

### Simulator and device separation
- CI/simulator: test domain math, model migration, document round trips, permission-denied paths, basic UI and reproducible app builds.
- Physical iPhone/iPad: validate ANGLE Metal path, shader compilation, context loss, high-refresh/low-refresh behavior, thermals, memory, inputs and real audio/device sensor routes if relevant.
- When tests depend on audio, sensors or input permissions, use synthetic fixtures in CI; do not silently substitute test signals for production sources.
- Store exact Xcode, iOS, device, VisualCore revision, ProjectM submodule revision, preset and test duration with performance reports.

## 12. Profiling plan, budgets and graceful fallback

Before specifying absolute fps, startup or memory targets, measure a baseline on the reference app and at least one representative device. Decide thresholds in a separate acceptance ADR; do not publish invented benchmark numbers.

- Separate acquisition sample rate from rendered frame rate.
- Use downsampling preserving min/max envelopes for high-frequency traces.
- Monitor ring-buffer overrun, input latency and frame-time jitter.

**Telemetry only as local diagnostics by default:** record per-pass timing if genuinely supported, present interval, app-side CPU duration, memory and resource counts, scene configuration, chosen quality tier and build IDs. Make collection opt-in if data ever leaves the device. Never label CPU timings as GPU timings.

**Fallback policy:** keep the app usable when expensive shader passes fail or a device is below target capability: reduce resolution/passes, use a simpler scene, preserve user state, and display a recoverable explanation. When no VisualCore render host exists, ship a native UI placeholder only for internal integration testing—not a misleading App Store release.

## 13. Risks, privacy, science/platform constraints and licenses

### App-specific risk register
1. **Risk 1:** Mic channels may be mono and routes change—negotiate actual format at runtime. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
2. **Risk 2:** Accurate line rendering can be expensive—decimate while preserving peaks. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
3. **Risk 3:** Terminology might imply calibrated hardware—provide explicit caveat. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.

### Cross-cutting obligations
- No private iOS APIs, undocumented system-level audio interception, automatic wallpaper changes or unsupported GPU access; test any requested platform capability against current public documentation.
- Apply least-privilege permission prompts, with useful demo/offline behavior for denied permissions. Document Photos, Files, microphone or audio rights only where that app actually needs them.
- Maintain licenses for ANGLE, VisualCore, ProjectM reference code and all bundled shaders, meshes, textures, fonts, datasets, sound and educational copy. Do not assume upstream assets may be redistributed.
- Use clear scientific/educational caveats wherever simulations or graphics are illustrative. Do not market a toy visualization as an instrument, diagnostic tool or accurate predictive model.
- Validate imported data formats, sizes, paths and schema versions; avoid executing untrusted user code except in the specifically constrained Shader Studio design.

### Content and App Store review checklist
- Document why each permission is necessary and the exact UI path requesting it.
- Provide privacy policy and required app data disclosures based on actual telemetry/storage behavior, not sample text.
- Check all media and code redistribution rights, attribution and trademark rules before the storefront submission.
- Keep claims in marketing and screenshots aligned to implemented working features and measured/attributed facts.

## 14. Xcode project, build, and CI commands

After selecting XcodeGen and writing a real `project.yml` during Phase 0/1, these are executable examples **from this app repo**. Scheme and target names must be confirmed with `xcodebuild -list`; do not assume VisualCore has a particular SPM product name.

```bash
# Use XcodeGen only if project.yml was adopted and reviewed
xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -list -project OscilloscopeStudio.xcodeproj
xcodebuild -project OscilloscopeStudio.xcodeproj -scheme OscilloscopeStudio -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
xcrun simctl list devices available
SIMULATOR_UDID="$(python3 scripts/select_simulator.py)"
test -n "$SIMULATOR_UDID" || { echo "No available simulator"; exit 1; }
xcodebuild -project OscilloscopeStudio.xcodeproj -scheme OscilloscopeStudio -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIMULATOR_UDID" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test
python3 scripts/check_repo.py
```

If the repo uses an `.xcworkspace`, SwiftPM-generated project or a different scheme, inspect it and replace these paths; the test commands above do not constitute successful execution here. Build/sign/archive and test native ANGLE/Metal rendering on macOS with Xcode and a physical device.

### Minimal Python repository audit script

Create `scripts/check_repo.py` during the first phase. It should verify presence of essential architecture documents and app-owned shaders, then print the pinned VisualCore version using an actual resolved dependency file. Do not automatically download code or modify an upstream checkout.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import sys
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
required = ["CLAUDE.md", "docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md"]
missing = [name for name in required if not (root / name).is_file()]
for path in missing:
    print(f"MISSING: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
if missing:
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("Repository guidance and integration contract are present")
```

### Portable Python 3 simulator selection helper

Save as `scripts/select_simulator.py`; it reads `xcrun simctl` JSON and chooses a booted iOS simulator first, otherwise an available iPhone simulator. This helper does not create or boot a device; select/boot one manually if no compatible runtime is installed.

```python
import json
import subprocess
import sys
output = subprocess.check_output(
    ["xcrun", "simctl", "list", "devices", "available", "-j"], text=True)
data = json.loads(output)
devices = [device for runtime, group in data.get("devices", {}).items()
           if "iOS" in runtime for device in group
           if device.get("isAvailable", True) and "iPhone" in device.get("name", "")]
device = next((d for d in devices if d.get("state") == "Booted"),
              devices[0] if devices else None)
if device is None:
    sys.exit("No available iPhone simulator. Check Xcode runtimes.")
print(device["udid"])
```

### Minimal XcodeGen target layout

For a fresh repo, an initial `project.yml` can be generated with the following app-only starter; replace deployment target and bundle ID with validated project values, then add local package products only after the VisualCore audit.

```yaml
name: OscilloscopeStudio
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.example.visualcore
targets:
  OscilloscopeStudio:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    deploymentTarget: "17.0"   # proposal, verify supported OS
    sources:
      - Apps/OscilloscopeStudio
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.visualcore.oscilloscope-studio
```

Install XcodeGen through its official distribution if not already available, verify `xcodegen --version`, and run `xcodegen generate` only after this file and target source exist. Avoid storing unreviewed private package tokens in `project.yml` or CI.

### Suggested macOS GitHub Actions job (create after actual build validation)

```yaml
name: iOS CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Verify Python and repository artifacts
        run: python3 scripts/check_repo.py
      - name: Inspect Xcode and app schemes
        run: xcodebuild -list -project OscilloscopeStudio.xcodeproj
      - name: Build simulator target
        run: xcodebuild -project OscilloscopeStudio.xcodeproj -scheme OscilloscopeStudio -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Pin CI action revisions and the Xcode version according to your organization’s supply-chain rules; add simulator unit tests and any authenticated VisualCore package fetch only after configuration is proven to work. CI on macOS does not substitute for physical GPU regression testing.

## 15. Acceptance criteria and definition of done

A first-release candidate is acceptable only when **all** of the following can be demonstrated:

- [ ] MVP-01: Time-domain waveform with adjustable gain/timebase and selectable trigger.
- [ ] MVP-02: Stereo XY/Lissajous view using available stereo input.
- [ ] MVP-03: FFT spectrum mode with calibrated dB-style annotation where valid.
- [ ] MVP-04: Freeze/capture, cursors and touch zoom.
- [ ] MVP-05: Demo synthetic sine/square/sweep generator for tests.
- [ ] MVP-06: Permission-aware audio input state and safe mic monitoring policy.
- [ ] Standalone app uses public audited VisualCore APIs and shared ANGLE/Metal path, not ProjectM-specific engine internals.
- [ ] Render-state serializations are versioned, validated, and safe after background/resume and renderer reset.
- [ ] Native UI is usable with accessibility features; reduced motion and quality controls behave as stated.
- [ ] Domain and integration test cases in §11 pass; unresolved errors are documented, not marked passing.
- [ ] At least one physical device run with recorded build/OS/device metadata validates actual GPU behavior.
- [ ] No unsupported privacy, scientific or platform capability claims remain in the product UI or listing.
- [ ] Bundled third-party code, shaders, assets, educational facts and sounds have reviewed license/source records.
- [ ] Build from a clean macOS checkout succeeds and the final PR contains exact verification commands and results.
- [ ] Any VisualCore changes have their own upstream PR plus before/after ProjectM reference regression evidence.

## 16. Ordered next actions

1. Create a new `OscilloscopeStudio` app repo and initialize the Claude/Spec Kit Python variant (commands in §7).
2. Perform read-only VisualCore package/render-host inspection; resolve actual public APIs and upstream gaps.
3. Save the constitution and app-specific design decisions in reviewed repository artifacts.
4. Run Phase 00 through all eight quality gates; complete any upstream VisualCore feature as a separate, reviewed change.
5. Implement Phase 01 audio fixture and acquisition interface as the smallest testable vertical slice.
6. Continue the remaining phases one by one; compare every release claim against the acceptance matrix.
7. Archive evidence from physical device validation and review the release privacy/license checklist.

# Digital Aquarium
## iOS application architecture and Spec Kit + Claude Code implementation manual

**Concept #09 of 25** | **Category:** Music and audio | **Proposed app/repository target:** `DigitalAquarium`
**Planning status:** proposed implementation guide; not proof of an existing application or released VisualCore package. **Source:** `AppsBrainstorm.md` catalog item 9; `README.md` VisualCore architecture and Spec Kit strategy.
**Rendering invariant:** reuse the existing ProjectM-proven OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal infrastructure exposed by VisualCore. Never create a duplicate EGL/ANGLE backend or link ProjectM engine internals into this independent app.

---

## 1. Executive summary and source traceability

A calming, customizable underwater habitat with autonomous fish, plants, bubbles and soft lighting.

### Original brainstorm concept

> A relaxing interactive environment with procedural fish, aquatic plants, lighting, bubbles, underwater effects, and optional audio-reactive behavior.

**VisualCore capabilities listed in the brainstorm:**
- Sprite and object systems
- Animation
- Procedural environments
- Particles
- Scene management
- Touch interaction

**Original product opportunity:** A polished ambient experience with customizable aquariums, creatures, environments, and behaviors.

**Brainstorm initial ranking:** #3 of 25. This is a strategic first-pass judgment, not measured App Store demand or revenue.

**Recommended product hypothesis:** A carefully scoped, offline-capable first release can demonstrate a distinct graphics workload and validate reusable VisualCore APIs. Test this hypothesis with a functioning vertical slice before expanding content or monetization.

## 2. Product contract and scope

### Primary audiences
- Families looking for a safe ambient experience
- Casual collectors who customize habitats
- Users wanting a passive beautiful display

### End-to-end user journeys
1. **Journey 1:** Choose starter habitat and watch animated fish.
2. **Journey 2:** Tap to feed or gently attract fish.
3. **Journey 3:** Place a plant, adjust lighting and save the aquarium.

### Version 0.1 feature contract
1. **Feature 01:** One complete aquarium with two fish species and plants. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
2. **Feature 02:** Bounded 2D/2.5D school behaviors and swim animation. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
3. **Feature 03:** Tap-to-feed and decoration placement gestures. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
4. **Feature 04:** Bubbles, caustics, depth layers and environmental particles. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
5. **Feature 05:** Persistent habitat configurations and safe restore. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
6. **Feature 06:** Low-motion/low-power ambient mode with auto dimming. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.

### Explicit non-goals
- Realistic ecosystem or animal care simulator
- Purchasable creature economy in MVP
- Online multi-user aquarium

### Later-stage ideas, not MVP commitments
- Audio-reactive lighting with legally permitted sources
- Seasonal habitat packs
- More complex social fish behavior

## 3. UX blueprint

The first launch should reach a meaningful working graphic or educational interaction without requiring an account. Use SwiftUI for navigation, settings, labels and accessibility; host VisualCore rendering in a verified UIView/UIViewRepresentable integration that owns no duplicate GPU lifecycle.

**Proposed screen inventory** (adapt to the app-specific flows above):
| Screen | Responsibility | Concrete behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Home / gallery | Start without setup | Curated Digital Aquarium example, recent scene and explicit entry point |
| Interactive scene | Primary VisualCore rendering surface | Touch and app-state changes mapped into validated domain commands |
| Inspector | Controls and explanations | Show effective parameter values, reset and valid ranges |
| Library / files | Persistence where relevant | Open, duplicate, save, import/export only via permitted system APIs |
| Settings / help | Quality, accessibility, privacy | Explain input permissions, limitations, credits and renderer fallback |

**Interaction design rules:** screen gestures must have a deterministic domain meaning; rendering can interpolate but cannot silently change persisted state. State-affecting controls should be testable independent of the GPU. All critical feedback must remain legible without bloom, color alone, or animation.

### State transitions to implement
```text
uninitialized → loading-assets → ready → active
                                  ↔ paused / backgrounded
                                  ↘ editing / exporting (if supported)
any GPU state → renderer-lost → recover-resources → ready
any document state → validation-error → recoverable-message
```

Do not upload application/scene state to a server by default. If future features introduce accounts, cloud sync or sharing, write a new privacy and threat-model spec before implementation.

## 4. Architecture: VisualCore consumer, not renderer fork

```text
DigitalAquarium SwiftUI app (navigation, accessibility, preferences)
    ↓ commands / immutable snapshots
DigitalAquariumCore (domain rules, models, persistence schemas, validation)
    ↓ render-state snapshot; never raw SwiftUI bindings
DigitalAquariumRendering (scene adapter, shaders, asset IDs, pass descriptions)
    ↓ public APIs discovered in the real VisualCore checkout
VisualCore runtime, shaders, effects, scenes, inputs, diagnostics
    ↓ shared EGL/context/render host as audited
Existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal implementation
    ↓
iOS device GPU and display
```

**Ownership policy:** The app owns its content, mathematical rules, domain schema, UI and business logic. VisualCore owns generic graphics infrastructure. `Coastrnaut/projectm-ios` remains VisualCore's pinned reference submodule, not an app dependency. Any VisualCore API needed but not present must be proposed upstream with a test and an API contract; do not stub an imaginary package into production.

### Contracts and threading
- A domain coordinator produces immutable render snapshots or bounded commands; presentation does not mutate simulation truth.
- The VisualCore render host controls the EGL context, resource lifetime, presentation and the required render thread/queue; all GL work obeys that ownership.
- Native SwiftUI overlays remain separate from shader drawing where legibility, hit-testing and VoiceOver need native controls.
- On scene resize, background, memory warning or renderer reset, reallocate GPU resources from versioned CPU state rather than persisting raw GL handles.
- Shaders are treated as bundled, versioned assets unless the specific product explicitly supports user-authored GLSL with additional guards.

### Application-specific components
- **`AquariumDocument.swift`**: data storage, schema validation, assets or export; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`FishBehaviorSystem.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`SpeciesCatalog.swift`**: data storage, schema validation, assets or export; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`HabitatEditor.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`AquariumScene.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`AquariumRenderer.swift`**: renderer-facing render orchestration and GPU pass bindings; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.

### File creation policy
- Generate the minimum Xcode app target and package source files required by the first vertical slice. Do not pre-create dozens of empty Swift files.
- Keep application shader files local when specific to this product; move a shader helper to VisualCore only after an independent use-case and regression tests justify reuse.
- Store data fixtures in JSON/CSV where appropriate, with explicit schema and license metadata; do not serialize GPU buffer addresses or EGL objects.
- Keep all feature specs under `specs/` created by Spec Kit; allow its installed release to determine feature numbering and active feature selection.

## 6. Domain model, algorithms and rendering design

### Versioned domain schemas (proposed types)
| Type | Field contract / required invariants |
|---|---|
| `AquariumDocument` | `AquariumDocument(id, version, waterColor, plants, fish, decor, lighting)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `FishAgent` | `FishAgent(species, position, velocity, heading, behavior, animationPhase)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `AquariumHabitat` | `AquariumHabitat(bounds, obstacles, currentField, depthLayers)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `FeedingEvent` | `FeedingEvent(position, timestamp, attractionRadius)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |

Use explicit units and coordinate spaces in type names or documentation. Reject NaN/Inf, invalid counts, truncated files, unreasonable allocations and unsupported versions where applicable. Canonical storage should be pure data; expensive buffers can be reconstructed.

### Algorithm and correctness decisions
1. Use bounded steering forces for separation, alignment and cohesion with a small neighbor search.
2. Fish orientation and fin animation follow velocity with smoothed heading.
3. Keep habitat edits deterministic and separately serialized from transient fish motion.
4. Reuse sprites/materials by species, batch draw calls and soft-mask water effects.

### App-specific render sequence
1. **Stage 1:** Load habitat assets and document state.
2. **Stage 2:** Update fish agents and plant animations in fixed steps.
3. **Stage 3:** Render depth-ordered background, fauna, vegetation, bubbles and caustics.
4. **Stage 4:** Composite subtle color grade and present with quality scaling.

### Rendering lifecycle and frame budget
- Create resources only after VisualCore signals a valid owning EGL context; release/recreate on context loss and size changes.
- Separate fixed-step simulation, event handling, visual animation time and wall time when the product uses more than one.
- Treat device tier as policy data: resolution scale, effect counts, iterations and object count may change; domain correctness and user state may not.
- Validate framebuffer completeness, shader compile/link results, texture format support and GPU resource handles before presenting a frame.
- Record frame pacing, app-owned CPU time, allocation counts and renderer recovery on a real device before selecting release targets.

### Required capability audit against VisualCore
- **Sprite and object systems** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Animation** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Procedural environments** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Particles** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Scene management** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Touch interaction** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.

> **Domain-specific engineering rule:** Use Digital Aquarium to validate VisualCore scenes, assets, particles and frame lifecycle as a second independent consumer after VisualCore Studio.

## 7. Local environment and reproducible bootstrap

**Prerequisites:** macOS and Xcode for iOS build, signing, Simulator and physical-device tests; Git, Python 3, `uv`, and Claude Code CLI. Windows can prepare specifications and source but cannot validate the iOS rendering path without a macOS builder. Follow current vendor instructions for installation; verify tool versions rather than assuming they exist.

**Terminal on macOS — commands to create this app repository:**
```bash
mkdir DigitalAquarium && cd DigitalAquarium
git init -b main
git --version
python3 --version
uv --version
claude --version
uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git
specify version
specify init --help
specify init --here --integration claude --script py
specify check
git status --short
claude
```

Initialize Spec Kit **once** in a newly created repository. In a non-empty existing repo, commit/backup first and inspect `specify init --help`; `--force` may merge/overwrite managed files and must not be run blindly. Never run Spec Kit initialization inside the VisualCore or ProjectM submodule from an app repo.

**Current Claude Code integration:** Spec Kit creates `.claude/skills/speckit-<command>/SKILL.md`; invoke skills in Claude chat using **hyphens**, e.g. `/speckit-specify`, not the dotted spelling used in some generic documentation. Confirm actual skills with `find .claude/skills -name SKILL.md` and Claude `/help` because installed versions can differ. See official [Claude integration](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html).

**Terminal — verify a local VisualCore checkout without assuming package products:**
```bash
test -d ../VisualCore || { echo "Clone or locate the VisualCore repository beside this app first"; exit 1; }
git -C ../VisualCore status --short
find ../VisualCore -name Package.swift -not -path "*/.build/*" -print
git -C ../VisualCore submodule status
```

If `../VisualCore` does not yet provide a consumer package, create an upstream integration feature and stop at a no-op host skeleton. Do not invent `VisualCoreRenderer` product names or fake ANGLE integration code.

**Deliverable:** Produce read-only repository inventory; map VisualCore package products, EGL host, render thread, shader/resource APIs, Xcode build steps, actual source ownership and baseline ProjectM regression tests. Record open architectural gaps. Do not modify VisualCore or ProjectM.
