## 10. Bounded Claude execution and Git workflow

**Terminal:**
```bash
git status --short
git diff --check
git diff --stat
git add -A
git commit -m "feat: complete reviewed implementation phase"
git log -3 --oneline
```

**Claude Code chat, at every task boundary:**
```text
Inspect the active Spec Kit tasks file. Implement only the next smallest dependency-complete task group. Before editing, list intended files, known VisualCore API contracts, test commands, and rollback steps. After editing, run tests and report actual results; do not claim device validation without device logs. Stop for review after this group.
```

Do not ask Claude to run all seven phases unattended. Spec Kit artifacts may expose architecture errors or rights/permission issues that materially change the following work. The Git baseline is reviewed per phase; commit evidence and tests in the application repository, and upstream patches separately.

## 11. Domain, renderer and UI verification matrix

| Layer | App-specific test | Evidence / gate |
|---|---|---|
| Pure domain model | Fish avoid leaving designated swim bounds | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Pure domain model | Save/load preserves species, decor transforms and lighting | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Background/resume does not fast-forward fish simulation | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Asset catalog rejects missing/unsupported resources gracefully | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Device or end-to-end | Long-running scene keeps fish count, particle count and GPU memory bounded | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Shared render lifecycle | Repeated renderer create, resize, background, resume, context recovery, release | Device log with no stale EGL/GL handles or persistent GPU memory growth |
| App UI and accessibility | First-session flow, disabled states, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver fallback | UI test + human review on representative iPhone and iPad |
| VisualCore regression | If VisualCore changes, ProjectM remains functional at pinned submodule commit | Existing ProjectM build/smoke log; any difference reviewed |

### Implementation-level fixtures
- Fixture 1: Fish avoid leaving designated swim bounds.
- Fixture 2: Save/load preserves species, decor transforms and lighting.
- Fixture 3: Background/resume does not fast-forward fish simulation.
- Fixture 4: Asset catalog rejects missing/unsupported resources gracefully.
- Fixture 5: Long-running scene keeps fish count, particle count and GPU memory bounded.

### Simulator and device separation
- CI/simulator: test domain math, model migration, document round trips, permission-denied paths, basic UI and reproducible app builds.
- Physical iPhone/iPad: validate ANGLE Metal path, shader compilation, context loss, high-refresh/low-refresh behavior, thermals, memory, inputs and real audio/device sensor routes if relevant.
- When tests depend on audio, sensors or input permissions, use synthetic fixtures in CI; do not silently substitute test signals for production sources.
- Store exact Xcode, iOS, device, VisualCore revision, ProjectM submodule revision, preset and test duration with performance reports.

## 12. Profiling plan, budgets and graceful fallback

Before specifying absolute fps, startup or memory targets, measure a baseline on the reference app and at least one representative device. Decide thresholds in a separate acceptance ADR; do not publish invented benchmark numbers.

- Target long-session thermal stability, not merely peak FPS.
- Allow user-defined quality and low-power sleep behavior.
- Measure batching efficiency, persistent memory and frame pacing after 15-minute ambient sessions.

**Telemetry only as local diagnostics by default:** record per-pass timing if genuinely supported, present interval, app-side CPU duration, memory and resource counts, scene configuration, chosen quality tier and build IDs. Make collection opt-in if data ever leaves the device. Never label CPU timings as GPU timings.

**Fallback policy:** keep the app usable when expensive shader passes fail or a device is below target capability: reduce resolution/passes, use a simpler scene, preserve user state, and display a recoverable explanation. When no VisualCore render host exists, ship a native UI placeholder only for internal integration testing—not a misleading App Store release.

## 13. Risks, privacy, science/platform constraints and licenses

### App-specific risk register
1. **Risk 1:** Asset provenance and third-party artwork licensing are central—ship only owned/licensed media. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
2. **Risk 2:** Too many independent sprites cause draw overhead—batch or atlas. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
3. **Risk 3:** AI-generated motion can look erratic—use capped forces and animation smoothing. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.

### Cross-cutting obligations
- No private iOS APIs, undocumented system-level audio interception, automatic wallpaper changes or unsupported GPU access; test any requested platform capability against current public documentation.
- Apply least-privilege permission prompts, with useful demo/offline behavior for denied permissions. Document Photos, Files, microphone or audio rights only where that app actually needs them.
- Maintain licenses for ANGLE, VisualCore, ProjectM reference code and all bundled shaders, meshes, textures, fonts, datasets, sound and educational copy. Do not assume upstream assets may be redistributed.
- Use clear scientific/educational caveats wherever simulations or graphics are illustrative. Do not market a toy visualization as an instrument, diagnostic tool or accurate predictive model.
- Validate imported data formats, sizes, paths and schema versions; avoid executing untrusted user code except in the specifically constrained Shader Studio design.

### Content and App Store review checklist
- Document why each permission is necessary and the exact UI path requesting it.
- Provide privacy policy and required app data disclosures based on actual telemetry/storage behavior, not sample text.
- Check all media and code redistribution rights, attribution and trademark rules before the storefront submission.
- Keep claims in marketing and screenshots aligned to implemented working features and measured/attributed facts.

## 14. Xcode project, build, and CI commands

After selecting XcodeGen and writing a real `project.yml` during Phase 0/1, these are executable examples **from this app repo**. Scheme and target names must be confirmed with `xcodebuild -list`; do not assume VisualCore has a particular SPM product name.

```bash
# Use XcodeGen only if project.yml was adopted and reviewed
xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -list -project DigitalAquarium.xcodeproj
xcodebuild -project DigitalAquarium.xcodeproj -scheme DigitalAquarium -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
xcrun simctl list devices available
SIMULATOR_UDID="$(python3 scripts/select_simulator.py)"
test -n "$SIMULATOR_UDID" || { echo "No available simulator"; exit 1; }
xcodebuild -project DigitalAquarium.xcodeproj -scheme DigitalAquarium -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIMULATOR_UDID" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test
python3 scripts/check_repo.py
```

If the repo uses an `.xcworkspace`, SwiftPM-generated project or a different scheme, inspect it and replace these paths; the test commands above do not constitute successful execution here. Build/sign/archive and test native ANGLE/Metal rendering on macOS with Xcode and a physical device.

### Minimal Python repository audit script

Create `scripts/check_repo.py` during the first phase. It should verify presence of essential architecture documents and app-owned shaders, then print the pinned VisualCore version using an actual resolved dependency file. Do not automatically download code or modify an upstream checkout.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import sys
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
required = ["CLAUDE.md", "docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md"]
missing = [name for name in required if not (root / name).is_file()]
for path in missing:
    print(f"MISSING: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
if missing:
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("Repository guidance and integration contract are present")
```

### Portable Python 3 simulator selection helper

Save as `scripts/select_simulator.py`; it reads `xcrun simctl` JSON and chooses a booted iOS simulator first, otherwise an available iPhone simulator. This helper does not create or boot a device; select/boot one manually if no compatible runtime is installed.

```python
import json
import subprocess
import sys
output = subprocess.check_output(
    ["xcrun", "simctl", "list", "devices", "available", "-j"], text=True)
data = json.loads(output)
devices = [device for runtime, group in data.get("devices", {}).items()
           if "iOS" in runtime for device in group
           if device.get("isAvailable", True) and "iPhone" in device.get("name", "")]
device = next((d for d in devices if d.get("state") == "Booted"),
              devices[0] if devices else None)
if device is None:
    sys.exit("No available iPhone simulator. Check Xcode runtimes.")
print(device["udid"])
```

### Minimal XcodeGen target layout

For a fresh repo, an initial `project.yml` can be generated with the following app-only starter; replace deployment target and bundle ID with validated project values, then add local package products only after the VisualCore audit.

```yaml
name: DigitalAquarium
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.example.visualcore
targets:
  DigitalAquarium:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    deploymentTarget: "17.0"   # proposal, verify supported OS
    sources:
      - Apps/DigitalAquarium
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.visualcore.digital-aquarium
```

Install XcodeGen through its official distribution if not already available, verify `xcodegen --version`, and run `xcodegen generate` only after this file and target source exist. Avoid storing unreviewed private package tokens in `project.yml` or CI.

### Suggested macOS GitHub Actions job (create after actual build validation)

```yaml
name: iOS CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Verify Python and repository artifacts
        run: python3 scripts/check_repo.py
      - name: Inspect Xcode and app schemes
        run: xcodebuild -list -project DigitalAquarium.xcodeproj
      - name: Build simulator target
        run: xcodebuild -project DigitalAquarium.xcodeproj -scheme DigitalAquarium -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Pin CI action revisions and the Xcode version according to your organization’s supply-chain rules; add simulator unit tests and any authenticated VisualCore package fetch only after configuration is proven to work. CI on macOS does not substitute for physical GPU regression testing.

## 15. Acceptance criteria and definition of done

A first-release candidate is acceptable only when **all** of the following can be demonstrated:

- [ ] MVP-01: One complete aquarium with two fish species and plants.
- [ ] MVP-02: Bounded 2D/2.5D school behaviors and swim animation.
- [ ] MVP-03: Tap-to-feed and decoration placement gestures.
- [ ] MVP-04: Bubbles, caustics, depth layers and environmental particles.
- [ ] MVP-05: Persistent habitat configurations and safe restore.
- [ ] MVP-06: Low-motion/low-power ambient mode with auto dimming.
- [ ] Standalone app uses public audited VisualCore APIs and shared ANGLE/Metal path, not ProjectM-specific engine internals.
- [ ] Render-state serializations are versioned, validated, and safe after background/resume and renderer reset.
- [ ] Native UI is usable with accessibility features; reduced motion and quality controls behave as stated.
- [ ] Domain and integration test cases in §11 pass; unresolved errors are documented, not marked passing.
- [ ] At least one physical device run with recorded build/OS/device metadata validates actual GPU behavior.
- [ ] No unsupported privacy, scientific or platform capability claims remain in the product UI or listing.
- [ ] Bundled third-party code, shaders, assets, educational facts and sounds have reviewed license/source records.
- [ ] Build from a clean macOS checkout succeeds and the final PR contains exact verification commands and results.
- [ ] Any VisualCore changes have their own upstream PR plus before/after ProjectM reference regression evidence.

## 16. Ordered next actions

1. Create a new `DigitalAquarium` app repo and initialize the Claude/Spec Kit Python variant (commands in §7).
2. Perform read-only VisualCore package/render-host inspection; resolve actual public APIs and upstream gaps.
3. Save the constitution and app-specific design decisions in reviewed repository artifacts.
4. Run Phase 00 through all eight quality gates; complete any upstream VisualCore feature as a separate, reviewed change.
5. Implement Phase 01 habitat model and content license audit as the smallest testable vertical slice.
6. Continue the remaining phases one by one; compare every release claim against the acceptance matrix.
7. Archive evidence from physical device validation and review the release privacy/license checklist.

# Neon Arcade
## iOS application architecture and Spec Kit + Claude Code implementation manual

**Concept #10 of 25** | **Category:** Games and interactive experiences | **Proposed app/repository target:** `NeonArcade`
**Planning status:** proposed implementation guide; not proof of an existing application or released VisualCore package. **Source:** `AppsBrainstorm.md` catalog item 10; `README.md` VisualCore architecture and Spec Kit strategy.
**Rendering invariant:** reuse the existing ProjectM-proven OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal infrastructure exposed by VisualCore. Never create a duplicate EGL/ANGLE backend or link ProjectM engine internals into this independent app.

---

## 1. Executive summary and source traceability

A compact collection of highly legible arcade games with glow, particles and disciplined game logic.

### Original brainstorm concept

> A collection of visually distinctive arcade games built around simple mechanics, glowing effects, particle systems, and procedural backgrounds.

**VisualCore capabilities listed in the brainstorm:**
- 2D rendering
- Particles
- Animation
- Input handling
- Collision visualization
- Scene transitions

**Original product opportunity:** A collection of small, polished games with a consistent visual identity.

**Recommended product hypothesis:** A carefully scoped, offline-capable first release can demonstrate a distinct graphics workload and validate reusable VisualCore APIs. Test this hypothesis with a functioning vertical slice before expanding content or monetization.

## 2. Product contract and scope

### Primary audiences
- Casual mobile players
- Kids and families looking for simple controls
- Developers evaluating VisualCore for game loops

### End-to-end user journeys
1. **Journey 1:** Launch a polished one-thumb dodge game, learn rules in five seconds.
2. **Journey 2:** Survive timed waves, get feedback on collision and score.
3. **Journey 3:** Restart instantly, unlock alternative visual palettes and track local high score.

### Version 0.1 feature contract
1. **Feature 01:** One complete game first: Neon Dodge with player lane, falling hazards and collectible orbs. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
2. **Feature 02:** Deterministic fixed-step update loop and authoritative collision rules. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
3. **Feature 03:** Start/pause/restart/game-over flows with local scores. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
4. **Feature 04:** Touch steering with configurable sensitivity. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
5. **Feature 05:** Particles, glow and visual feedback constrained by game readability. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
6. **Feature 06:** Sound/haptic toggles and reduced-flash controls. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.

### Explicit non-goals
- An entire arcade collection before first release
- Unmoderated online leaderboards or user-generated levels
- Monetized loot boxes

### Later-stage ideas, not MVP commitments
- Second game with a separate rules engine and shared renderer
- On-device achievements
- Signed replay exchange

## 3. UX blueprint

The first launch should reach a meaningful working graphic or educational interaction without requiring an account. Use SwiftUI for navigation, settings, labels and accessibility; host VisualCore rendering in a verified UIView/UIViewRepresentable integration that owns no duplicate GPU lifecycle.

**Proposed screen inventory** (adapt to the app-specific flows above):
| Screen | Responsibility | Concrete behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Home / gallery | Start without setup | Curated Neon Arcade example, recent scene and explicit entry point |
| Interactive scene | Primary VisualCore rendering surface | Touch and app-state changes mapped into validated domain commands |
| Inspector | Controls and explanations | Show effective parameter values, reset and valid ranges |
| Library / files | Persistence where relevant | Open, duplicate, save, import/export only via permitted system APIs |
| Settings / help | Quality, accessibility, privacy | Explain input permissions, limitations, credits and renderer fallback |

**Interaction design rules:** screen gestures must have a deterministic domain meaning; rendering can interpolate but cannot silently change persisted state. State-affecting controls should be testable independent of the GPU. All critical feedback must remain legible without bloom, color alone, or animation.

### State transitions to implement
```text
uninitialized → loading-assets → ready → active
                                  ↔ paused / backgrounded
                                  ↘ editing / exporting (if supported)
any GPU state → renderer-lost → recover-resources → ready
any document state → validation-error → recoverable-message
```

Do not upload application/scene state to a server by default. If future features introduce accounts, cloud sync or sharing, write a new privacy and threat-model spec before implementation.

## 4. Architecture: VisualCore consumer, not renderer fork

```text
NeonArcade SwiftUI app (navigation, accessibility, preferences)
    ↓ commands / immutable snapshots
NeonArcadeCore (domain rules, models, persistence schemas, validation)
    ↓ render-state snapshot; never raw SwiftUI bindings
NeonArcadeRendering (scene adapter, shaders, asset IDs, pass descriptions)
    ↓ public APIs discovered in the real VisualCore checkout
VisualCore runtime, shaders, effects, scenes, inputs, diagnostics
    ↓ shared EGL/context/render host as audited
Existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal implementation
    ↓
iOS device GPU and display
```

**Ownership policy:** The app owns its content, mathematical rules, domain schema, UI and business logic. VisualCore owns generic graphics infrastructure. `Coastrnaut/projectm-ios` remains VisualCore's pinned reference submodule, not an app dependency. Any VisualCore API needed but not present must be proposed upstream with a test and an API contract; do not stub an imaginary package into production.

### Contracts and threading
- A domain coordinator produces immutable render snapshots or bounded commands; presentation does not mutate simulation truth.
- The VisualCore render host controls the EGL context, resource lifetime, presentation and the required render thread/queue; all GL work obeys that ownership.
- Native SwiftUI overlays remain separate from shader drawing where legibility, hit-testing and VoiceOver need native controls.
- On scene resize, background, memory warning or renderer reset, reallocate GPU resources from versioned CPU state rather than persisting raw GL handles.
- Shaders are treated as bundled, versioned assets unless the specific product explicitly supports user-authored GLSL with additional guards.

### Application-specific components
- **`GameRun.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`FixedStepClock.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`CollisionSolver.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`WaveDirector.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`HighScoreStore.swift`**: data storage, schema validation, assets or export; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`NeonDodgeRenderer.swift`**: renderer-facing render orchestration and GPU pass bindings; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.

## 6. Domain model, algorithms and rendering design

### Versioned domain schemas (proposed types)
| Type | Field contract / required invariants |
|---|---|
| `GameRun` | `GameRun(seed, elapsedTicks, score, lives, paused, waveIndex)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `PlayerState` | `PlayerState(position, velocity, hitbox, invulnerabilityTicks)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `SpawnWave` | `SpawnWave(patternID, spawnTick, hazardDefinitions)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `HighScore` | `HighScore(boardVersion, score, achievedAt)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |

Use explicit units and coordinate spaces in type names or documentation. Reject NaN/Inf, invalid counts, truncated files, unreasonable allocations and unsupported versions where applicable. Canonical storage should be pure data; expensive buffers can be reconstructed.

### Algorithm and correctness decisions
1. Advance game world with fixed delta tick independent of display frame rate.
2. Use continuous or swept collision for fast moving hazards to prevent tunneling.
3. Separate collision geometry from sprites and post-effects.
4. Serialize deterministic input events for test replays; render may interpolate but never decides hit outcomes.

### App-specific render sequence
1. **Stage 1:** Process touch input into intent vector.
2. **Stage 2:** Run input and wave spawning on fixed-step simulation.
3. **Stage 3:** Resolve collision/scoring on CPU domain model.
4. **Stage 4:** Render layered sprites, hazards, additive glow and feedback particles through VisualCore.

### Rendering lifecycle and frame budget
- Create resources only after VisualCore signals a valid owning EGL context; release/recreate on context loss and size changes.
- Separate fixed-step simulation, event handling, visual animation time and wall time when the product uses more than one.
- Treat device tier as policy data: resolution scale, effect counts, iterations and object count may change; domain correctness and user state may not.
- Validate framebuffer completeness, shader compile/link results, texture format support and GPU resource handles before presenting a frame.
- Record frame pacing, app-owned CPU time, allocation counts and renderer recovery on a real device before selecting release targets.

### Required capability audit against VisualCore
- **2D rendering** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Particles** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Animation** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Input handling** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Collision visualization** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Scene transitions** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.

> **Domain-specific engineering rule:** Keep graphics effects a VisualCore client, not the authoritative game simulation. Visual readability is a functional acceptance criterion.

## 7. Local environment and reproducible bootstrap

**Prerequisites:** macOS and Xcode for iOS build, signing, Simulator and physical-device tests; Git, Python 3, `uv`, and Claude Code CLI. Windows can prepare specifications and source but cannot validate the iOS rendering path without a macOS builder. Follow current vendor instructions for installation; verify tool versions rather than assuming they exist.

**Terminal on macOS — commands to create this app repository:**
```bash
mkdir NeonArcade && cd NeonArcade
git init -b main
git --version
python3 --version
uv --version
claude --version
uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git
specify version
specify init --help
specify init --here --integration claude --script py
specify check
git status --short
claude
```

Initialize Spec Kit **once** in a newly created repository. In a non-empty existing repo, commit/backup first and inspect `specify init --help`; `--force` may merge/overwrite managed files and must not be run blindly. Never run Spec Kit initialization inside the VisualCore or ProjectM submodule from an app repo.

**Current Claude Code integration:** Spec Kit creates `.claude/skills/speckit-<command>/SKILL.md`; invoke skills in Claude chat using **hyphens**, e.g. `/speckit-specify`, not the dotted spelling used in some generic documentation. Confirm actual skills with `find .claude/skills -name SKILL.md` and Claude `/help` because installed versions can differ. See official [Claude integration](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html).

**Terminal — verify a local VisualCore checkout without assuming package products:**
```bash
test -d ../VisualCore || { echo "Clone or locate the VisualCore repository beside this app first"; exit 1; }
git -C ../VisualCore status --short
find ../VisualCore -name Package.swift -not -path "*/.build/*" -print
git -C ../VisualCore submodule status
```

If `../VisualCore` does not yet provide a consumer package, create an upstream integration feature and stop at a no-op host skeleton. Do not invent `VisualCoreRenderer` product names or fake ANGLE integration code.

## 8. Paste-ready repository constitution and Claude policy

**Terminal:**

```bash
git status --short
git diff --check

```

**Claude Code chat, at every task boundary:**
```text
Inspect the active Spec Kit tasks file. Implement only the next smallest dependency-complete task group. Before editing, list intended files, known VisualCore API contracts, test commands, and rollback steps. After editing, run tests and report actual results; do not claim device validation without device logs. Stop for review after this group.
```

Do not ask Claude to run all seven phases unattended. Spec Kit artifacts may expose architecture errors or rights/permission issues that materially change the following work. The Git baseline is reviewed per phase; commit evidence and tests in the application repository, and upstream patches separately.

## 11. Domain, renderer and UI verification matrix

| Layer | App-specific test | Evidence / gate |
|---|---|---|
| Pure domain model | Recorded input replay produces identical score and collision ticks | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Pure domain model | Background/resume freezes simulation rather than catching up | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Swept collision catches high-speed hazards | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | High score is not corrupted by abrupt termination | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Device or end-to-end | Hitboxes remain readable when bloom quality settings change | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Shared render lifecycle | Repeated renderer create, resize, background, resume, context recovery, release | Device log with no stale EGL/GL handles or persistent GPU memory growth |
| App UI and accessibility | First-session flow, disabled states, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver fallback | UI test + human review on representative iPhone and iPad |
| VisualCore regression | If VisualCore changes, ProjectM remains functional at pinned submodule commit | Existing ProjectM build/smoke log; any difference reviewed |

### Implementation-level fixtures
- Fixture 1: Recorded input replay produces identical score and collision ticks.
- Fixture 2: Background/resume freezes simulation rather than catching up.
- Fixture 3: Swept collision catches high-speed hazards.
- Fixture 4: High score is not corrupted by abrupt termination.
- Fixture 5: Hitboxes remain readable when bloom quality settings change.

### Simulator and device separation
- CI/simulator: test domain math, model migration, document round trips, permission-denied paths, basic UI and reproducible app builds.
- Physical iPhone/iPad: validate ANGLE Metal path, shader compilation, context loss, high-refresh/low-refresh behavior, thermals, memory, inputs and real audio/device sensor routes if relevant.
- When tests depend on audio, sensors or input permissions, use synthetic fixtures in CI; do not silently substitute test signals for production sources.
- Store exact Xcode, iOS, device, VisualCore revision, ProjectM submodule revision, preset and test duration with performance reports.

## 12. Profiling plan, budgets and graceful fallback

Before specifying absolute fps, startup or memory targets, measure a baseline on the reference app and at least one representative device. Decide thresholds in a separate acceptance ADR; do not publish invented benchmark numbers.

- Prioritize predictable input-to-action latency and p95 frame time.
- Measure overdraw and avoid full-screen expensive bloom on low tiers.
- Run 30 and 60 Hz timing tests for equivalent simulation outcomes.

**Telemetry only as local diagnostics by default:** record per-pass timing if genuinely supported, present interval, app-side CPU duration, memory and resource counts, scene configuration, chosen quality tier and build IDs. Make collection opt-in if data ever leaves the device. Never label CPU timings as GPU timings.

**Fallback policy:** keep the app usable when expensive shader passes fail or a device is below target capability: reduce resolution/passes, use a simpler scene, preserve user state, and display a recoverable explanation. When no VisualCore render host exists, ship a native UI placeholder only for internal integration testing—not a misleading App Store release.

## 13. Risks, privacy, science/platform constraints and licenses

### App-specific risk register
1. **Risk 1:** Effects that obscure obstacles hurt playability—cap bloom and preserve contrast. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
2. **Risk 2:** Frame-rate-dependent game logic causes inconsistent difficulty—fixed timestep. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
3. **Risk 3:** Additional games multiply maintenance—ship one vertical slice and validate retention. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.

### Cross-cutting obligations
- No private iOS APIs, undocumented system-level audio interception, automatic wallpaper changes or unsupported GPU access; test any requested platform capability against current public documentation.
- Apply least-privilege permission prompts, with useful demo/offline behavior for denied permissions. Document Photos, Files, microphone or audio rights only where that app actually needs them.
- Maintain licenses for ANGLE, VisualCore, ProjectM reference code and all bundled shaders, meshes, textures, fonts, datasets, sound and educational copy. Do not assume upstream assets may be redistributed.
- Use clear scientific/educational caveats wherever simulations or graphics are illustrative. Do not market a toy visualization as an instrument, diagnostic tool or accurate predictive model.
- Validate imported data formats, sizes, paths and schema versions; avoid executing untrusted user code except in the specifically constrained Shader Studio design.

### Content and App Store review checklist
- Document why each permission is necessary and the exact UI path requesting it.
- Provide privacy policy and required app data disclosures based on actual telemetry/storage behavior, not sample text.
- Check all media and code redistribution rights, attribution and trademark rules before the storefront submission.
- Keep claims in marketing and screenshots aligned to implemented working features and measured/attributed facts.

## 14. Xcode project, build, and CI commands

After selecting XcodeGen and writing a real `project.yml` during Phase 0/1, these are executable examples **from this app repo**. Scheme and target names must be confirmed with `xcodebuild -list`; do not assume VisualCore has a particular SPM product name.

```bash
# Use XcodeGen only if project.yml was adopted and reviewed
xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -list -project NeonArcade.xcodeproj
xcodebuild -project NeonArcade.xcodeproj -scheme NeonArcade -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
xcrun simctl list devices available
SIMULATOR_UDID="$(python3 scripts/select_simulator.py)"
test -n "$SIMULATOR_UDID" || { echo "No available simulator"; exit 1; }
xcodebuild -project NeonArcade.xcodeproj -scheme NeonArcade -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIMULATOR_UDID" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test
python3 scripts/check_repo.py
```

If the repo uses an `.xcworkspace`, SwiftPM-generated project or a different scheme, inspect it and replace these paths; the test commands above do not constitute successful execution here. Build/sign/archive and test native ANGLE/Metal rendering on macOS with Xcode and a physical device.

### Minimal Python repository audit script

Create `scripts/check_repo.py` during the first phase. It should verify presence of essential architecture documents and app-owned shaders, then print the pinned VisualCore version using an actual resolved dependency file. Do not automatically download code or modify an upstream checkout.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import sys
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
required = ["CLAUDE.md", "docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md"]
missing = [name for name in required if not (root / name).is_file()]
for path in missing:
    print(f"MISSING: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
if missing:
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("Repository guidance and integration contract are present")
```

### Portable Python 3 simulator selection helper

Save as `scripts/select_simulator.py`; it reads `xcrun simctl` JSON and chooses a booted iOS simulator first, otherwise an available iPhone simulator. This helper does not create or boot a device; select/boot one manually if no compatible runtime is installed.

```python
import json
import subprocess
import sys
output = subprocess.check_output(
    ["xcrun", "simctl", "list", "devices", "available", "-j"], text=True)
data = json.loads(output)
devices = [device for runtime, group in data.get("devices", {}).items()
           if "iOS" in runtime for device in group
           if device.get("isAvailable", True) and "iPhone" in device.get("name", "")]
device = next((d for d in devices if d.get("state") == "Booted"),
              devices[0] if devices else None)
if device is None:
    sys.exit("No available iPhone simulator. Check Xcode runtimes.")
print(device["udid"])
```

### Minimal XcodeGen target layout

For a fresh repo, an initial `project.yml` can be generated with the following app-only starter; replace deployment target and bundle ID with validated project values, then add local package products only after the VisualCore audit.

```yaml
name: NeonArcade
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.example.visualcore
targets:
  NeonArcade:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    deploymentTarget: "17.0"   # proposal, verify supported OS
    sources:
      - Apps/NeonArcade
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.visualcore.neon-arcade
```

Install XcodeGen through its official distribution if not already available, verify `xcodegen --version`, and run `xcodegen generate` only after this file and target source exist. Avoid storing unreviewed private package tokens in `project.yml` or CI.

### Suggested macOS GitHub Actions job (create after actual build validation)

```yaml
name: iOS CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Verify Python and repository artifacts
        run: python3 scripts/check_repo.py
      - name: Inspect Xcode and app schemes
        run: xcodebuild -list -project NeonArcade.xcodeproj
      - name: Build simulator target
        run: xcodebuild -project NeonArcade.xcodeproj -scheme NeonArcade -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Pin CI action revisions and the Xcode version according to your organization’s supply-chain rules; add simulator unit tests and any authenticated VisualCore package fetch only after configuration is proven to work. CI on macOS does not substitute for physical GPU regression testing.

## 15. Acceptance criteria and definition of done

A first-release candidate is acceptable only when **all** of the following can be demonstrated:

- [ ] MVP-01: One complete game first: Neon Dodge with player lane, falling hazards and collectible orbs.
- [ ] MVP-02: Deterministic fixed-step update loop and authoritative collision rules.
- [ ] MVP-03: Start/pause/restart/game-over flows with local scores.
- [ ] MVP-04: Touch steering with configurable sensitivity.
- [ ] MVP-05: Particles, glow and visual feedback constrained by game readability.
- [ ] MVP-06: Sound/haptic toggles and reduced-flash controls.
- [ ] Standalone app uses public audited VisualCore APIs and shared ANGLE/Metal path, not ProjectM-specific engine internals.
- [ ] Render-state serializations are versioned, validated, and safe after background/resume and renderer reset.
- [ ] Native UI is usable with accessibility features; reduced motion and quality controls behave as stated.
- [ ] Domain and integration test cases in §11 pass; unresolved errors are documented, not marked passing.
- [ ] At least one physical device run with recorded build/OS/device metadata validates actual GPU behavior.
- [ ] No unsupported privacy, scientific or platform capability claims remain in the product UI or listing.
- [ ] Bundled third-party code, shaders, assets, educational facts and sounds have reviewed license/source records.
- [ ] Build from a clean macOS checkout succeeds and the final PR contains exact verification commands and results.
- [ ] Any VisualCore changes have their own upstream PR plus before/after ProjectM reference regression evidence.

## 16. Ordered next actions

1. Create a new `NeonArcade` app repo and initialize the Claude/Spec Kit Python variant (commands in §7).
2. Perform read-only VisualCore package/render-host inspection; resolve actual public APIs and upstream gaps.
3. Save the constitution and app-specific design decisions in reviewed repository artifacts.
4. Run Phase 00 through all eight quality gates; complete any upstream VisualCore feature as a separate, reviewed change.
5. Implement Phase 01 fixed-step engine and collision fixtures as the smallest testable vertical slice.
6. Continue the remaining phases one by one; compare every release claim against the acceptance matrix.
7. Archive evidence from physical device validation and review the release privacy/license checklist.

# Physics Playground
## iOS application architecture and Spec Kit + Claude Code implementation manual

**Concept #11 of 25** | **Category:** Games and interactive experiences | **Proposed app/repository target:** `PhysicsPlayground`
**Planning status:** proposed implementation guide; not proof of an existing application or released VisualCore package. **Source:** `AppsBrainstorm.md` catalog item 11; `README.md` VisualCore architecture and Spec Kit strategy.
**Rendering invariant:** reuse the existing ProjectM-proven OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal infrastructure exposed by VisualCore. Never create a duplicate EGL/ANGLE backend or link ProjectM engine internals into this independent app.

---

## 1. Executive summary and source traceability

A deterministic sandbox for gravity, collisions, springs and forces with explanatory overlays.

### Original brainstorm concept

> An interactive sandbox for gravity, collisions, springs, magnets, fluids, and other physical interactions.

**VisualCore capabilities listed in the brainstorm:**
- Scene rendering
- Geometry
- Animation
- Shader-based effects
- Data visualization

**Original product opportunity:** An educational and entertaining physics toy.

**Recommended product hypothesis:** A carefully scoped, offline-capable first release can demonstrate a distinct graphics workload and validate reusable VisualCore APIs. Test this hypothesis with a functioning vertical slice before expanding content or monetization.

## 2. Product contract and scope

### Primary audiences
- Children experimenting with motion
- Teachers giving live demonstrations
- Physics enthusiasts seeking an approachable simulation toy

### End-to-end user journeys
1. **Journey 1:** Drop objects into a stage and start gravity.
2. **Journey 2:** Draw a spring between objects and alter stiffness.
3. **Journey 3:** Pause, single-step, inspect energy and reset from a preset.

### Version 0.1 feature contract
1. **Feature 01:** 2D circles and boxes with rigid-body collision. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
2. **Feature 02:** Constant gravity, springs and drag forces. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
3. **Feature 03:** Object spawn, grab, pin and delete gestures. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
4. **Feature 04:** Simulation pause/single step, time scale and reset. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
5. **Feature 05:** Presets for pendulum, spring chain and stacked objects. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
6. **Feature 06:** Optional velocity/force vector overlays and measured state panel. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.

### Explicit non-goals
- Physically complete engineering simulation
- Real 3D soft bodies or fluid solver
- Safety-critical prediction claims

### Later-stage ideas, not MVP commitments
- Inclined planes, rotational motors and magnets
- Data-plot export and classroom activities
- More sophisticated 3D constraints

## 3. UX blueprint

The first launch should reach a meaningful working graphic or educational interaction without requiring an account. Use SwiftUI for navigation, settings, labels and accessibility; host VisualCore rendering in a verified UIView/UIViewRepresentable integration that owns no duplicate GPU lifecycle.

**Proposed screen inventory** (adapt to the app-specific flows above):
| Screen | Responsibility | Concrete behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Home / gallery | Start without setup | Curated Physics Playground example, recent scene and explicit entry point |
| Interactive scene | Primary VisualCore rendering surface | Touch and app-state changes mapped into validated domain commands |
| Inspector | Controls and explanations | Show effective parameter values, reset and valid ranges |
| Library / files | Persistence where relevant | Open, duplicate, save, import/export only via permitted system APIs |
| Settings / help | Quality, accessibility, privacy | Explain input permissions, limitations, credits and renderer fallback |

**Interaction design rules:** screen gestures must have a deterministic domain meaning; rendering can interpolate but cannot silently change persisted state. State-affecting controls should be testable independent of the GPU. All critical feedback must remain legible without bloom, color alone, or animation.

### State transitions to implement
```text
uninitialized → loading-assets → ready → active
                                  ↔ paused / backgrounded
                                  ↘ editing / exporting (if supported)
any GPU state → renderer-lost → recover-resources → ready
any document state → validation-error → recoverable-message
```

Do not upload application/scene state to a server by default. If future features introduce accounts, cloud sync or sharing, write a new privacy and threat-model spec before implementation.

## 4. Architecture: VisualCore consumer, not renderer fork

```text
PhysicsPlayground SwiftUI app (navigation, accessibility, preferences)
    ↓ commands / immutable snapshots
PhysicsPlaygroundCore (domain rules, models, persistence schemas, validation)
    ↓ render-state snapshot; never raw SwiftUI bindings
PhysicsPlaygroundRendering (scene adapter, shaders, asset IDs, pass descriptions)
    ↓ public APIs discovered in the real VisualCore checkout
VisualCore runtime, shaders, effects, scenes, inputs, diagnostics
    ↓ shared EGL/context/render host as audited
Existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal implementation
    ↓
iOS device GPU and display
```

**Ownership policy:** The app owns its content, mathematical rules, domain schema, UI and business logic. VisualCore owns generic graphics infrastructure. `Coastrnaut/projectm-ios` remains VisualCore's pinned reference submodule, not an app dependency. Any VisualCore API needed but not present must be proposed upstream with a test and an API contract; do not stub an imaginary package into production.

### Contracts and threading
- A domain coordinator produces immutable render snapshots or bounded commands; presentation does not mutate simulation truth.
- The VisualCore render host controls the EGL context, resource lifetime, presentation and the required render thread/queue; all GL work obeys that ownership.
- Native SwiftUI overlays remain separate from shader drawing where legibility, hit-testing and VoiceOver need native controls.
- On scene resize, background, memory warning or renderer reset, reallocate GPU resources from versioned CPU state rather than persisting raw GL handles.
- Shaders are treated as bundled, versioned assets unless the specific product explicitly supports user-authored GLSL with additional guards.

### Application-specific components
- **`PhysicsWorld.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`RigidBody.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`CollisionDetection.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`ContactSolver.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`SpringConstraint.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`ExperimentStore.swift`**: data storage, schema validation, assets or export; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`PhysicsRenderer.swift`**: renderer-facing render orchestration and GPU pass bindings; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.

After VisualCore is published, pin an immutable reviewed tag/revision. The project generator and package structure should be selected before the first implementation PR.

### File creation policy
- Generate the minimum Xcode app target and package source files required by the first vertical slice. Do not pre-create dozens of empty Swift files.
- Keep application shader files local when specific to this product; move a shader helper to VisualCore only after an independent use-case and regression tests justify reuse.
- Store data fixtures in JSON/CSV where appropriate, with explicit schema and license metadata; do not serialize GPU buffer addresses or EGL objects.
- Keep all feature specs under `specs/` created by Spec Kit; allow its installed release to determine feature numbering and active feature selection.

## 6. Domain model, algorithms and rendering design

### Versioned domain schemas (proposed types)
| Type | Field contract / required invariants |
|---|---|
| `PhysicsBody` | `PhysicsBody(id, shape, mass, inertia, pose, velocity, restitution, friction)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `SpringConstraint` | `SpringConstraint(bodyA, bodyB, restLength, stiffness, damping)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `WorldSettings` | `WorldSettings(gravity, fixedTimeStep, solverIterations, boundary)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `ExperimentDocument` | `ExperimentDocument(schemaVersion, bodies, constraints, settings)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |

Use explicit units and coordinate spaces in type names or documentation. Reject NaN/Inf, invalid counts, truncated files, unreasonable allocations and unsupported versions where applicable. Canonical storage should be pure data; expensive buffers can be reconstructed.

### Algorithm and correctness decisions
1. Start with a fixed-step CPU 2D solver and broadphase for a small object count.
2. Use impulse-based collision with restitution/friction and conservative positional correction.
3. Apply spring forces with stability guardrails and bounded stiffness for chosen dt.
4. Compute diagnostics separately; explicitly label results as educational approximations.

### App-specific render sequence
1. **Stage 1:** Collect editor operations.
2. **Stage 2:** Advance force accumulator, broadphase and narrowphase collision.
3. **Stage 3:** Solve constraints and integrate poses at bounded fixed time step.
4. **Stage 4:** Upload transforms and draw rigid bodies, vector arrows and contact effects.

### Rendering lifecycle and frame budget
- Create resources only after VisualCore signals a valid owning EGL context; release/recreate on context loss and size changes.
- Separate fixed-step simulation, event handling, visual animation time and wall time when the product uses more than one.
- Treat device tier as policy data: resolution scale, effect counts, iterations and object count may change; domain correctness and user state may not.
- Validate framebuffer completeness, shader compile/link results, texture format support and GPU resource handles before presenting a frame.
- Record frame pacing, app-owned CPU time, allocation counts and renderer recovery on a real device before selecting release targets.

### Required capability audit against VisualCore
- **Scene rendering** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Geometry** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Animation** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Shader-based effects** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Data visualization** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.

> **Domain-specific engineering rule:** Do not offload simulation into a shader merely because VisualCore offers GPUs; choose CPU deterministic baseline and use VisualCore strictly for visualization.

## 7. Local environment and reproducible bootstrap

**Prerequisites:** macOS and Xcode for iOS build, signing, Simulator and physical-device tests; Git, Python 3, `uv`, and Claude Code CLI. Windows can prepare specifications and source but cannot validate the iOS rendering path without a macOS builder. Follow current vendor instructions for installation; verify tool versions rather than assuming they exist.

**Terminal on macOS — commands to create this app repository:**
```bash
mkdir PhysicsPlayground && cd PhysicsPlayground
git init -b main
git --version
python3 --version
uv --version
claude --version
uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git
specify version
specify init --help
specify init --here --integration claude --script py
specify check
git status --short
claude
```

Initialize Spec Kit **once** in a newly created repository. In a non-empty existing repo, commit/backup first and inspect `specify init --help`; `--force` may merge/overwrite managed files and must not be run blindly. Never run Spec Kit initialization inside the VisualCore or ProjectM submodule from an app repo.

**Current Claude Code integration:** Spec Kit creates `.claude/skills/speckit-<command>/SKILL.md`; invoke skills in Claude chat using **hyphens**, e.g. `/speckit-specify`, not the dotted spelling used in some generic documentation. Confirm actual skills with `find .claude/skills -name SKILL.md` and Claude `/help` because installed versions can differ. See official [Claude integration](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html).

**Terminal — verify a local VisualCore checkout without assuming package products:**
```bash
test -d ../VisualCore || { echo "Clone or locate the VisualCore repository beside this app first"; exit 1; }
git -C ../VisualCore status --short
find ../VisualCore -name Package.swift -not -path "*/.build/*" -print
git -C ../VisualCore submodule status
```

If `../VisualCore` does not yet provide a consumer package, create an upstream integration feature and stop at a no-op host skeleton. Do not invent `VisualCoreRenderer` product names or fake ANGLE integration code.

**Inside Claude Code chat, from this app repo:**
```text
/speckit-constitution Define the constitution for Physics Playground. Build a standalone iOS/iPadOS VisualCore consumer, never a fork of projectm-ios. Reuse only audited VisualCore public APIs over the existing OpenGL ES→ANGLE→Metal integration. Domain rules and persisted files must be testable without GPU access. Keep the app offline-first, disclose permissions, use bounded GPU resources, support accessibility, record asset licenses, and prohibit unsupported scientific/platform claims. Require a ProjectM regression check whenever VisualCore is modified. Use Python 3 for repository automation; no PowerShell dependency. Implement only one approved Spec Kit phase at a time.
```

```markdown
# Physics Playground — Claude Code Engineering Rules

- Product goal: A deterministic sandbox for gravity, collisions, springs and forces with explanatory overlays.
- Read `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md` before editing graphics integration.
- VisualCore owns the graphics lifecycle; never create an independent ANGLE/EGL initialization path.
- Do not import ProjectM engine internals or duplicate third-party sources.
- Domain truth, deterministic tests and versioned persistence must not depend on GL contexts.
- Use Python scripts for repeatable source/schema/license validation.
- Request explicit approval before changing the adjacent VisualCore repository.
- Report uncertainty and platform limitations; do not invent APIs or test results.
- Complete Spec Kit clarify → plan → checklist → tasks → analyze before implementing a phase.
- Run relevant tests; log exact macOS/Xcode/device/VisualCore revisions used.
- Keep each PR bounded to one feature phase and document migration/rollback plan.
```

## 9. Implementation phases with **actual Spec Kit / Claude Code commands**

Run the following blocks **inside Claude Code chat**, **not** your shell. Each phase should produce its own `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, tests and reviewable PR; use the actual active feature convention generated by your Spec Kit version. Execute the next phase only after the preceding acceptance checks pass. Slash commands below follow the current Claude skill installation; if your installed integration differs, inspect its generated `.claude/skills/`.

### Phase 00 — Foundation and VisualCore boundary audit

**Deliverable:** Produce read-only repository inventory; map VisualCore package products, EGL host, render thread, shader/resource APIs, Xcode build steps, actual source ownership and baseline ProjectM regression tests. Record open architectural gaps. Do not modify VisualCore or ProjectM.

**Review / acceptance gates:**
- An evidence-backed integration matrix references real files, symbols and package products
- The app can compile an empty SwiftUI shell before custom graphics integration
- A written stop/go decision identifies anything missing upstream

```text
/speckit-specify For Physics Playground Phase 00 (Foundation and VisualCore boundary audit): Produce read-only repository inventory; map VisualCore package products, EGL host, render thread, shader/resource APIs, Xcode build steps, actual source ownership and baseline ProjectM regression tests. Record open architectural gaps. Do not modify VisualCore or ProjectM. Capture measurable user stories, edge cases, traceability to the brainstorm and negative requirements.
/speckit-clarify Review this Phase 00 spec for unverified VisualCore APIs, permissions, algorithm semantics, performance assumptions and unsupported iOS behavior. Ask only blocking questions; record decisions in spec artifacts.
/speckit-plan Create the Phase 00 technical plan. Give exact app-owned source paths, dependency direction, lifecycle contracts, data schemas, tests, build commands, migration and rollback; reference only APIs verified by the read-only audit.
/speckit-checklist Generate a Phase 00 checklist covering requirements completeness, privacy, architecture ownership, iOS lifecycle, testability, performance and release constraints as applicable.
/speckit-tasks Break Phase 00 into dependency-ordered tasks with specific files, tests, integration acceptance criteria, commit boundaries and review checkpoints.
/speckit-analyze Validate Phase 00 spec/plan/tasks consistency, remove speculative dependencies, identify missing tests, and stop if blockers remain.
/speckit-implement Execute only approved Phase 00 tasks in small groups. For each group implement tests first where sensible, run available build/validation, report changed files and results; do not modify VisualCore without an approved upstream task.
/speckit-converge Compare Phase 00 implementation with requirements and tests, append any unresolved tasks, and produce an evidence-based completion report.
```

**Stop point:** Review the diff, execute the phase-specific tests, and commit only when the phase meets its stated acceptance. In particular, absence of a working VisualCore host is a blocker, not permission to create a second backend.

### Phase 06 — Final verification, privacy, packaging and release

**Deliverable:** Complete release readiness for Physics Playground: privacy/permission strings, accessibility, App Store asset/credit review, local data migration, CPU/GPU/device tests, crash recovery, and build/archive instructions. No fabricated measured performance claims.

**Review / acceptance gates:**
- Release checklist and artifact inventory are complete
- All required automated and device tests have attached results
- Unsupported promised features are removed from UI and marketing copy

```text
/speckit-specify For Physics Playground Phase 06 (Final verification, privacy, packaging and release): Complete release readiness for Physics Playground: privacy/permission strings, accessibility, App Store asset/credit review, local data migration, CPU/GPU/device tests, crash recovery, and build/archive instructions. No fabricated measured performance claims. Capture measurable user stories, edge cases, traceability to the brainstorm and negative requirements.
/speckit-clarify Review this Phase 06 spec for unverified VisualCore APIs, permissions, algorithm semantics, performance assumptions and unsupported iOS behavior. Ask only blocking questions; record decisions in spec artifacts.
/speckit-plan Create the Phase 06 technical plan. Give exact app-owned source paths, dependency direction, lifecycle contracts, data schemas, tests, build commands, migration and rollback; reference only APIs verified by the read-only audit.
/speckit-checklist Generate a Phase 06 checklist covering requirements completeness, privacy, architecture ownership, iOS lifecycle, testability, performance and release constraints as applicable.
/speckit-tasks Break Phase 06 into dependency-ordered tasks with specific files, tests, integration acceptance criteria, commit boundaries and review checkpoints.
/speckit-analyze Validate Phase 06 spec/plan/tasks consistency, remove speculative dependencies, identify missing tests, and stop if blockers remain.
/speckit-implement Execute only approved Phase 06 tasks in small groups. For each group implement tests first where sensible, run available build/validation, report changed files and results; do not modify VisualCore without an approved upstream task.
/speckit-converge Compare Phase 06 implementation with requirements and tests, append any unresolved tasks, and produce an evidence-based completion report.
```

**Stop point:** Review the diff, execute the phase-specific tests, and commit only when the phase meets its stated acceptance. In particular, absence of a working VisualCore host is a blocker, not permission to create a second backend.

## 10. Bounded Claude execution and Git workflow

**Terminal:**
```bash
git status --short
git diff --check
git diff --stat
git add -A
git commit -m "feat: complete reviewed implementation phase"
git log -3 --oneline
```

**Claude Code chat, at every task boundary:**
```text
Inspect the active Spec Kit tasks file. Implement only the next smallest dependency-complete task group. Before editing, list intended files, known VisualCore API contracts, test commands, and rollback steps. After editing, run tests and report actual results; do not claim device validation without device logs. Stop for review after this group.
```

Do not ask Claude to run all seven phases unattended. Spec Kit artifacts may expose architecture errors or rights/permission issues that materially change the following work. The Git baseline is reviewed per phase; commit evidence and tests in the application repository, and upstream patches separately.

## 11. Domain, renderer and UI verification matrix

| Layer | App-specific test | Evidence / gate |
|---|---|---|
| Pure domain model | Two-body elastic collision approximates expected momentum within solver tolerance | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Pure domain model | Resting stack remains bounded over long runs | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Mass zero is treated as static and never divided by zero | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Spring energy test has known bounded behavior | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Device or end-to-end | Identical initial state and event stream reproduce deterministic CPU results | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Shared render lifecycle | Repeated renderer create, resize, background, resume, context recovery, release | Device log with no stale EGL/GL handles or persistent GPU memory growth |
| App UI and accessibility | First-session flow, disabled states, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver fallback | UI test + human review on representative iPhone and iPad |
| VisualCore regression | If VisualCore changes, ProjectM remains functional at pinned submodule commit | Existing ProjectM build/smoke log; any difference reviewed |

### Implementation-level fixtures
- Fixture 1: Two-body elastic collision approximates expected momentum within solver tolerance.
- Fixture 2: Resting stack remains bounded over long runs.
- Fixture 3: Mass zero is treated as static and never divided by zero.
- Fixture 4: Spring energy test has known bounded behavior.
- Fixture 5: Identical initial state and event stream reproduce deterministic CPU results.

### Simulator and device separation
- CI/simulator: test domain math, model migration, document round trips, permission-denied paths, basic UI and reproducible app builds.
- Physical iPhone/iPad: validate ANGLE Metal path, shader compilation, context loss, high-refresh/low-refresh behavior, thermals, memory, inputs and real audio/device sensor routes if relevant.
- When tests depend on audio, sensors or input permissions, use synthetic fixtures in CI; do not silently substitute test signals for production sources.
- Store exact Xcode, iOS, device, VisualCore revision, ProjectM submodule revision, preset and test duration with performance reports.

## 12. Profiling plan, budgets and graceful fallback

Before specifying absolute fps, startup or memory targets, measure a baseline on the reference app and at least one representative device. Decide thresholds in a separate acceptance ADR; do not publish invented benchmark numbers.

- Measure CPU solver time separately from GPU draw time.
- Maintain maximum active-body budget and optional sleep detection.
- Reduced-quality mode lowers draw complexity without changing simulation laws.

**Telemetry only as local diagnostics by default:** record per-pass timing if genuinely supported, present interval, app-side CPU duration, memory and resource counts, scene configuration, chosen quality tier and build IDs. Make collection opt-in if data ever leaves the device. Never label CPU timings as GPU timings.

**Fallback policy:** keep the app usable when expensive shader passes fail or a device is below target capability: reduce resolution/passes, use a simpler scene, preserve user state, and display a recoverable explanation. When no VisualCore render host exists, ship a native UI placeholder only for internal integration testing—not a misleading App Store release.

## 13. Risks, privacy, science/platform constraints and licenses

### App-specific risk register
1. **Risk 1:** Numerical instability from large dt or stiff springs—fixed substeps and parameter caps. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
2. **Risk 2:** Users may assume engineering accuracy—document educational model and units. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
3. **Risk 3:** Object count may grow without limit—enforce scene budget. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.

### Cross-cutting obligations
- No private iOS APIs, undocumented system-level audio interception, automatic wallpaper changes or unsupported GPU access; test any requested platform capability against current public documentation.
- Apply least-privilege permission prompts, with useful demo/offline behavior for denied permissions. Document Photos, Files, microphone or audio rights only where that app actually needs them.
- Maintain licenses for ANGLE, VisualCore, ProjectM reference code and all bundled shaders, meshes, textures, fonts, datasets, sound and educational copy. Do not assume upstream assets may be redistributed.
- Use clear scientific/educational caveats wherever simulations or graphics are illustrative. Do not market a toy visualization as an instrument, diagnostic tool or accurate predictive model.
- Validate imported data formats, sizes, paths and schema versions; avoid executing untrusted user code except in the specifically constrained Shader Studio design.

### Content and App Store review checklist
- Document why each permission is necessary and the exact UI path requesting it.
- Provide privacy policy and required app data disclosures based on actual telemetry/storage behavior, not sample text.
- Check all media and code redistribution rights, attribution and trademark rules before the storefront submission.
- Keep claims in marketing and screenshots aligned to implemented working features and measured/attributed facts.

## 14. Xcode project, build, and CI commands

After selecting XcodeGen and writing a real `project.yml` during Phase 0/1, these are executable examples **from this app repo**. Scheme and target names must be confirmed with `xcodebuild -list`; do not assume VisualCore has a particular SPM product name.

```bash
# Use XcodeGen only if project.yml was adopted and reviewed
xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -list -project PhysicsPlayground.xcodeproj
xcodebuild -project PhysicsPlayground.xcodeproj -scheme PhysicsPlayground -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
xcrun simctl list devices available
SIMULATOR_UDID="$(python3 scripts/select_simulator.py)"
test -n "$SIMULATOR_UDID" || { echo "No available simulator"; exit 1; }
xcodebuild -project PhysicsPlayground.xcodeproj -scheme PhysicsPlayground -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIMULATOR_UDID" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test
python3 scripts/check_repo.py
```

If the repo uses an `.xcworkspace`, SwiftPM-generated project or a different scheme, inspect it and replace these paths; the test commands above do not constitute successful execution here. Build/sign/archive and test native ANGLE/Metal rendering on macOS with Xcode and a physical device.

### Minimal Python repository audit script

Create `scripts/check_repo.py` during the first phase. It should verify presence of essential architecture documents and app-owned shaders, then print the pinned VisualCore version using an actual resolved dependency file. Do not automatically download code or modify an upstream checkout.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import sys
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
required = ["CLAUDE.md", "docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md"]
missing = [name for name in required if not (root / name).is_file()]
for path in missing:
    print(f"MISSING: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
if missing:
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("Repository guidance and integration contract are present")
```

### Portable Python 3 simulator selection helper

Save as `scripts/select_simulator.py`; it reads `xcrun simctl` JSON and chooses a booted iOS simulator first, otherwise an available iPhone simulator. This helper does not create or boot a device; select/boot one manually if no compatible runtime is installed.

```python
import json
import subprocess
import sys
output = subprocess.check_output(
    ["xcrun", "simctl", "list", "devices", "available", "-j"], text=True)
data = json.loads(output)
devices = [device for runtime, group in data.get("devices", {}).items()
           if "iOS" in runtime for device in group
           if device.get("isAvailable", True) and "iPhone" in device.get("name", "")]
device = next((d for d in devices if d.get("state") == "Booted"),
              devices[0] if devices else None)
if device is None:
    sys.exit("No available iPhone simulator. Check Xcode runtimes.")
print(device["udid"])
```

### Minimal XcodeGen target layout

For a fresh repo, an initial `project.yml` can be generated with the following app-only starter; replace deployment target and bundle ID with validated project values, then add local package products only after the VisualCore audit.

```yaml
name: PhysicsPlayground
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.example.visualcore
targets:
  PhysicsPlayground:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    deploymentTarget: "17.0"   # proposal, verify supported OS
    sources:
      - Apps/PhysicsPlayground
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.visualcore.physics-playground
```

Install XcodeGen through its official distribution if not already available, verify `xcodegen --version`, and run `xcodegen generate` only after this file and target source exist. Avoid storing unreviewed private package tokens in `project.yml` or CI.

### Suggested macOS GitHub Actions job (create after actual build validation)

```yaml
name: iOS CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Verify Python and repository artifacts
        run: python3 scripts/check_repo.py
      - name: Inspect Xcode and app schemes
        run: xcodebuild -list -project PhysicsPlayground.xcodeproj
      - name: Build simulator target
        run: xcodebuild -project PhysicsPlayground.xcodeproj -scheme PhysicsPlayground -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Pin CI action revisions and the Xcode version according to your organization’s supply-chain rules; add simulator unit tests and any authenticated VisualCore package fetch only after configuration is proven to work. CI on macOS does not substitute for physical GPU regression testing.

## 15. Acceptance criteria and definition of done

A first-release candidate is acceptable only when **all** of the following can be demonstrated:

- [ ] MVP-01: 2D circles and boxes with rigid-body collision.
- [ ] MVP-02: Constant gravity, springs and drag forces.
- [ ] MVP-03: Object spawn, grab, pin and delete gestures.
- [ ] MVP-04: Simulation pause/single step, time scale and reset.
- [ ] MVP-05: Presets for pendulum, spring chain and stacked objects.
- [ ] MVP-06: Optional velocity/force vector overlays and measured state panel.
- [ ] Standalone app uses public audited VisualCore APIs and shared ANGLE/Metal path, not ProjectM-specific engine internals.
- [ ] Render-state serializations are versioned, validated, and safe after background/resume and renderer reset.
- [ ] Native UI is usable with accessibility features; reduced motion and quality controls behave as stated.
- [ ] Domain and integration test cases in §11 pass; unresolved errors are documented, not marked passing.
- [ ] At least one physical device run with recorded build/OS/device metadata validates actual GPU behavior.
- [ ] No unsupported privacy, scientific or platform capability claims remain in the product UI or listing.
- [ ] Bundled third-party code, shaders, assets, educational facts and sounds have reviewed license/source records.
- [ ] Build from a clean macOS checkout succeeds and the final PR contains exact verification commands and results.
- [ ] Any VisualCore changes have their own upstream PR plus before/after ProjectM reference regression evidence.

## 16. Ordered next actions

1. Create a new `PhysicsPlayground` app repo and initialize the Claude/Spec Kit Python variant (commands in §7).
2. Perform read-only VisualCore package/render-host inspection; resolve actual public APIs and upstream gaps.
3. Save the constitution and app-specific design decisions in reviewed repository artifacts.
4. Run Phase 00 through all eight quality gates; complete any upstream VisualCore feature as a separate, reviewed change.
5. Implement Phase 01 physics model/units and deterministic tests as the smallest testable vertical slice.
6. Continue the remaining phases one by one; compare every release claim against the acceptance matrix.
7. Archive evidence from physical device validation and review the release privacy/license checklist.
