# Tiny Worlds
## iOS application architecture and Spec Kit + Claude Code implementation manual

**Concept #12 of 25** | **Category:** Games and interactive experiences | **Proposed app/repository target:** `TinyWorlds`
**Planning status:** proposed implementation guide; not proof of an existing application or released VisualCore package. **Source:** `AppsBrainstorm.md` catalog item 12; `README.md` VisualCore architecture and Spec Kit strategy.
**Rendering invariant:** reuse the existing ProjectM-proven OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal infrastructure exposed by VisualCore. Never create a duplicate EGL/ANGLE backend or link ProjectM engine internals into this independent app.

---

## 1. Executive summary and source traceability

A curated gallery of miniature procedural environments with orbit navigation and gentle customization.

### Original brainstorm concept

> A collection of miniature procedural worlds users can explore, customize, and populate with objects.

**VisualCore capabilities listed in the brainstorm:**
- 3D scenes
- Camera and navigation
- Procedural meshes
- Lighting
- Materials and assets

**Original product opportunity:** A creative exploration app with collectible environments and customization.

**Recommended product hypothesis:** A carefully scoped, offline-capable first release can demonstrate a distinct graphics workload and validate reusable VisualCore APIs. Test this hypothesis with a functioning vertical slice before expanding content or monetization.

## 2. Product contract and scope

### Primary audiences
- Players who enjoy miniature dioramas
- Creators arranging small worlds
- Users seeking low-pressure exploration

### End-to-end user journeys
1. **Journey 1:** Open a tiny island with animated scenery.
2. **Journey 2:** Orbit and zoom camera to explore.
3. **Journey 3:** Change terrain seed, place one prop and save the world.

### Version 0.1 feature contract
1. **Feature 01:** Three small world presets: island, asteroid garden and miniature city. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
2. **Feature 02:** Orbit camera with constrained zoom and comfortable control. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
3. **Feature 03:** Seeded terrain/mesh generation with stable boundaries. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
4. **Feature 04:** Prop placement and scene light adjustment. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
5. **Feature 05:** Saved world composition and thumbnails. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
6. **Feature 06:** Dynamic detail tier based on GPU/memory budget. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.

### Explicit non-goals
- Infinite terrain or open-world streaming
- Multiplayer world creation
- Photorealistic GI and full physics gameplay

### Later-stage ideas, not MVP commitments
- Interactive citizens and ambient ecology
- World-to-world transitions
- Sharing signed deterministic world seeds

## 3. UX blueprint

The first launch should reach a meaningful working graphic or educational interaction without requiring an account. Use SwiftUI for navigation, settings, labels and accessibility; host VisualCore rendering in a verified UIView/UIViewRepresentable integration that owns no duplicate GPU lifecycle.

**Proposed screen inventory** (adapt to the app-specific flows above):
| Screen | Responsibility | Concrete behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Home / gallery | Start without setup | Curated Tiny Worlds example, recent scene and explicit entry point |
| Interactive scene | Primary VisualCore rendering surface | Touch and app-state changes mapped into validated domain commands |
| Inspector | Controls and explanations | Show effective parameter values, reset and valid ranges |
| Library / files | Persistence where relevant | Open, duplicate, save, import/export only via permitted system APIs |
| Settings / help | Quality, accessibility, privacy | Explain input permissions, limitations, credits and renderer fallback |

**Interaction design rules:** screen gestures must have a deterministic domain meaning; rendering can interpolate but cannot silently change persisted state. State-affecting controls should be testable independent of the GPU. All critical feedback must remain legible without bloom, color alone, or animation.

### State transitions to implement
```text
uninitialized → loading-assets → ready → active
                                  ↔ paused / backgrounded
                                  ↘ editing / exporting (if supported)
any GPU state → renderer-lost → recover-resources → ready
any document state → validation-error → recoverable-message
```

Do not upload application/scene state to a server by default. If future features introduce accounts, cloud sync or sharing, write a new privacy and threat-model spec before implementation.

## 4. Architecture: VisualCore consumer, not renderer fork

```text
TinyWorlds SwiftUI app (navigation, accessibility, preferences)
    ↓ commands / immutable snapshots
TinyWorldsCore (domain rules, models, persistence schemas, validation)
    ↓ render-state snapshot; never raw SwiftUI bindings
TinyWorldsRendering (scene adapter, shaders, asset IDs, pass descriptions)
    ↓ public APIs discovered in the real VisualCore checkout
VisualCore runtime, shaders, effects, scenes, inputs, diagnostics
    ↓ shared EGL/context/render host as audited
Existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal implementation
    ↓
iOS device GPU and display
```

**Ownership policy:** The app owns its content, mathematical rules, domain schema, UI and business logic. VisualCore owns generic graphics infrastructure. `Coastrnaut/projectm-ios` remains VisualCore's pinned reference submodule, not an app dependency. Any VisualCore API needed but not present must be proposed upstream with a test and an API contract; do not stub an imaginary package into production.

### Contracts and threading
- A domain coordinator produces immutable render snapshots or bounded commands; presentation does not mutate simulation truth.
- The VisualCore render host controls the EGL context, resource lifetime, presentation and the required render thread/queue; all GL work obeys that ownership.
- Native SwiftUI overlays remain separate from shader drawing where legibility, hit-testing and VoiceOver need native controls.
- On scene resize, background, memory warning or renderer reset, reallocate GPU resources from versioned CPU state rather than persisting raw GL handles.
- Shaders are treated as bundled, versioned assets unless the specific product explicitly supports user-authored GLSL with additional guards.

### Application-specific components
- **`TinyWorldDocument.swift`**: data storage, schema validation, assets or export; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`TerrainGenerator.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`MeshLODBuilder.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`PropCatalog.swift`**: data storage, schema validation, assets or export; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`WorldEditor.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`OrbitCamera.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`TinyWorldRenderer.swift`**: renderer-facing render orchestration and GPU pass bindings; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.

## 6. Domain model, algorithms and rendering design

### Versioned domain schemas (proposed types)
| Type | Field contract / required invariants |
|---|---|
| `TinyWorld` | `TinyWorld(seed, biomeID, terrainParams, props, lighting, schemaVersion)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `TerrainChunk` | `TerrainChunk(coord, meshLOD, assetVersion)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `WorldProp` | `WorldProp(assetID, transform, variationSeed)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `CameraRig` | `CameraRig(orbitYaw, pitch, distance, focus)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |

Use explicit units and coordinate spaces in type names or documentation. Reject NaN/Inf, invalid counts, truncated files, unreasonable allocations and unsupported versions where applicable. Canonical storage should be pure data; expensive buffers can be reconstructed.

### Algorithm and correctness decisions
1. Use deterministic height/shape noise with reproducible seed and edge-consistent normal generation.
2. Generate bounded geometry at load/edit time, not every frame.
3. Separate visual meshes from coarse selection/picking geometry.
4. Maintain near/far and world unit conventions and avoid camera penetration.

### App-specific render sequence
1. **Stage 1:** Load world descriptor and seed.
2. **Stage 2:** Generate or retrieve terrain meshes, instance props and configure lighting.
3. **Stage 3:** Render geometry depth/opaque then particles/atmosphere.
4. **Stage 4:** Apply color grading and UI overlays before presentation.

### Rendering lifecycle and frame budget
- Create resources only after VisualCore signals a valid owning EGL context; release/recreate on context loss and size changes.
- Separate fixed-step simulation, event handling, visual animation time and wall time when the product uses more than one.
- Treat device tier as policy data: resolution scale, effect counts, iterations and object count may change; domain correctness and user state may not.
- Validate framebuffer completeness, shader compile/link results, texture format support and GPU resource handles before presenting a frame.
- Record frame pacing, app-owned CPU time, allocation counts and renderer recovery on a real device before selecting release targets.

### Required capability audit against VisualCore
- **3D scenes** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Camera and navigation** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Procedural meshes** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Lighting** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Materials and assets** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.

> **Domain-specific engineering rule:** Tiny Worlds is the strongest reason to evaluate VisualCore 3D scenes and assets after an audited graphics feature baseline exists.

```bash
specify version
specify init --help
specify init --here --integration claude --script py
specify check
git status --short
claude
```

Initialize Spec Kit **once** in a newly created repository. In a non-empty existing repo, commit/backup first and inspect `specify init --help`; `--force` may merge/overwrite managed files and must not be run blindly. Never run Spec Kit initialization inside the VisualCore or ProjectM submodule from an app repo.

**Current Claude Code integration:** Spec Kit creates `.claude/skills/speckit-<command>/SKILL.md`; invoke skills in Claude chat using **hyphens**, e.g. `/speckit-specify`, not the dotted spelling used in some generic documentation. Confirm actual skills with `find .claude/skills -name SKILL.md` and Claude `/help` because installed versions can differ. See official [Claude integration](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html).

**Terminal — verify a local VisualCore checkout without assuming package products:**
```bash
test -d ../VisualCore || { echo "Clone or locate the VisualCore repository beside this app first"; exit 1; }
git -C ../VisualCore status --short
find ../VisualCore -name Package.swift -not -path "*/.build/*" -print
git -C ../VisualCore submodule status
```

If `../VisualCore` does not yet provide a consumer package, create an upstream integration feature and stop at a no-op host skeleton. Do not invent `VisualCoreRenderer` product names or fake ANGLE integration code.

```markdown
# Tiny Worlds — Claude Code Engineering Rules

- Product goal: A curated gallery of miniature procedural environments with orbit navigation and gentle customization.

- VisualCore owns the graphics lifecycle; never create an independent ANGLE/EGL initialization path.
```

## 10. Bounded Claude execution and Git workflow

**Terminal:**
```bash
git status --short
git diff --check
git diff --stat
git add -A
git commit -m "feat: complete reviewed implementation phase"
git log -3 --oneline
```

**Claude Code chat, at every task boundary:**
```text
Inspect the active Spec Kit tasks file. Implement only the next smallest dependency-complete task group. Before editing, list intended files, known VisualCore API contracts, test commands, and rollback steps. After editing, run tests and report actual results; do not claim device validation without device logs. Stop for review after this group.
```

Do not ask Claude to run all seven phases unattended. Spec Kit artifacts may expose architecture errors or rights/permission issues that materially change the following work. The Git baseline is reviewed per phase; commit evidence and tests in the application repository, and upstream patches separately.

## 11. Domain, renderer and UI verification matrix

| Layer | App-specific test | Evidence / gate |
|---|---|---|
| Pure domain model | Same seed and settings yield identical mesh hashes in reference generator | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Pure domain model | All LOD indices remain in bounds | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Placed props persist at exact transforms | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Orbit camera respects limits, no clipping through terrain | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Device or end-to-end | World load/unload cycles do not retain stale GPU objects | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Shared render lifecycle | Repeated renderer create, resize, background, resume, context recovery, release | Device log with no stale EGL/GL handles or persistent GPU memory growth |
| App UI and accessibility | First-session flow, disabled states, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver fallback | UI test + human review on representative iPhone and iPad |
| VisualCore regression | If VisualCore changes, ProjectM remains functional at pinned submodule commit | Existing ProjectM build/smoke log; any difference reviewed |

### Implementation-level fixtures
- Fixture 1: Same seed and settings yield identical mesh hashes in reference generator.
- Fixture 2: All LOD indices remain in bounds.
- Fixture 3: Placed props persist at exact transforms.
- Fixture 4: Orbit camera respects limits, no clipping through terrain.
- Fixture 5: World load/unload cycles do not retain stale GPU objects.

### Simulator and device separation
- CI/simulator: test domain math, model migration, document round trips, permission-denied paths, basic UI and reproducible app builds.
- Physical iPhone/iPad: validate ANGLE Metal path, shader compilation, context loss, high-refresh/low-refresh behavior, thermals, memory, inputs and real audio/device sensor routes if relevant.
- When tests depend on audio, sensors or input permissions, use synthetic fixtures in CI; do not silently substitute test signals for production sources.
- Store exact Xcode, iOS, device, VisualCore revision, ProjectM submodule revision, preset and test duration with performance reports.

## 12. Profiling plan, budgets and graceful fallback

Before specifying absolute fps, startup or memory targets, measure a baseline on the reference app and at least one representative device. Decide thresholds in a separate acceptance ADR; do not publish invented benchmark numbers.

- Profile scene load, mesh generation time, draw count, overdraw and peak memory.
- Limit visible chunks, use baked/simple lighting on low tiers.
- Keep camera responsive during geometry rebuilds.

**Telemetry only as local diagnostics by default:** record per-pass timing if genuinely supported, present interval, app-side CPU duration, memory and resource counts, scene configuration, chosen quality tier and build IDs. Make collection opt-in if data ever leaves the device. Never label CPU timings as GPU timings.

**Fallback policy:** keep the app usable when expensive shader passes fail or a device is below target capability: reduce resolution/passes, use a simpler scene, preserve user state, and display a recoverable explanation. When no VisualCore render host exists, ship a native UI placeholder only for internal integration testing—not a misleading App Store release.

## 13. Risks, privacy, science/platform constraints and licenses

### App-specific risk register
1. **Risk 1:** Procedural meshes may spike startup—async generation and loading indicator. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
2. **Risk 2:** Asset size can dominate app download—use atlases and instancing. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
3. **Risk 3:** World editing conflicts with generation—commit snapshots atomically. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.

### Cross-cutting obligations
- No private iOS APIs, undocumented system-level audio interception, automatic wallpaper changes or unsupported GPU access; test any requested platform capability against current public documentation.
- Apply least-privilege permission prompts, with useful demo/offline behavior for denied permissions. Document Photos, Files, microphone or audio rights only where that app actually needs them.
- Maintain licenses for ANGLE, VisualCore, ProjectM reference code and all bundled shaders, meshes, textures, fonts, datasets, sound and educational copy. Do not assume upstream assets may be redistributed.
- Use clear scientific/educational caveats wherever simulations or graphics are illustrative. Do not market a toy visualization as an instrument, diagnostic tool or accurate predictive model.
- Validate imported data formats, sizes, paths and schema versions; avoid executing untrusted user code except in the specifically constrained Shader Studio design.

### Content and App Store review checklist
- Document why each permission is necessary and the exact UI path requesting it.
- Provide privacy policy and required app data disclosures based on actual telemetry/storage behavior, not sample text.
- Check all media and code redistribution rights, attribution and trademark rules before the storefront submission.
- Keep claims in marketing and screenshots aligned to implemented working features and measured/attributed facts.

## 14. Xcode project, build, and CI commands

After selecting XcodeGen and writing a real `project.yml` during Phase 0/1, these are executable examples **from this app repo**. Scheme and target names must be confirmed with `xcodebuild -list`; do not assume VisualCore has a particular SPM product name.

```bash
# Use XcodeGen only if project.yml was adopted and reviewed
xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -list -project TinyWorlds.xcodeproj
xcodebuild -project TinyWorlds.xcodeproj -scheme TinyWorlds -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
xcrun simctl list devices available
SIMULATOR_UDID="$(python3 scripts/select_simulator.py)"
test -n "$SIMULATOR_UDID" || { echo "No available simulator"; exit 1; }
xcodebuild -project TinyWorlds.xcodeproj -scheme TinyWorlds -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIMULATOR_UDID" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test
python3 scripts/check_repo.py
```

If the repo uses an `.xcworkspace`, SwiftPM-generated project or a different scheme, inspect it and replace these paths; the test commands above do not constitute successful execution here. Build/sign/archive and test native ANGLE/Metal rendering on macOS with Xcode and a physical device.

### Minimal Python repository audit script

Create `scripts/check_repo.py` during the first phase. It should verify presence of essential architecture documents and app-owned shaders, then print the pinned VisualCore version using an actual resolved dependency file. Do not automatically download code or modify an upstream checkout.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import sys
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
required = ["CLAUDE.md", "docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md"]
missing = [name for name in required if not (root / name).is_file()]
for path in missing:
    print(f"MISSING: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
if missing:
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("Repository guidance and integration contract are present")
```

### Portable Python 3 simulator selection helper

Save as `scripts/select_simulator.py`; it reads `xcrun simctl` JSON and chooses a booted iOS simulator first, otherwise an available iPhone simulator. This helper does not create or boot a device; select/boot one manually if no compatible runtime is installed.

```python
import json
import subprocess
import sys
output = subprocess.check_output(
    ["xcrun", "simctl", "list", "devices", "available", "-j"], text=True)
data = json.loads(output)
devices = [device for runtime, group in data.get("devices", {}).items()
           if "iOS" in runtime for device in group
           if device.get("isAvailable", True) and "iPhone" in device.get("name", "")]
device = next((d for d in devices if d.get("state") == "Booted"),
              devices[0] if devices else None)
if device is None:
    sys.exit("No available iPhone simulator. Check Xcode runtimes.")
print(device["udid"])
```

### Minimal XcodeGen target layout

For a fresh repo, an initial `project.yml` can be generated with the following app-only starter; replace deployment target and bundle ID with validated project values, then add local package products only after the VisualCore audit.

```yaml
name: TinyWorlds
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.example.visualcore
targets:
  TinyWorlds:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    deploymentTarget: "17.0"   # proposal, verify supported OS
    sources:
      - Apps/TinyWorlds
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.visualcore.tiny-worlds
```

Install XcodeGen through its official distribution if not already available, verify `xcodegen --version`, and run `xcodegen generate` only after this file and target source exist. Avoid storing unreviewed private package tokens in `project.yml` or CI.

### Suggested macOS GitHub Actions job (create after actual build validation)

```yaml
name: iOS CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Verify Python and repository artifacts
        run: python3 scripts/check_repo.py
      - name: Inspect Xcode and app schemes
        run: xcodebuild -list -project TinyWorlds.xcodeproj
      - name: Build simulator target
        run: xcodebuild -project TinyWorlds.xcodeproj -scheme TinyWorlds -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Pin CI action revisions and the Xcode version according to your organization’s supply-chain rules; add simulator unit tests and any authenticated VisualCore package fetch only after configuration is proven to work. CI on macOS does not substitute for physical GPU regression testing.

## 15. Acceptance criteria and definition of done

A first-release candidate is acceptable only when **all** of the following can be demonstrated:

- [ ] MVP-01: Three small world presets: island, asteroid garden and miniature city.
- [ ] MVP-02: Orbit camera with constrained zoom and comfortable control.
- [ ] MVP-03: Seeded terrain/mesh generation with stable boundaries.
- [ ] MVP-04: Prop placement and scene light adjustment.
- [ ] MVP-05: Saved world composition and thumbnails.
- [ ] MVP-06: Dynamic detail tier based on GPU/memory budget.
- [ ] Standalone app uses public audited VisualCore APIs and shared ANGLE/Metal path, not ProjectM-specific engine internals.
- [ ] Render-state serializations are versioned, validated, and safe after background/resume and renderer reset.
- [ ] Native UI is usable with accessibility features; reduced motion and quality controls behave as stated.
- [ ] Domain and integration test cases in §11 pass; unresolved errors are documented, not marked passing.
- [ ] At least one physical device run with recorded build/OS/device metadata validates actual GPU behavior.
- [ ] No unsupported privacy, scientific or platform capability claims remain in the product UI or listing.
- [ ] Bundled third-party code, shaders, assets, educational facts and sounds have reviewed license/source records.
- [ ] Build from a clean macOS checkout succeeds and the final PR contains exact verification commands and results.
- [ ] Any VisualCore changes have their own upstream PR plus before/after ProjectM reference regression evidence.

# Light Maze
## iOS application architecture and Spec Kit + Claude Code implementation manual

**Concept #13 of 25** | **Category:** Games and interactive experiences | **Proposed app/repository target:** `LightMaze`
**Planning status:** proposed implementation guide; not proof of an existing application or released VisualCore package. **Source:** `AppsBrainstorm.md` catalog item 13; `README.md` VisualCore architecture and Spec Kit strategy.
**Rendering invariant:** reuse the existing ProjectM-proven OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal infrastructure exposed by VisualCore. Never create a duplicate EGL/ANGLE backend or link ProjectM engine internals into this independent app.

---

## 1. Executive summary and source traceability

A precise, tactile light-reflection puzzle game with visually rich beams and deterministic rules.

### Original brainstorm concept

> A puzzle game involving beams of light, mirrors, reflections, portals, and dynamic geometric environments.

**VisualCore capabilities listed in the brainstorm:**
- Render targets
- Shaders
- Geometry and transformations
- Touch controls
- Compositing and visual feedback

**Original product opportunity:** A visually distinctive puzzle game with increasingly complex mechanics.

**Recommended product hypothesis:** A carefully scoped, offline-capable first release can demonstrate a distinct graphics workload and validate reusable VisualCore APIs. Test this hypothesis with a functioning vertical slice before expanding content or monetization.

## 2. Product contract and scope

### Primary audiences
- Puzzle fans
- Children learning reflection geometry
- Players wanting short, meaningful sessions

### End-to-end user journeys
1. **Journey 1:** Rotate a mirror to redirect a beam into target sensor.
2. **Journey 2:** Complete three introductory levels.
3. **Journey 3:** Restart or request hint, then progress through a small curated set.

### Version 0.1 feature contract
1. **Feature 01:** At least 20 handcrafted levels with emitter, wall, mirror, target and optional prism tile. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
2. **Feature 02:** Drag/rotate interactions snapped to puzzle grid. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
3. **Feature 03:** Deterministic ray propagation with reflection and finite bounce cap. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
4. **Feature 04:** Level select, unlock progression, undo/restart and success feedback. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
5. **Feature 05:** Visual glow and color cues without hiding beam connectivity. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
6. **Feature 06:** Built-in solvability test for level data. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.

### Explicit non-goals
- Photorealistic optics with refraction physics
- Unvalidated user-generated level sharing
- Endless procedural level generation

### Later-stage ideas, not MVP commitments
- Additional beam colors, splitters and portals
- Level editor and local puzzle packs
- Optional puzzle replay sharing

## 3. UX blueprint

The first launch should reach a meaningful working graphic or educational interaction without requiring an account. Use SwiftUI for navigation, settings, labels and accessibility; host VisualCore rendering in a verified UIView/UIViewRepresentable integration that owns no duplicate GPU lifecycle.

**Proposed screen inventory** (adapt to the app-specific flows above):
| Screen | Responsibility | Concrete behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Home / gallery | Start without setup | Curated Light Maze example, recent scene and explicit entry point |
| Interactive scene | Primary VisualCore rendering surface | Touch and app-state changes mapped into validated domain commands |
| Inspector | Controls and explanations | Show effective parameter values, reset and valid ranges |
| Library / files | Persistence where relevant | Open, duplicate, save, import/export only via permitted system APIs |
| Settings / help | Quality, accessibility, privacy | Explain input permissions, limitations, credits and renderer fallback |

**Interaction design rules:** screen gestures must have a deterministic domain meaning; rendering can interpolate but cannot silently change persisted state. State-affecting controls should be testable independent of the GPU. All critical feedback must remain legible without bloom, color alone, or animation.

### State transitions to implement
```text
uninitialized → loading-assets → ready → active
                                  ↔ paused / backgrounded
                                  ↘ editing / exporting (if supported)
any GPU state → renderer-lost → recover-resources → ready
any document state → validation-error → recoverable-message
```

Do not upload application/scene state to a server by default. If future features introduce accounts, cloud sync or sharing, write a new privacy and threat-model spec before implementation.

## 4. Architecture: VisualCore consumer, not renderer fork

```text
LightMaze SwiftUI app (navigation, accessibility, preferences)
    ↓ commands / immutable snapshots
LightMazeCore (domain rules, models, persistence schemas, validation)
    ↓ render-state snapshot; never raw SwiftUI bindings
LightMazeRendering (scene adapter, shaders, asset IDs, pass descriptions)
    ↓ public APIs discovered in the real VisualCore checkout
VisualCore runtime, shaders, effects, scenes, inputs, diagnostics
    ↓ shared EGL/context/render host as audited
Existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal implementation
    ↓
iOS device GPU and display
```

**Ownership policy:** The app owns its content, mathematical rules, domain schema, UI and business logic. VisualCore owns generic graphics infrastructure. `Coastrnaut/projectm-ios` remains VisualCore's pinned reference submodule, not an app dependency. Any VisualCore API needed but not present must be proposed upstream with a test and an API contract; do not stub an imaginary package into production.

### Contracts and threading
- A domain coordinator produces immutable render snapshots or bounded commands; presentation does not mutate simulation truth.
- The VisualCore render host controls the EGL context, resource lifetime, presentation and the required render thread/queue; all GL work obeys that ownership.
- Native SwiftUI overlays remain separate from shader drawing where legibility, hit-testing and VoiceOver need native controls.
- On scene resize, background, memory warning or renderer reset, reallocate GPU resources from versioned CPU state rather than persisting raw GL handles.
- Shaders are treated as bundled, versioned assets unless the specific product explicitly supports user-authored GLSL with additional guards.

### Application-specific components
- **`PuzzleGrid.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`RayTracer2D.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`OpticalRules.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`LevelValidator.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`ProgressStore.swift`**: data storage, schema validation, assets or export; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`LightMazeRenderer.swift`**: renderer-facing render orchestration and GPU pass bindings; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.

### File creation policy

- Store data fixtures in JSON/CSV where appropriate, with explicit schema and license metadata; do not serialize GPU buffer addresses or EGL objects.
- Keep all feature specs under `specs/` created by Spec Kit; allow its installed release to determine feature numbering and active feature selection.

## 6. Domain model, algorithms and rendering design

### Versioned domain schemas (proposed types)
| Type | Field contract / required invariants |
|---|---|
| `PuzzleGrid` | `PuzzleGrid(width, height, cellSize, tiles, schemaVersion)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `OpticalElement` | `OpticalElement(type, cell, orientation, wavelengthMode, active)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `BeamSegment` | `BeamSegment(start, end, colorChannel, sourceID, bounceIndex)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `PuzzleProgress` | `PuzzleProgress(levelID, completed, bestMoves)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |

Use explicit units and coordinate spaces in type names or documentation. Reject NaN/Inf, invalid counts, truncated files, unreasonable allocations and unsupported versions where applicable. Canonical storage should be pure data; expensive buffers can be reconstructed.

### Algorithm and correctness decisions
1. Compute ray/segment intersection on CPU from exact grid geometry; treat shader beam rendering as presentation only.
2. Avoid self-intersection with explicit epsilon and last-hit tracking; cap bounces and detect cycles.
3. Propagate color channels through splitters only when authored in rules; start with monochrome in Phase 1.
4. Use solver/replay tests to verify solutions and guard against unintended shortcuts.

### App-specific render sequence
1. **Stage 1:** Apply user mirror edit to immutable grid snapshot.
2. **Stage 2:** Recompute beam tree and sensor states on CPU.
3. **Stage 3:** Generate glowing beam quads from exact segments, render mirrors, walls and targets.
4. **Stage 4:** Animate solved feedback without changing logical results.

### Rendering lifecycle and frame budget
- Create resources only after VisualCore signals a valid owning EGL context; release/recreate on context loss and size changes.
- Separate fixed-step simulation, event handling, visual animation time and wall time when the product uses more than one.
- Treat device tier as policy data: resolution scale, effect counts, iterations and object count may change; domain correctness and user state may not.
- Validate framebuffer completeness, shader compile/link results, texture format support and GPU resource handles before presenting a frame.
- Record frame pacing, app-owned CPU time, allocation counts and renderer recovery on a real device before selecting release targets.

### Required capability audit against VisualCore
- **Render targets** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Shaders** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Geometry and transformations** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Touch controls** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Compositing and visual feedback** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.

> **Domain-specific engineering rule:** Formal puzzle rules and level validation matter more than animation features. A shader must never decide if the puzzle is solved.

## 7. Local environment and reproducible bootstrap

**Prerequisites:** macOS and Xcode for iOS build, signing, Simulator and physical-device tests; Git, Python 3, `uv`, and Claude Code CLI. Windows can prepare specifications and source but cannot validate the iOS rendering path without a macOS builder. Follow current vendor instructions for installation; verify tool versions rather than assuming they exist.

**Terminal on macOS — commands to create this app repository:**
```bash
mkdir LightMaze && cd LightMaze
git init -b main
git --version
python3 --version
uv --version
claude --version
uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git
specify version
specify init --help
specify init --here --integration claude --script py
specify check
git status --short
claude
```

Initialize Spec Kit **once** in a newly created repository. In a non-empty existing repo, commit/backup first and inspect `specify init --help`; `--force` may merge/overwrite managed files and must not be run blindly. Never run Spec Kit initialization inside the VisualCore or ProjectM submodule from an app repo.

**Current Claude Code integration:** Spec Kit creates `.claude/skills/speckit-<command>/SKILL.md`; invoke skills in Claude chat using **hyphens**, e.g. `/speckit-specify`, not the dotted spelling used in some generic documentation. Confirm actual skills with `find .claude/skills -name SKILL.md` and Claude `/help` because installed versions can differ. See official [Claude integration](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html).

**Terminal — verify a local VisualCore checkout without assuming package products:**
```bash
test -d ../VisualCore || { echo "Clone or locate the VisualCore repository beside this app first"; exit 1; }
git -C ../VisualCore status --short
find ../VisualCore -name Package.swift -not -path "*/.build/*" -print
git -C ../VisualCore submodule status
```

If `../VisualCore` does not yet provide a consumer package, create an upstream integration feature and stop at a no-op host skeleton. Do not invent `VisualCoreRenderer` product names or fake ANGLE integration code.

## 9. Implementation phases with **actual Spec Kit / Claude Code commands**

Run the following blocks **inside Claude Code chat**, **not** your shell. Each phase should produce its own `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, tests and reviewable PR; use the actual active feature convention generated by your Spec Kit version. Execute the next phase only after the preceding acceptance checks pass. Slash commands below follow the current Claude skill installation; if your installed integration differs, inspect its generated `.claude/skills/`.

### Phase 00 — Foundation and VisualCore boundary audit

**Deliverable:** Produce read-only repository inventory; map VisualCore package products, EGL host, render thread, shader/resource APIs, Xcode build steps, actual source ownership and baseline ProjectM regression tests. Record open architectural gaps. Do not modify VisualCore or ProjectM.

**Review / acceptance gates:**
- An evidence-backed integration matrix references real files, symbols and package products
- The app can compile an empty SwiftUI shell before custom graphics integration
- A written stop/go decision identifies anything missing upstream

```text
/speckit-specify For Light Maze Phase 00 (Foundation and VisualCore boundary audit): Produce read-only repository inventory; map VisualCore package products, EGL host, render thread, shader/resource APIs, Xcode build steps, actual source ownership and baseline ProjectM regression tests. Record open architectural gaps. Do not modify VisualCore or ProjectM. Capture measurable user stories, edge cases, traceability to the brainstorm and negative requirements.
/speckit-clarify Review this Phase 00 spec for unverified VisualCore APIs, permissions, algorithm semantics, performance assumptions and unsupported iOS behavior. Ask only blocking questions; record decisions in spec artifacts.
/speckit-plan Create the Phase 00 technical plan. Give exact app-owned source paths, dependency direction, lifecycle contracts, data schemas, tests, build commands, migration and rollback; reference only APIs verified by the read-only audit.
/speckit-checklist Generate a Phase 00 checklist covering requirements completeness, privacy, architecture ownership, iOS lifecycle, testability, performance and release constraints as applicable.
/speckit-tasks Break Phase 00 into dependency-ordered tasks with specific files, tests, integration acceptance criteria, commit boundaries and review checkpoints.
/speckit-analyze Validate Phase 00 spec/plan/tasks consistency, remove speculative dependencies, identify missing tests, and stop if blockers remain.
/speckit-implement Execute only approved Phase 00 tasks in small groups. For each group implement tests first where sensible, run available build/validation, report changed files and results; do not modify VisualCore without an approved upstream task.
/speckit-converge Compare Phase 00 implementation with requirements and tests, append any unresolved tasks, and produce an evidence-based completion report.
```

**Stop point:** Review the diff, execute the phase-specific tests, and commit only when the phase meets its stated acceptance. In particular, absence of a working VisualCore host is a blocker, not permission to create a second backend.

## 10. Bounded Claude execution and Git workflow

**Terminal:**
```bash
git status --short
git diff --check
git diff --stat
git add -A
git commit -m "feat: complete reviewed implementation phase"
git log -3 --oneline
```

**Claude Code chat, at every task boundary:**
```text
Inspect the active Spec Kit tasks file. Implement only the next smallest dependency-complete task group. Before editing, list intended files, known VisualCore API contracts, test commands, and rollback steps. After editing, run tests and report actual results; do not claim device validation without device logs. Stop for review after this group.
```

Do not ask Claude to run all seven phases unattended. Spec Kit artifacts may expose architecture errors or rights/permission issues that materially change the following work. The Git baseline is reviewed per phase; commit evidence and tests in the application repository, and upstream patches separately.

## 11. Domain, renderer and UI verification matrix

| Layer | App-specific test | Evidence / gate |
|---|---|---|
| Pure domain model | Incidence angle equals reflection angle within tolerance | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Pure domain model | Repeating mirror loops end at bounded bounce budget | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | All shipping levels have at least one verified solution | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Undo restores exact previous grid and beam state | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Device or end-to-end | Beam visual endpoints match ray solver coordinates | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Shared render lifecycle | Repeated renderer create, resize, background, resume, context recovery, release | Device log with no stale EGL/GL handles or persistent GPU memory growth |
| App UI and accessibility | First-session flow, disabled states, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver fallback | UI test + human review on representative iPhone and iPad |
| VisualCore regression | If VisualCore changes, ProjectM remains functional at pinned submodule commit | Existing ProjectM build/smoke log; any difference reviewed |

### Implementation-level fixtures
- Fixture 1: Incidence angle equals reflection angle within tolerance.
- Fixture 2: Repeating mirror loops end at bounded bounce budget.
- Fixture 3: All shipping levels have at least one verified solution.
- Fixture 4: Undo restores exact previous grid and beam state.
- Fixture 5: Beam visual endpoints match ray solver coordinates.

### Simulator and device separation
- CI/simulator: test domain math, model migration, document round trips, permission-denied paths, basic UI and reproducible app builds.
- Physical iPhone/iPad: validate ANGLE Metal path, shader compilation, context loss, high-refresh/low-refresh behavior, thermals, memory, inputs and real audio/device sensor routes if relevant.
- When tests depend on audio, sensors or input permissions, use synthetic fixtures in CI; do not silently substitute test signals for production sources.
- Store exact Xcode, iOS, device, VisualCore revision, ProjectM submodule revision, preset and test duration with performance reports.

## 12. Profiling plan, budgets and graceful fallback

Before specifying absolute fps, startup or memory targets, measure a baseline on the reference app and at least one representative device. Decide thresholds in a separate acceptance ADR; do not publish invented benchmark numbers.

- Low scene complexity; optimize latency and deterministic state changes rather than throughput.
- Keep bloom capped so color-coded logic stays legible.
- Use battery-friendly idle rendering when puzzle state is unchanged.

**Telemetry only as local diagnostics by default:** record per-pass timing if genuinely supported, present interval, app-side CPU duration, memory and resource counts, scene configuration, chosen quality tier and build IDs. Make collection opt-in if data ever leaves the device. Never label CPU timings as GPU timings.

**Fallback policy:** keep the app usable when expensive shader passes fail or a device is below target capability: reduce resolution/passes, use a simpler scene, preserve user state, and display a recoverable explanation. When no VisualCore render host exists, ship a native UI placeholder only for internal integration testing—not a misleading App Store release.

## 13. Risks, privacy, science/platform constraints and licenses

### App-specific risk register
1. **Risk 1:** Visual beams can diverge from logical paths—single source of truth in CPU tracer. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
2. **Risk 2:** Puzzle content is expensive to design—ship small validated set. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
3. **Risk 3:** Touch rotation imprecision—snap to grid and provide large tap targets. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.

### Cross-cutting obligations
- No private iOS APIs, undocumented system-level audio interception, automatic wallpaper changes or unsupported GPU access; test any requested platform capability against current public documentation.
- Apply least-privilege permission prompts, with useful demo/offline behavior for denied permissions. Document Photos, Files, microphone or audio rights only where that app actually needs them.
- Maintain licenses for ANGLE, VisualCore, ProjectM reference code and all bundled shaders, meshes, textures, fonts, datasets, sound and educational copy. Do not assume upstream assets may be redistributed.
- Use clear scientific/educational caveats wherever simulations or graphics are illustrative. Do not market a toy visualization as an instrument, diagnostic tool or accurate predictive model.
- Validate imported data formats, sizes, paths and schema versions; avoid executing untrusted user code except in the specifically constrained Shader Studio design.

### Content and App Store review checklist
- Document why each permission is necessary and the exact UI path requesting it.
- Provide privacy policy and required app data disclosures based on actual telemetry/storage behavior, not sample text.
- Check all media and code redistribution rights, attribution and trademark rules before the storefront submission.
- Keep claims in marketing and screenshots aligned to implemented working features and measured/attributed facts.

## 14. Xcode project, build, and CI commands

After selecting XcodeGen and writing a real `project.yml` during Phase 0/1, these are executable examples **from this app repo**. Scheme and target names must be confirmed with `xcodebuild -list`; do not assume VisualCore has a particular SPM product name.

```bash
# Use XcodeGen only if project.yml was adopted and reviewed
xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -list -project LightMaze.xcodeproj
xcodebuild -project LightMaze.xcodeproj -scheme LightMaze -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
xcrun simctl list devices available
SIMULATOR_UDID="$(python3 scripts/select_simulator.py)"
test -n "$SIMULATOR_UDID" || { echo "No available simulator"; exit 1; }
xcodebuild -project LightMaze.xcodeproj -scheme LightMaze -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIMULATOR_UDID" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test
python3 scripts/check_repo.py
```

If the repo uses an `.xcworkspace`, SwiftPM-generated project or a different scheme, inspect it and replace these paths; the test commands above do not constitute successful execution here. Build/sign/archive and test native ANGLE/Metal rendering on macOS with Xcode and a physical device.

### Minimal Python repository audit script

Create `scripts/check_repo.py` during the first phase. It should verify presence of essential architecture documents and app-owned shaders, then print the pinned VisualCore version using an actual resolved dependency file. Do not automatically download code or modify an upstream checkout.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import sys
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
required = ["CLAUDE.md", "docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md"]
missing = [name for name in required if not (root / name).is_file()]
for path in missing:
    print(f"MISSING: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
if missing:
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("Repository guidance and integration contract are present")
```

### Portable Python 3 simulator selection helper

Save as `scripts/select_simulator.py`; it reads `xcrun simctl` JSON and chooses a booted iOS simulator first, otherwise an available iPhone simulator. This helper does not create or boot a device; select/boot one manually if no compatible runtime is installed.

```python
import json
import subprocess
import sys
output = subprocess.check_output(
    ["xcrun", "simctl", "list", "devices", "available", "-j"], text=True)
data = json.loads(output)
devices = [device for runtime, group in data.get("devices", {}).items()
           if "iOS" in runtime for device in group
           if device.get("isAvailable", True) and "iPhone" in device.get("name", "")]
device = next((d for d in devices if d.get("state") == "Booted"),
              devices[0] if devices else None)
if device is None:
    sys.exit("No available iPhone simulator. Check Xcode runtimes.")
print(device["udid"])
```

### Minimal XcodeGen target layout

For a fresh repo, an initial `project.yml` can be generated with the following app-only starter; replace deployment target and bundle ID with validated project values, then add local package products only after the VisualCore audit.

```yaml
name: LightMaze
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.example.visualcore
targets:
  LightMaze:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    deploymentTarget: "17.0"   # proposal, verify supported OS
    sources:
      - Apps/LightMaze
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.visualcore.light-maze
```

Install XcodeGen through its official distribution if not already available, verify `xcodegen --version`, and run `xcodegen generate` only after this file and target source exist. Avoid storing unreviewed private package tokens in `project.yml` or CI.

### Suggested macOS GitHub Actions job (create after actual build validation)

```yaml
name: iOS CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Verify Python and repository artifacts
        run: python3 scripts/check_repo.py
      - name: Inspect Xcode and app schemes
        run: xcodebuild -list -project LightMaze.xcodeproj
      - name: Build simulator target
        run: xcodebuild -project LightMaze.xcodeproj -scheme LightMaze -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Pin CI action revisions and the Xcode version according to your organization’s supply-chain rules; add simulator unit tests and any authenticated VisualCore package fetch only after configuration is proven to work. CI on macOS does not substitute for physical GPU regression testing.

## 15. Acceptance criteria and definition of done

A first-release candidate is acceptable only when **all** of the following can be demonstrated:

- [ ] MVP-01: At least 20 handcrafted levels with emitter, wall, mirror, target and optional prism tile.
- [ ] MVP-02: Drag/rotate interactions snapped to puzzle grid.
- [ ] MVP-03: Deterministic ray propagation with reflection and finite bounce cap.
- [ ] MVP-04: Level select, unlock progression, undo/restart and success feedback.
- [ ] MVP-05: Visual glow and color cues without hiding beam connectivity.
- [ ] MVP-06: Built-in solvability test for level data.
- [ ] Standalone app uses public audited VisualCore APIs and shared ANGLE/Metal path, not ProjectM-specific engine internals.
- [ ] Render-state serializations are versioned, validated, and safe after background/resume and renderer reset.
- [ ] Native UI is usable with accessibility features; reduced motion and quality controls behave as stated.
- [ ] Domain and integration test cases in §11 pass; unresolved errors are documented, not marked passing.
- [ ] At least one physical device run with recorded build/OS/device metadata validates actual GPU behavior.
- [ ] No unsupported privacy, scientific or platform capability claims remain in the product UI or listing.
- [ ] Bundled third-party code, shaders, assets, educational facts and sounds have reviewed license/source records.
- [ ] Build from a clean macOS checkout succeeds and the final PR contains exact verification commands and results.
- [ ] Any VisualCore changes have their own upstream PR plus before/after ProjectM reference regression evidence.

## 16. Ordered next actions

1. Create a new `LightMaze` app repo and initialize the Claude/Spec Kit Python variant (commands in §7).
2. Perform read-only VisualCore package/render-host inspection; resolve actual public APIs and upstream gaps.
3. Save the constitution and app-specific design decisions in reviewed repository artifacts.
4. Run Phase 00 through all eight quality gates; complete any upstream VisualCore feature as a separate, reviewed change.
5. Implement Phase 01 grid/ray reflection solver and fixtures as the smallest testable vertical slice.
6. Continue the remaining phases one by one; compare every release claim against the acceptance matrix.
7. Archive evidence from physical device validation and review the release privacy/license checklist.

# Solar System Explorer
## iOS application architecture and Spec Kit + Claude Code implementation manual

**Concept #14 of 25** | **Category:** Education and science | **Proposed app/repository target:** `SolarSystemExplorer`
**Planning status:** proposed implementation guide; not proof of an existing application or released VisualCore package. **Source:** `AppsBrainstorm.md` catalog item 14; `README.md` VisualCore architecture and Spec Kit strategy.
**Rendering invariant:** reuse the existing ProjectM-proven OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal infrastructure exposed by VisualCore. Never create a duplicate EGL/ANGLE backend or link ProjectM engine internals into this independent app.

---

## 1. Executive summary and source traceability

An educational solar system viewer that cleanly distinguishes astronomical scale, time simulation and artistically exaggerated displays.

### Original brainstorm concept

> An interactive 3D solar system with orbital mechanics, planetary details, time controls, and educational information.

**VisualCore capabilities listed in the brainstorm:**
- 3D scenes
- Camera controls
- Materials and lighting
- Animation
- Time-based simulation

**Original product opportunity:** An educational astronomy experience with guided tours and interactive exploration.

**Recommended product hypothesis:** A carefully scoped, offline-capable first release can demonstrate a distinct graphics workload and validate reusable VisualCore APIs. Test this hypothesis with a functioning vertical slice before expanding content or monetization.

## 2. Product contract and scope

### Primary audiences
- Students learning planetary order and relative motion
- Families exploring space together
- Astronomy hobbyists seeking a visually compelling primer

### End-to-end user journeys
1. **Journey 1:** Open orbit overview with labeled planets.
2. **Journey 2:** Select planet to inspect a fact card and orbit.
3. **Journey 3:** Change simulation date/rate, reset to present and take guided tour.

### Version 0.1 feature contract
1. **Feature 01:** Sun and eight major planets with curated fact cards and licensed textures. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
2. **Feature 02:** Orbit view, planet focus and camera navigation. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
3. **Feature 03:** Play/pause/speed up simulated motion with explicit date/time display. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
4. **Feature 04:** Separate true-relative and visibility-enhanced size/distance modes. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
5. **Feature 05:** Guided tours with narration-free captions. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
6. **Feature 06:** References and units displayed on educational claims. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.

### Explicit non-goals
- NASA-grade ephemeris or high precision live sky position
- Real-time telescope alignment
- Unlicensed imagery/data scraping

### Later-stage ideas, not MVP commitments
- Additional dwarf planets and moons
- Source-specific ephemeris datasets with validation
- Educational quizzes and AR exploration

## 3. UX blueprint

The first launch should reach a meaningful working graphic or educational interaction without requiring an account. Use SwiftUI for navigation, settings, labels and accessibility; host VisualCore rendering in a verified UIView/UIViewRepresentable integration that owns no duplicate GPU lifecycle.

**Proposed screen inventory** (adapt to the app-specific flows above):
| Screen | Responsibility | Concrete behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Home / gallery | Start without setup | Curated Solar System Explorer example, recent scene and explicit entry point |
| Interactive scene | Primary VisualCore rendering surface | Touch and app-state changes mapped into validated domain commands |
| Inspector | Controls and explanations | Show effective parameter values, reset and valid ranges |
| Library / files | Persistence where relevant | Open, duplicate, save, import/export only via permitted system APIs |
| Settings / help | Quality, accessibility, privacy | Explain input permissions, limitations, credits and renderer fallback |

**Interaction design rules:** screen gestures must have a deterministic domain meaning; rendering can interpolate but cannot silently change persisted state. State-affecting controls should be testable independent of the GPU. All critical feedback must remain legible without bloom, color alone, or animation.

### State transitions to implement
```text
uninitialized → loading-assets → ready → active
                                  ↔ paused / backgrounded
                                  ↘ editing / exporting (if supported)
any GPU state → renderer-lost → recover-resources → ready
any document state → validation-error → recoverable-message
```

Do not upload application/scene state to a server by default. If future features introduce accounts, cloud sync or sharing, write a new privacy and threat-model spec before implementation.

## 4. Architecture: VisualCore consumer, not renderer fork

```text
SolarSystemExplorer SwiftUI app (navigation, accessibility, preferences)
    ↓ commands / immutable snapshots
SolarSystemExplorerCore (domain rules, models, persistence schemas, validation)
    ↓ render-state snapshot; never raw SwiftUI bindings
SolarSystemExplorerRendering (scene adapter, shaders, asset IDs, pass descriptions)
    ↓ public APIs discovered in the real VisualCore checkout
VisualCore runtime, shaders, effects, scenes, inputs, diagnostics
    ↓ shared EGL/context/render host as audited
Existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal implementation
    ↓
iOS device GPU and display
```

**Ownership policy:** The app owns its content, mathematical rules, domain schema, UI and business logic. VisualCore owns generic graphics infrastructure. `Coastrnaut/projectm-ios` remains VisualCore's pinned reference submodule, not an app dependency. Any VisualCore API needed but not present must be proposed upstream with a test and an API contract; do not stub an imaginary package into production.

### Contracts and threading
- A domain coordinator produces immutable render snapshots or bounded commands; presentation does not mutate simulation truth.
- The VisualCore render host controls the EGL context, resource lifetime, presentation and the required render thread/queue; all GL work obeys that ownership.
- Native SwiftUI overlays remain separate from shader drawing where legibility, hit-testing and VoiceOver need native controls.
- On scene resize, background, memory warning or renderer reset, reallocate GPU resources from versioned CPU state rather than persisting raw GL handles.
- Shaders are treated as bundled, versioned assets unless the specific product explicitly supports user-authored GLSL with additional guards.

### Application-specific components
- **`CelestialBodyCatalog.swift`**: data storage, schema validation, assets or export; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`OrbitCalculator.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`UnitConversion.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`SolarClock.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`PlanetFocusController.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`SolarRenderer.swift`**: renderer-facing render orchestration and GPU pass bindings; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.

## 6. Domain model, algorithms and rendering design

### Versioned domain schemas (proposed types)
| Type | Field contract / required invariants |
|---|---|
| `CelestialBody` | `CelestialBody(id, meanRadiusKm, semiMajorAxisAU, periodDays, axialTiltDeg, textureID, sourceRef)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `OrbitElements` | `OrbitElements(modelVersion, epochUTC, parameters, validityRange)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `SolarView` | `SolarView(camera, simulationUTC, timeRate, scaleMode, selectedBody)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `FactCard` | `FactCard(bodyID, fact, value, units, citation)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |

Use explicit units and coordinate spaces in type names or documentation. Reject NaN/Inf, invalid counts, truncated files, unreasonable allocations and unsupported versions where applicable. Canonical storage should be pure data; expensive buffers can be reconstructed.

### Algorithm and correctness decisions
1. Start with labeled approximate Kepler or simplified analytic orbits, not precision ephemerides.
2. Keep double-precision orbital state on CPU and convert camera-relative positions for GPU.
3. Make AU/km conversions explicit and separate physical radii from visual display scale.
4. Label timestamps and time zones; clock speed cannot imply predictive precision beyond model scope.

### App-specific render sequence
1. **Stage 1:** Advance simulation time and compute orbit positions in double precision.
2. **Stage 2:** Produce camera-relative model transforms and LOD choices.
3. **Stage 3:** Render star background, Sun, planets, orbit trails and labels.
4. **Stage 4:** Show educational card overlays and scale mode legend.

### Rendering lifecycle and frame budget
- Create resources only after VisualCore signals a valid owning EGL context; release/recreate on context loss and size changes.
- Separate fixed-step simulation, event handling, visual animation time and wall time when the product uses more than one.
- Treat device tier as policy data: resolution scale, effect counts, iterations and object count may change; domain correctness and user state may not.
- Validate framebuffer completeness, shader compile/link results, texture format support and GPU resource handles before presenting a frame.
- Record frame pacing, app-owned CPU time, allocation counts and renderer recovery on a real device before selecting release targets.

### Required capability audit against VisualCore
- **3D scenes** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.

## 7. Local environment and reproducible bootstrap

**Prerequisites:** macOS and Xcode for iOS build, signing, Simulator and physical-device tests; Git, Python 3, `uv`, and Claude Code CLI. Windows can prepare specifications and source but cannot validate the iOS rendering path without a macOS builder. Follow current vendor instructions for installation; verify tool versions rather than assuming they exist.

**Terminal on macOS — commands to create this app repository:**
```bash
mkdir SolarSystemExplorer && cd SolarSystemExplorer
git init -b main
git --version
python3 --version
uv --version
claude --version
uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git
specify version
specify init --help
specify init --here --integration claude --script py
specify check
git status --short
claude
```

Initialize Spec Kit **once** in a newly created repository. In a non-empty existing repo, commit/backup first and inspect `specify init --help`; `--force` may merge/overwrite managed files and must not be run blindly. Never run Spec Kit initialization inside the VisualCore or ProjectM submodule from an app repo.

**Current Claude Code integration:** Spec Kit creates `.claude/skills/speckit-<command>/SKILL.md`; invoke skills in Claude chat using **hyphens**, e.g. `/speckit-specify`, not the dotted spelling used in some generic documentation. Confirm actual skills with `find .claude/skills -name SKILL.md` and Claude `/help` because installed versions can differ. See official [Claude integration](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html).

**Terminal — verify a local VisualCore checkout without assuming package products:**
```bash
test -d ../VisualCore || { echo "Clone or locate the VisualCore repository beside this app first"; exit 1; }
git -C ../VisualCore status --short
find ../VisualCore -name Package.swift -not -path "*/.build/*" -print
git -C ../VisualCore submodule status
```

If `../VisualCore` does not yet provide a consumer package, create an upstream integration feature and stop at a no-op host skeleton. Do not invent `VisualCoreRenderer` product names or fake ANGLE integration code.
