**Terminal:**
```bash
git status --short
git diff --check
git diff --stat
git add -A
git commit -m "feat: complete reviewed implementation phase"
git log -3 --oneline
```

**Claude Code chat, at every task boundary:**
```text
Inspect the active Spec Kit tasks file. Implement only the next smallest dependency-complete task group. Before editing, list intended files, known VisualCore API contracts, test commands, and rollback steps. After editing, run tests and report actual results; do not claim device validation without device logs. Stop for review after this group.
```

Do not ask Claude to run all seven phases unattended. Spec Kit artifacts may expose architecture errors or rights/permission issues that materially change the following work. The Git baseline is reviewed per phase; commit evidence and tests in the application repository, and upstream patches separately.

## 11. Domain, renderer and UI verification matrix

| Layer | App-specific test | Evidence / gate |
|---|---|---|
| Pure domain model | Compiler-error line mapping points to actual authored line | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Pure domain model | Compilation failure never replaces working preview | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Oversized project is rejected before GPU work | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Missing uniforms and incompatible GLES versions show specific guidance | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Device or end-to-end | Compile/run repeated cycles do not leak shader/program objects | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Shared render lifecycle | Repeated renderer create, resize, background, resume, context recovery, release | Device log with no stale EGL/GL handles or persistent GPU memory growth |
| App UI and accessibility | First-session flow, disabled states, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver fallback | UI test + human review on representative iPhone and iPad |
| VisualCore regression | If VisualCore changes, ProjectM remains functional at pinned submodule commit | Existing ProjectM build/smoke log; any difference reviewed |

### Implementation-level fixtures
- Fixture 1: Compiler-error line mapping points to actual authored line.
- Fixture 2: Compilation failure never replaces working preview.
- Fixture 3: Oversized project is rejected before GPU work.
- Fixture 4: Missing uniforms and incompatible GLES versions show specific guidance.
- Fixture 5: Compile/run repeated cycles do not leak shader/program objects.

### Simulator and device separation
- CI/simulator: test domain math, model migration, document round trips, permission-denied paths, basic UI and reproducible app builds.
- Physical iPhone/iPad: validate ANGLE Metal path, shader compilation, context loss, high-refresh/low-refresh behavior, thermals, memory, inputs and real audio/device sensor routes if relevant.
- When tests depend on audio, sensors or input permissions, use synthetic fixtures in CI; do not silently substitute test signals for production sources.
- Store exact Xcode, iOS, device, VisualCore revision, ProjectM submodule revision, preset and test duration with performance reports.

## 12. Profiling plan, budgets and graceful fallback

Before specifying absolute fps, startup or memory targets, measure a baseline on the reference app and at least one representative device. Decide thresholds in a separate acceptance ADR; do not publish invented benchmark numbers.

- Cap preview resolution/FPS, program count and per-session compile attempts.
- Measure compile/link time and shader presentation time separately.
- Provide safe default templates and clear recovery if renderer resets.

**Telemetry only as local diagnostics by default:** record per-pass timing if genuinely supported, present interval, app-side CPU duration, memory and resource counts, scene configuration, chosen quality tier and build IDs. Make collection opt-in if data ever leaves the device. Never label CPU timings as GPU timings.

**Fallback policy:** keep the app usable when expensive shader passes fail or a device is below target capability: reduce resolution/passes, use a simpler scene, preserve user state, and display a recoverable explanation. When no VisualCore render host exists, ship a native UI placeholder only for internal integration testing—not a misleading App Store release.

## 13. Risks, privacy, science/platform constraints and licenses

### App-specific risk register
1. **Risk 1:** User GLSL can trigger expensive driver behavior—cap input/preview and offer stop/reset, but do not promise execution sandbox. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
2. **Risk 2:** Keyboard/editor ergonomics on iPhone—prioritize iPad and hardware keyboard. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
3. **Risk 3:** Shader language/version support may vary by ANGLE—query capabilities and expose compatibility profile. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.

### Cross-cutting obligations
- No private iOS APIs, undocumented system-level audio interception, automatic wallpaper changes or unsupported GPU access; test any requested platform capability against current public documentation.
- Apply least-privilege permission prompts, with useful demo/offline behavior for denied permissions. Document Photos, Files, microphone or audio rights only where that app actually needs them.
- Maintain licenses for ANGLE, VisualCore, ProjectM reference code and all bundled shaders, meshes, textures, fonts, datasets, sound and educational copy. Do not assume upstream assets may be redistributed.
- Use clear scientific/educational caveats wherever simulations or graphics are illustrative. Do not market a toy visualization as an instrument, diagnostic tool or accurate predictive model.
- Validate imported data formats, sizes, paths and schema versions; avoid executing untrusted user code except in the specifically constrained Shader Studio design.

### Content and App Store review checklist
- Document why each permission is necessary and the exact UI path requesting it.
- Provide privacy policy and required app data disclosures based on actual telemetry/storage behavior, not sample text.
- Check all media and code redistribution rights, attribution and trademark rules before the storefront submission.
- Keep claims in marketing and screenshots aligned to implemented working features and measured/attributed facts.

## 14. Xcode project, build, and CI commands

After selecting XcodeGen and writing a real `project.yml` during Phase 0/1, these are executable examples **from this app repo**. Scheme and target names must be confirmed with `xcodebuild -list`; do not assume VisualCore has a particular SPM product name.

```bash
# Use XcodeGen only if project.yml was adopted and reviewed
xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -list -project ShaderStudio.xcodeproj
xcodebuild -project ShaderStudio.xcodeproj -scheme ShaderStudio -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
xcrun simctl list devices available
SIMULATOR_UDID="$(python3 scripts/select_simulator.py)"
test -n "$SIMULATOR_UDID" || { echo "No available simulator"; exit 1; }
xcodebuild -project ShaderStudio.xcodeproj -scheme ShaderStudio -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIMULATOR_UDID" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test
python3 scripts/check_repo.py
```

If the repo uses an `.xcworkspace`, SwiftPM-generated project or a different scheme, inspect it and replace these paths; the test commands above do not constitute successful execution here. Build/sign/archive and test native ANGLE/Metal rendering on macOS with Xcode and a physical device.

### Minimal Python repository audit script

Create `scripts/check_repo.py` during the first phase. It should verify presence of essential architecture documents and app-owned shaders, then print the pinned VisualCore version using an actual resolved dependency file. Do not automatically download code or modify an upstream checkout.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import sys
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
required = ["CLAUDE.md", "docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md"]
missing = [name for name in required if not (root / name).is_file()]
for path in missing:
    print(f"MISSING: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
if missing:
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("Repository guidance and integration contract are present")
```

### Portable Python 3 simulator selection helper

Save as `scripts/select_simulator.py`; it reads `xcrun simctl` JSON and chooses a booted iOS simulator first, otherwise an available iPhone simulator. This helper does not create or boot a device; select/boot one manually if no compatible runtime is installed.

```python
import json
import subprocess
import sys
output = subprocess.check_output(
    ["xcrun", "simctl", "list", "devices", "available", "-j"], text=True)
data = json.loads(output)
devices = [device for runtime, group in data.get("devices", {}).items()
           if "iOS" in runtime for device in group
           if device.get("isAvailable", True) and "iPhone" in device.get("name", "")]
device = next((d for d in devices if d.get("state") == "Booted"),
              devices[0] if devices else None)
if device is None:
    sys.exit("No available iPhone simulator. Check Xcode runtimes.")
print(device["udid"])
```

### Minimal XcodeGen target layout

For a fresh repo, an initial `project.yml` can be generated with the following app-only starter; replace deployment target and bundle ID with validated project values, then add local package products only after the VisualCore audit.

```yaml
name: ShaderStudio
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.example.visualcore
targets:
  ShaderStudio:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    deploymentTarget: "17.0"   # proposal, verify supported OS
    sources:
      - Apps/ShaderStudio
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.visualcore.shader-studio
```

Install XcodeGen through its official distribution if not already available, verify `xcodegen --version`, and run `xcodegen generate` only after this file and target source exist. Avoid storing unreviewed private package tokens in `project.yml` or CI.

### Suggested macOS GitHub Actions job (create after actual build validation)

```yaml
name: iOS CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Verify Python and repository artifacts
        run: python3 scripts/check_repo.py
      - name: Inspect Xcode and app schemes
        run: xcodebuild -list -project ShaderStudio.xcodeproj
      - name: Build simulator target
        run: xcodebuild -project ShaderStudio.xcodeproj -scheme ShaderStudio -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Pin CI action revisions and the Xcode version according to your organization’s supply-chain rules; add simulator unit tests and any authenticated VisualCore package fetch only after configuration is proven to work. CI on macOS does not substitute for physical GPU regression testing.

## 15. Acceptance criteria and definition of done

A first-release candidate is acceptable only when **all** of the following can be demonstrated:

- [ ] MVP-01: Code editor with syntax assistance and line-numbered diagnostics.
- [ ] MVP-02: Local GLSL ES fragment shader templates with defined uniforms and texture inputs.
- [ ] MVP-03: Explicit Compile/Run action and last-known-good preview fallback.
- [ ] MVP-04: Parameter inspector for bounded uniforms.
- [ ] MVP-05: Local project save/open and versioned shader files.
- [ ] MVP-06: Resource/complexity limits, watchdog UX and recoverable failures.
- [ ] Standalone app uses public audited VisualCore APIs and shared ANGLE/Metal path, not ProjectM-specific engine internals.
- [ ] Render-state serializations are versioned, validated, and safe after background/resume and renderer reset.
- [ ] Native UI is usable with accessibility features; reduced motion and quality controls behave as stated.
- [ ] Domain and integration test cases in §11 pass; unresolved errors are documented, not marked passing.
- [ ] At least one physical device run with recorded build/OS/device metadata validates actual GPU behavior.
- [ ] No unsupported privacy, scientific or platform capability claims remain in the product UI or listing.
- [ ] Bundled third-party code, shaders, assets, educational facts and sounds have reviewed license/source records.
- [ ] Build from a clean macOS checkout succeeds and the final PR contains exact verification commands and results.
- [ ] Any VisualCore changes have their own upstream PR plus before/after ProjectM reference regression evidence.

## 16. Ordered next actions

1. Create a new `ShaderStudio` app repo and initialize the Claude/Spec Kit Python variant (commands in §7).
2. Perform read-only VisualCore package/render-host inspection; resolve actual public APIs and upstream gaps.
3. Save the constitution and app-specific design decisions in reviewed repository artifacts.
4. Run Phase 00 through all eight quality gates; complete any upstream VisualCore feature as a separate, reviewed change.
5. Implement Phase 01 glsl/diagnostic contract and editor shell as the smallest testable vertical slice.
6. Continue the remaining phases one by one; compare every release claim against the acceptance matrix.
7. Archive evidence from physical device validation and review the release privacy/license checklist.

# Visual Programming Lab
## iOS application architecture and Spec Kit + Claude Code implementation manual

**Concept #23 of 25** | **Category:** Developer and creator tools | **Proposed app/repository target:** `VisualProgrammingLab`
**Planning status:** proposed implementation guide; not proof of an existing application or released VisualCore package. **Source:** `AppsBrainstorm.md` catalog item 23; `README.md` VisualCore architecture and Spec Kit strategy.
**Rendering invariant:** reuse the existing ProjectM-proven OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal infrastructure exposed by VisualCore. Never create a duplicate EGL/ANGLE backend or link ProjectM engine internals into this independent app.

---

## 1. Executive summary and source traceability

A constrained node-graph editor for composing parameterized visuals without writing shader code.

### Original brainstorm concept

> A node-based visual programming environment for building interactive graphics without writing code.

**VisualCore capabilities listed in the brainstorm:**
- Render graph
- Compositing
- Parameter system
- Reusable effects
- Graph serialization

**Original product opportunity:** A more ambitious creative tool that could eventually support reusable user-created visual projects.

**Recommended product hypothesis:** A carefully scoped, offline-capable first release can demonstrate a distinct graphics workload and validate reusable VisualCore APIs. Test this hypothesis with a functioning vertical slice before expanding content or monetization.

## 2. Product contract and scope

### Primary audiences
- Creative users who prefer visual programming
- Educators demonstrating dataflow
- Developers validating VisualCore graph abstractions

### End-to-end user journeys
1. **Journey 1:** Open example graph with Noise → Colorize → Output.
2. **Journey 2:** Add a Mix node and connect typed ports.
3. **Journey 3:** See preview update, save graph and reopen it.

### Version 0.1 feature contract
1. **Feature 01:** Typed node graph for scalar, color, texture and time values. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
2. **Feature 02:** Initial node library: Time, Constant, Noise, Gradient, Mix, Blur, Output. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
3. **Feature 03:** Touch graph canvas with wire routing, zoom and selection. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
4. **Feature 04:** Cycle detection and clear invalid-connection feedback. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
5. **Feature 05:** Preview renderer that compiles/translates a bounded acyclic graph. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
6. **Feature 06:** Versioned graph persistence with migration hooks. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.

### Explicit non-goals
- Arbitrary scripting/code execution
- Unbounded loops or feedback nodes in MVP
- Desktop-class node editor with hundreds of nodes

### Later-stage ideas, not MVP commitments
- Custom subgraphs and feedback nodes with explicit frame delay
- Graph export to static preset
- Community sharing with schema/security review

## 3. UX blueprint

The first launch should reach a meaningful working graphic or educational interaction without requiring an account. Use SwiftUI for navigation, settings, labels and accessibility; host VisualCore rendering in a verified UIView/UIViewRepresentable integration that owns no duplicate GPU lifecycle.

**Proposed screen inventory** (adapt to the app-specific flows above):
| Screen | Responsibility | Concrete behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Home / gallery | Start without setup | Curated Visual Programming Lab example, recent scene and explicit entry point |
| Interactive scene | Primary VisualCore rendering surface | Touch and app-state changes mapped into validated domain commands |
| Inspector | Controls and explanations | Show effective parameter values, reset and valid ranges |
| Library / files | Persistence where relevant | Open, duplicate, save, import/export only via permitted system APIs |
| Settings / help | Quality, accessibility, privacy | Explain input permissions, limitations, credits and renderer fallback |

**Interaction design rules:** screen gestures must have a deterministic domain meaning; rendering can interpolate but cannot silently change persisted state. State-affecting controls should be testable independent of the GPU. All critical feedback must remain legible without bloom, color alone, or animation.

### State transitions to implement
```text
uninitialized → loading-assets → ready → active
                                  ↔ paused / backgrounded
                                  ↘ editing / exporting (if supported)
any GPU state → renderer-lost → recover-resources → ready
any document state → validation-error → recoverable-message
```

Do not upload application/scene state to a server by default. If future features introduce accounts, cloud sync or sharing, write a new privacy and threat-model spec before implementation.

## 4. Architecture: VisualCore consumer, not renderer fork

```text
VisualProgrammingLab SwiftUI app (navigation, accessibility, preferences)
    ↓ commands / immutable snapshots
VisualProgrammingLabCore (domain rules, models, persistence schemas, validation)
    ↓ render-state snapshot; never raw SwiftUI bindings
VisualProgrammingLabRendering (scene adapter, shaders, asset IDs, pass descriptions)
    ↓ public APIs discovered in the real VisualCore checkout
VisualCore runtime, shaders, effects, scenes, inputs, diagnostics
    ↓ shared EGL/context/render host as audited
Existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal implementation
    ↓
iOS device GPU and display
```

**Ownership policy:** The app owns its content, mathematical rules, domain schema, UI and business logic. VisualCore owns generic graphics infrastructure. `Coastrnaut/projectm-ios` remains VisualCore's pinned reference submodule, not an app dependency. Any VisualCore API needed but not present must be proposed upstream with a test and an API contract; do not stub an imaginary package into production.

### Contracts and threading
- A domain coordinator produces immutable render snapshots or bounded commands; presentation does not mutate simulation truth.
- The VisualCore render host controls the EGL context, resource lifetime, presentation and the required render thread/queue; all GL work obeys that ownership.
- Native SwiftUI overlays remain separate from shader drawing where legibility, hit-testing and VoiceOver need native controls.
- On scene resize, background, memory warning or renderer reset, reallocate GPU resources from versioned CPU state rather than persisting raw GL handles.
- Shaders are treated as bundled, versioned assets unless the specific product explicitly supports user-authored GLSL with additional guards.

### Application-specific components
- **`VisualGraph.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`NodeRegistry.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`TypeChecker.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`TopologicalSort.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`RenderGraphCompiler.swift`**: renderer-facing render orchestration and GPU pass bindings; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`GraphCanvas.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`GraphPreviewRenderer.swift`**: renderer-facing render orchestration and GPU pass bindings; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.

### File creation policy

- Store data fixtures in JSON/CSV where appropriate, with explicit schema and license metadata; do not serialize GPU buffer addresses or EGL objects.
- Keep all feature specs under `specs/` created by Spec Kit; allow its installed release to determine feature numbering and active feature selection.

## 6. Domain model, algorithms and rendering design

### Versioned domain schemas (proposed types)
| Type | Field contract / required invariants |
|---|---|
| `GraphNode` | `GraphNode(id, kind, parameterValues, position)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `GraphPort` | `GraphPort(nodeID, portID, valueType, direction)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `GraphEdge` | `GraphEdge(sourceNode, sourcePort, targetNode, targetPort)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `VisualGraph` | `VisualGraph(version, nodes, edges, outputNodeID)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `CompiledGraph` | `CompiledGraph(orderedNodes, allocations, diagnostics)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |

Use explicit units and coordinate spaces in type names or documentation. Reject NaN/Inf, invalid counts, truncated files, unreasonable allocations and unsupported versions where applicable. Canonical storage should be pure data; expensive buffers can be reconstructed.

### Algorithm and correctness decisions
1. Validate graph topology by topological sort and reject cycles before GPU work.
2. Use declared typed input/output ports to enforce composability.
3. Compile known nodes into a bounded render pass schedule; separate graph interpreter and renderer.
4. Cache compiled subgraphs by content hash and invalidate downstream nodes on edits.
5. Keep feedback/cyclic effects out until explicit state ownership is designed.

### App-specific render sequence
1. **Stage 1:** Apply graph edit to immutable model.
2. **Stage 2:** Validate ports and dependency ordering.
3. **Stage 3:** Compile known node operators into VisualCore passes and allocate textures based on lifetimes.
4. **Stage 4:** Render preview, map diagnostics to graph nodes and present.

### Rendering lifecycle and frame budget
- Create resources only after VisualCore signals a valid owning EGL context; release/recreate on context loss and size changes.
- Separate fixed-step simulation, event handling, visual animation time and wall time when the product uses more than one.
- Treat device tier as policy data: resolution scale, effect counts, iterations and object count may change; domain correctness and user state may not.
- Validate framebuffer completeness, shader compile/link results, texture format support and GPU resource handles before presenting a frame.
- Record frame pacing, app-owned CPU time, allocation counts and renderer recovery on a real device before selecting release targets.

### Required capability audit against VisualCore
- **Render graph** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Compositing** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Parameter system** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Reusable effects** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Graph serialization** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.

> **Domain-specific engineering rule:** Node graph semantics are a product-specific dependency layer on top of VisualCoreEffects, not an excuse to introduce a second rendering backend.

## 7. Local environment and reproducible bootstrap

**Prerequisites:** macOS and Xcode for iOS build, signing, Simulator and physical-device tests; Git, Python 3, `uv`, and Claude Code CLI. Windows can prepare specifications and source but cannot validate the iOS rendering path without a macOS builder. Follow current vendor instructions for installation; verify tool versions rather than assuming they exist.

**Terminal on macOS — commands to create this app repository:**
```bash
mkdir VisualProgrammingLab && cd VisualProgrammingLab
git init -b main
git --version
python3 --version
uv --version
claude --version
uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git
specify version
specify init --help
specify init --here --integration claude --script py
specify check
git status --short
claude
```

Initialize Spec Kit **once** in a newly created repository. In a non-empty existing repo, commit/backup first and inspect `specify init --help`; `--force` may merge/overwrite managed files and must not be run blindly. Never run Spec Kit initialization inside the VisualCore or ProjectM submodule from an app repo.

**Current Claude Code integration:** Spec Kit creates `.claude/skills/speckit-<command>/SKILL.md`; invoke skills in Claude chat using **hyphens**, e.g. `/speckit-specify`, not the dotted spelling used in some generic documentation. Confirm actual skills with `find .claude/skills -name SKILL.md` and Claude `/help` because installed versions can differ. See official [Claude integration](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html).

**Terminal — verify a local VisualCore checkout without assuming package products:**
```bash
test -d ../VisualCore || { echo "Clone or locate the VisualCore repository beside this app first"; exit 1; }
git -C ../VisualCore status --short
find ../VisualCore -name Package.swift -not -path "*/.build/*" -print
git -C ../VisualCore submodule status
```

If `../VisualCore` does not yet provide a consumer package, create an upstream integration feature and stop at a no-op host skeleton. Do not invent `VisualCoreRenderer` product names or fake ANGLE integration code.

## 10. Bounded Claude execution and Git workflow

**Terminal:**
```bash
git status --short
git diff --check
git diff --stat
git add -A
git commit -m "feat: complete reviewed implementation phase"
git log -3 --oneline
```

**Claude Code chat, at every task boundary:**
```text
Inspect the active Spec Kit tasks file. Implement only the next smallest dependency-complete task group. Before editing, list intended files, known VisualCore API contracts, test commands, and rollback steps. After editing, run tests and report actual results; do not claim device validation without device logs. Stop for review after this group.
```

Do not ask Claude to run all seven phases unattended. Spec Kit artifacts may expose architecture errors or rights/permission issues that materially change the following work. The Git baseline is reviewed per phase; commit evidence and tests in the application repository, and upstream patches separately.

## 11. Domain, renderer and UI verification matrix

| Layer | App-specific test | Evidence / gate |
|---|---|---|
| Pure domain model | Cycle is rejected with identifiable edge/path | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Pure domain model | Color cannot connect to scalar input without explicit converter | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Disconnected Output gives clear error state | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Save/load preserves node IDs, port links and layout | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Device or end-to-end | A simple graph produces expected pixel fixtures and avoids unnecessary passes | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Shared render lifecycle | Repeated renderer create, resize, background, resume, context recovery, release | Device log with no stale EGL/GL handles or persistent GPU memory growth |
| App UI and accessibility | First-session flow, disabled states, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver fallback | UI test + human review on representative iPhone and iPad |
| VisualCore regression | If VisualCore changes, ProjectM remains functional at pinned submodule commit | Existing ProjectM build/smoke log; any difference reviewed |

### Implementation-level fixtures
- Fixture 1: Cycle is rejected with identifiable edge/path.
- Fixture 2: Color cannot connect to scalar input without explicit converter.
- Fixture 3: Disconnected Output gives clear error state.
- Fixture 4: Save/load preserves node IDs, port links and layout.
- Fixture 5: A simple graph produces expected pixel fixtures and avoids unnecessary passes.

### Simulator and device separation
- CI/simulator: test domain math, model migration, document round trips, permission-denied paths, basic UI and reproducible app builds.
- Physical iPhone/iPad: validate ANGLE Metal path, shader compilation, context loss, high-refresh/low-refresh behavior, thermals, memory, inputs and real audio/device sensor routes if relevant.
- When tests depend on audio, sensors or input permissions, use synthetic fixtures in CI; do not silently substitute test signals for production sources.
- Store exact Xcode, iOS, device, VisualCore revision, ProjectM submodule revision, preset and test duration with performance reports.

## 12. Profiling plan, budgets and graceful fallback

Before specifying absolute fps, startup or memory targets, measure a baseline on the reference app and at least one representative device. Decide thresholds in a separate acceptance ADR; do not publish invented benchmark numbers.

- Measure compile time, pass count, temporary memory and preview latency.
- Use low-res preview while editing.
- Validate graph resource budget before allocating GPU targets.

**Telemetry only as local diagnostics by default:** record per-pass timing if genuinely supported, present interval, app-side CPU duration, memory and resource counts, scene configuration, chosen quality tier and build IDs. Make collection opt-in if data ever leaves the device. Never label CPU timings as GPU timings.

**Fallback policy:** keep the app usable when expensive shader passes fail or a device is below target capability: reduce resolution/passes, use a simpler scene, preserve user state, and display a recoverable explanation. When no VisualCore render host exists, ship a native UI placeholder only for internal integration testing—not a misleading App Store release.

## 13. Risks, privacy, science/platform constraints and licenses

### App-specific risk register
1. **Risk 1:** User-generated graphs can consume excessive FBO memory—static budget before compile. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
2. **Risk 2:** Complex touch wiring can be frustrating—large targets and zoom. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
3. **Risk 3:** Stable graph file formats require migration policy. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.

### Cross-cutting obligations
- No private iOS APIs, undocumented system-level audio interception, automatic wallpaper changes or unsupported GPU access; test any requested platform capability against current public documentation.
- Apply least-privilege permission prompts, with useful demo/offline behavior for denied permissions. Document Photos, Files, microphone or audio rights only where that app actually needs them.
- Maintain licenses for ANGLE, VisualCore, ProjectM reference code and all bundled shaders, meshes, textures, fonts, datasets, sound and educational copy. Do not assume upstream assets may be redistributed.
- Use clear scientific/educational caveats wherever simulations or graphics are illustrative. Do not market a toy visualization as an instrument, diagnostic tool or accurate predictive model.
- Validate imported data formats, sizes, paths and schema versions; avoid executing untrusted user code except in the specifically constrained Shader Studio design.

### Content and App Store review checklist
- Document why each permission is necessary and the exact UI path requesting it.
- Provide privacy policy and required app data disclosures based on actual telemetry/storage behavior, not sample text.
- Check all media and code redistribution rights, attribution and trademark rules before the storefront submission.
- Keep claims in marketing and screenshots aligned to implemented working features and measured/attributed facts.

## 14. Xcode project, build, and CI commands

After selecting XcodeGen and writing a real `project.yml` during Phase 0/1, these are executable examples **from this app repo**. Scheme and target names must be confirmed with `xcodebuild -list`; do not assume VisualCore has a particular SPM product name.

```bash
# Use XcodeGen only if project.yml was adopted and reviewed
xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -list -project VisualProgrammingLab.xcodeproj
xcodebuild -project VisualProgrammingLab.xcodeproj -scheme VisualProgrammingLab -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
xcrun simctl list devices available
SIMULATOR_UDID="$(python3 scripts/select_simulator.py)"
test -n "$SIMULATOR_UDID" || { echo "No available simulator"; exit 1; }
xcodebuild -project VisualProgrammingLab.xcodeproj -scheme VisualProgrammingLab -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIMULATOR_UDID" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test
python3 scripts/check_repo.py
```

If the repo uses an `.xcworkspace`, SwiftPM-generated project or a different scheme, inspect it and replace these paths; the test commands above do not constitute successful execution here. Build/sign/archive and test native ANGLE/Metal rendering on macOS with Xcode and a physical device.

### Minimal Python repository audit script

Create `scripts/check_repo.py` during the first phase. It should verify presence of essential architecture documents and app-owned shaders, then print the pinned VisualCore version using an actual resolved dependency file. Do not automatically download code or modify an upstream checkout.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import sys
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
required = ["CLAUDE.md", "docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md"]
missing = [name for name in required if not (root / name).is_file()]
for path in missing:
    print(f"MISSING: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
if missing:
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("Repository guidance and integration contract are present")
```

### Portable Python 3 simulator selection helper

Save as `scripts/select_simulator.py`; it reads `xcrun simctl` JSON and chooses a booted iOS simulator first, otherwise an available iPhone simulator. This helper does not create or boot a device; select/boot one manually if no compatible runtime is installed.

```python
import json
import subprocess
import sys
output = subprocess.check_output(
    ["xcrun", "simctl", "list", "devices", "available", "-j"], text=True)
data = json.loads(output)
devices = [device for runtime, group in data.get("devices", {}).items()
           if "iOS" in runtime for device in group
           if device.get("isAvailable", True) and "iPhone" in device.get("name", "")]
device = next((d for d in devices if d.get("state") == "Booted"),
              devices[0] if devices else None)
if device is None:
    sys.exit("No available iPhone simulator. Check Xcode runtimes.")
print(device["udid"])
```

### Minimal XcodeGen target layout

For a fresh repo, an initial `project.yml` can be generated with the following app-only starter; replace deployment target and bundle ID with validated project values, then add local package products only after the VisualCore audit.

```yaml
name: VisualProgrammingLab
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.example.visualcore
targets:
  VisualProgrammingLab:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    deploymentTarget: "17.0"   # proposal, verify supported OS
    sources:
      - Apps/VisualProgrammingLab
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.visualcore.visual-programming-lab
```

Install XcodeGen through its official distribution if not already available, verify `xcodegen --version`, and run `xcodegen generate` only after this file and target source exist. Avoid storing unreviewed private package tokens in `project.yml` or CI.

### Suggested macOS GitHub Actions job (create after actual build validation)

```yaml
name: iOS CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Verify Python and repository artifacts
        run: python3 scripts/check_repo.py
      - name: Inspect Xcode and app schemes
        run: xcodebuild -list -project VisualProgrammingLab.xcodeproj
      - name: Build simulator target
        run: xcodebuild -project VisualProgrammingLab.xcodeproj -scheme VisualProgrammingLab -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Pin CI action revisions and the Xcode version according to your organization’s supply-chain rules; add simulator unit tests and any authenticated VisualCore package fetch only after configuration is proven to work. CI on macOS does not substitute for physical GPU regression testing.

## 15. Acceptance criteria and definition of done

A first-release candidate is acceptable only when **all** of the following can be demonstrated:

- [ ] MVP-01: Typed node graph for scalar, color, texture and time values.
- [ ] MVP-02: Initial node library: Time, Constant, Noise, Gradient, Mix, Blur, Output.
- [ ] MVP-03: Touch graph canvas with wire routing, zoom and selection.
- [ ] MVP-04: Cycle detection and clear invalid-connection feedback.
- [ ] MVP-05: Preview renderer that compiles/translates a bounded acyclic graph.
- [ ] MVP-06: Versioned graph persistence with migration hooks.
- [ ] Standalone app uses public audited VisualCore APIs and shared ANGLE/Metal path, not ProjectM-specific engine internals.
- [ ] Render-state serializations are versioned, validated, and safe after background/resume and renderer reset.
- [ ] Native UI is usable with accessibility features; reduced motion and quality controls behave as stated.
- [ ] Domain and integration test cases in §11 pass; unresolved errors are documented, not marked passing.
- [ ] At least one physical device run with recorded build/OS/device metadata validates actual GPU behavior.
- [ ] No unsupported privacy, scientific or platform capability claims remain in the product UI or listing.
- [ ] Bundled third-party code, shaders, assets, educational facts and sounds have reviewed license/source records.
- [ ] Build from a clean macOS checkout succeeds and the final PR contains exact verification commands and results.
- [ ] Any VisualCore changes have their own upstream PR plus before/after ProjectM reference regression evidence.

## 16. Ordered next actions

1. Create a new `VisualProgrammingLab` app repo and initialize the Claude/Spec Kit Python variant (commands in §7).
2. Perform read-only VisualCore package/render-host inspection; resolve actual public APIs and upstream gaps.
3. Save the constitution and app-specific design decisions in reviewed repository artifacts.
4. Run Phase 00 through all eight quality gates; complete any upstream VisualCore feature as a separate, reviewed change.
5. Implement Phase 01 graph schema and type-checking fixtures as the smallest testable vertical slice.
6. Continue the remaining phases one by one; compare every release claim against the acceptance matrix.
7. Archive evidence from physical device validation and review the release privacy/license checklist.

# Graphics Benchmark Lab
## iOS application architecture and Spec Kit + Claude Code implementation manual

**Concept #24 of 25** | **Category:** Developer and creator tools | **Proposed app/repository target:** `GraphicsBenchmarkLab`
**Planning status:** proposed implementation guide; not proof of an existing application or released VisualCore package. **Source:** `AppsBrainstorm.md` catalog item 24; `README.md` VisualCore architecture and Spec Kit strategy.
**Rendering invariant:** reuse the existing ProjectM-proven OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal infrastructure exposed by VisualCore. Never create a duplicate EGL/ANGLE backend or link ProjectM engine internals into this independent app.

---

## 1. Executive summary and source traceability

A transparent, repeatable suite of GPU graphics workloads and instrumentation with measured-device caveats.

### Original brainstorm concept

> A technical application for testing GPU performance, shader throughput, fill rate, rendering latency, and memory behavior across Apple devices.

**VisualCore capabilities listed in the brainstorm:**
- GPU timing
- Diagnostics
- Profiling
- Benchmark scenes
- Device and configuration reporting

**Original product opportunity:** A developer-oriented utility and an internal performance-regression tool. Benchmark results must clearly distinguish repeatable measurements from device- and thermal-state-dependent observations.

**Recommended product hypothesis:** A carefully scoped, offline-capable first release can demonstrate a distinct graphics workload and validate reusable VisualCore APIs. Test this hypothesis with a functioning vertical slice before expanding content or monetization.

## 2. Product contract and scope

### Primary audiences
- iOS graphics engineers
- Framework maintainers verifying regressions
- Technically curious users comparing their own devices

### End-to-end user journeys
1. **Journey 1:** Choose fill-rate stress scene and fixed preset.
2. **Journey 2:** Run a structured warmup and measurement session.
3. **Journey 3:** Review fps/frame-time distribution and save result with device and test metadata.

### Version 0.1 feature contract
1. **Feature 01:** Repeatable baseline scenes: textured quads, shader ALU stress and particles. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
2. **Feature 02:** Warmup, controlled measurement and cooldown phases. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
3. **Feature 03:** Frame-time percentile, CPU submit time and optional supported GPU timer metrics. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
4. **Feature 04:** Device/OS/build/quality/thermal-context report with provenance. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
5. **Feature 05:** Results export as versioned JSON or CSV. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
6. **Feature 06:** In-app explanation of benchmark limits and variability. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.

### Explicit non-goals
- Ranking all devices from single run as scientific truth
- GPU timer claims without supported extension/profiler
- Collecting private hardware identifiers or automatic uploads

### Later-stage ideas, not MVP commitments
- Trend charts and local run comparison
- Automated CI performance probe with dedicated devices
- Optional anonymized opt-in result sharing after privacy review

## 3. UX blueprint

The first launch should reach a meaningful working graphic or educational interaction without requiring an account. Use SwiftUI for navigation, settings, labels and accessibility; host VisualCore rendering in a verified UIView/UIViewRepresentable integration that owns no duplicate GPU lifecycle.

**Proposed screen inventory** (adapt to the app-specific flows above):
| Screen | Responsibility | Concrete behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Home / gallery | Start without setup | Curated Graphics Benchmark Lab example, recent scene and explicit entry point |
| Interactive scene | Primary VisualCore rendering surface | Touch and app-state changes mapped into validated domain commands |
| Inspector | Controls and explanations | Show effective parameter values, reset and valid ranges |
| Library / files | Persistence where relevant | Open, duplicate, save, import/export only via permitted system APIs |
| Settings / help | Quality, accessibility, privacy | Explain input permissions, limitations, credits and renderer fallback |

**Interaction design rules:** screen gestures must have a deterministic domain meaning; rendering can interpolate but cannot silently change persisted state. State-affecting controls should be testable independent of the GPU. All critical feedback must remain legible without bloom, color alone, or animation.

### State transitions to implement
```text
uninitialized → loading-assets → ready → active
                                  ↔ paused / backgrounded
                                  ↘ editing / exporting (if supported)
any GPU state → renderer-lost → recover-resources → ready
any document state → validation-error → recoverable-message
```

Do not upload application/scene state to a server by default. If future features introduce accounts, cloud sync or sharing, write a new privacy and threat-model spec before implementation.

## 4. Architecture: VisualCore consumer, not renderer fork

```text
GraphicsBenchmarkLab SwiftUI app (navigation, accessibility, preferences)
    ↓ commands / immutable snapshots
GraphicsBenchmarkLabCore (domain rules, models, persistence schemas, validation)
    ↓ render-state snapshot; never raw SwiftUI bindings
GraphicsBenchmarkLabRendering (scene adapter, shaders, asset IDs, pass descriptions)
    ↓ public APIs discovered in the real VisualCore checkout
VisualCore runtime, shaders, effects, scenes, inputs, diagnostics
    ↓ shared EGL/context/render host as audited
Existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal implementation
    ↓
iOS device GPU and display
```

**Ownership policy:** The app owns its content, mathematical rules, domain schema, UI and business logic. VisualCore owns generic graphics infrastructure. `Coastrnaut/projectm-ios` remains VisualCore's pinned reference submodule, not an app dependency. Any VisualCore API needed but not present must be proposed upstream with a test and an API contract; do not stub an imaginary package into production.

### Contracts and threading
- A domain coordinator produces immutable render snapshots or bounded commands; presentation does not mutate simulation truth.
- The VisualCore render host controls the EGL context, resource lifetime, presentation and the required render thread/queue; all GL work obeys that ownership.
- Native SwiftUI overlays remain separate from shader drawing where legibility, hit-testing and VoiceOver need native controls.
- On scene resize, background, memory warning or renderer reset, reallocate GPU resources from versioned CPU state rather than persisting raw GL handles.
- Shaders are treated as bundled, versioned assets unless the specific product explicitly supports user-authored GLSL with additional guards.

### Application-specific components
- **`BenchmarkCatalog.swift`**: data storage, schema validation, assets or export; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`BenchmarkRunner.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`FrameMetricsCollector.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`TimingCapabilityProbe.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`Statistics.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`ResultsStore.swift`**: data storage, schema validation, assets or export; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`BenchmarkSceneRenderer.swift`**: renderer-facing render orchestration and GPU pass bindings; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.

- Keep all feature specs under `specs/` created by Spec Kit; allow its installed release to determine feature numbering and active feature selection.

## 6. Domain model, algorithms and rendering design

### Versioned domain schemas (proposed types)
| Type | Field contract / required invariants |
|---|---|
| `BenchmarkCase` | `BenchmarkCase(id, version, shaderHash, drawCount, targetResolution, resourceBudget)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `BenchmarkRun` | `BenchmarkRun(id, deviceModel, osVersion, appBuild, ANGLEBuild, startedAt, duration, state)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `FrameMeasurement` | `FrameMeasurement(frameIndex, cpuMs, presentMs, gpuMsOptional, dropped)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `Summary` | `Summary(p50, p95, p99, warmupExcluded, sampleCount, qualityFlags)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |

Use explicit units and coordinate spaces in type names or documentation. Reject NaN/Inf, invalid counts, truncated files, unreasonable allocations and unsupported versions where applicable. Canonical storage should be pure data; expensive buffers can be reconstructed.

### Algorithm and correctness decisions
1. Build fixed deterministic scenes with versioned assets and recorded config.
2. Partition warmup from measurement and use monotonic clocks.
3. Only report GPU time if implementation confirms accurate, non-disjoint timing support; never substitute CPU timings with GPU label.
4. Record thermal state/visibility/charger context as available and mark any comparability caveats.
5. Use statistical distributions, not just average FPS.

### App-specific render sequence
1. **Stage 1:** Load case and verify config/assets.
2. **Stage 2:** Warm up renderer under fixed workload.
3. **Stage 3:** Capture frame timings with supported instrumentation during measured interval.
4. **Stage 4:** Persist raw samples, compute percentiles and display caveated report with export.

### Rendering lifecycle and frame budget
- Create resources only after VisualCore signals a valid owning EGL context; release/recreate on context loss and size changes.
- Separate fixed-step simulation, event handling, visual animation time and wall time when the product uses more than one.
- Treat device tier as policy data: resolution scale, effect counts, iterations and object count may change; domain correctness and user state may not.
- Validate framebuffer completeness, shader compile/link results, texture format support and GPU resource handles before presenting a frame.
- Record frame pacing, app-owned CPU time, allocation counts and renderer recovery on a real device before selecting release targets.

### Required capability audit against VisualCore
- **GPU timing** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Diagnostics** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Profiling** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Benchmark scenes** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Device and configuration reporting** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.

> **Domain-specific engineering rule:** Measurement provenance is a feature requirement; do not rank devices or claim rigorous GPU throughput from unsupported timing sources.

## 7. Local environment and reproducible bootstrap

**Prerequisites:** macOS and Xcode for iOS build, signing, Simulator and physical-device tests; Git, Python 3, `uv`, and Claude Code CLI. Windows can prepare specifications and source but cannot validate the iOS rendering path without a macOS builder. Follow current vendor instructions for installation; verify tool versions rather than assuming they exist.

**Terminal on macOS — commands to create this app repository:**
```bash
mkdir GraphicsBenchmarkLab && cd GraphicsBenchmarkLab
git init -b main
git --version
python3 --version
uv --version
claude --version
uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git
specify version
specify init --help
specify init --here --integration claude --script py
specify check
git status --short
claude
```

Initialize Spec Kit **once** in a newly created repository. In a non-empty existing repo, commit/backup first and inspect `specify init --help`; `--force` may merge/overwrite managed files and must not be run blindly. Never run Spec Kit initialization inside the VisualCore or ProjectM submodule from an app repo.

**Current Claude Code integration:** Spec Kit creates `.claude/skills/speckit-<command>/SKILL.md`; invoke skills in Claude chat using **hyphens**, e.g. `/speckit-specify`, not the dotted spelling used in some generic documentation. Confirm actual skills with `find .claude/skills -name SKILL.md` and Claude `/help` because installed versions can differ. See official [Claude integration](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html).

**Terminal — verify a local VisualCore checkout without assuming package products:**
```bash
test -d ../VisualCore || { echo "Clone or locate the VisualCore repository beside this app first"; exit 1; }
git -C ../VisualCore status --short
find ../VisualCore -name Package.swift -not -path "*/.build/*" -print
git -C ../VisualCore submodule status
```

If `../VisualCore` does not yet provide a consumer package, create an upstream integration feature and stop at a no-op host skeleton. Do not invent `VisualCoreRenderer` product names or fake ANGLE integration code.

```text
Inspect the active Spec Kit tasks file. Implement only the next smallest dependency-complete task group. Before editing, list intended files, known VisualCore API contracts, test commands, and rollback steps. After editing, run tests and report actual results; do not claim device validation without device logs. Stop for review after this group.
```

Do not ask Claude to run all seven phases unattended. Spec Kit artifacts may expose architecture errors or rights/permission issues that materially change the following work. The Git baseline is reviewed per phase; commit evidence and tests in the application repository, and upstream patches separately.

## 11. Domain, renderer and UI verification matrix

| Layer | App-specific test | Evidence / gate |
|---|---|---|
| Pure domain model | Statistics p50/p95/p99 match fixture samples including edge cases | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Pure domain model | Unsupported GPU timer produces null, not fabricated zeros | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Measurement excludes warmup interval | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Identical case version and settings are stored with run | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Device or end-to-end | App background/thermal interruption flags a run as invalid/qualified | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Shared render lifecycle | Repeated renderer create, resize, background, resume, context recovery, release | Device log with no stale EGL/GL handles or persistent GPU memory growth |
| App UI and accessibility | First-session flow, disabled states, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver fallback | UI test + human review on representative iPhone and iPad |
| VisualCore regression | If VisualCore changes, ProjectM remains functional at pinned submodule commit | Existing ProjectM build/smoke log; any difference reviewed |

### Implementation-level fixtures
- Fixture 1: Statistics p50/p95/p99 match fixture samples including edge cases.
- Fixture 2: Unsupported GPU timer produces null, not fabricated zeros.
- Fixture 3: Measurement excludes warmup interval.
- Fixture 4: Identical case version and settings are stored with run.
- Fixture 5: App background/thermal interruption flags a run as invalid/qualified.

### Simulator and device separation
- CI/simulator: test domain math, model migration, document round trips, permission-denied paths, basic UI and reproducible app builds.
- Physical iPhone/iPad: validate ANGLE Metal path, shader compilation, context loss, high-refresh/low-refresh behavior, thermals, memory, inputs and real audio/device sensor routes if relevant.
- When tests depend on audio, sensors or input permissions, use synthetic fixtures in CI; do not silently substitute test signals for production sources.
- Store exact Xcode, iOS, device, VisualCore revision, ProjectM submodule revision, preset and test duration with performance reports.

## 12. Profiling plan, budgets and graceful fallback

Before specifying absolute fps, startup or memory targets, measure a baseline on the reference app and at least one representative device. Decide thresholds in a separate acceptance ADR; do not publish invented benchmark numbers.

- Define baseline per-device measurement windows and revisit after VisualCore changes.
- Record CPU/GPU measurement method and confidence.
- Limit stress durations and allow immediate stop.

**Telemetry only as local diagnostics by default:** record per-pass timing if genuinely supported, present interval, app-side CPU duration, memory and resource counts, scene configuration, chosen quality tier and build IDs. Make collection opt-in if data ever leaves the device. Never label CPU timings as GPU timings.

**Fallback policy:** keep the app usable when expensive shader passes fail or a device is below target capability: reduce resolution/passes, use a simpler scene, preserve user state, and display a recoverable explanation. When no VisualCore render host exists, ship a native UI placeholder only for internal integration testing—not a misleading App Store release.

## 13. Risks, privacy, science/platform constraints and licenses

### App-specific risk register
1. **Risk 1:** Thermal throttling and display refresh skew results—record context and repeat trials. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
2. **Risk 2:** GL timing extension availability uncertain—feature detect, avoid false GPU claims. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
3. **Risk 3:** Aggressive stress testing can overheat devices—bound duration and implement cooldown/stop. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.

### Cross-cutting obligations
- No private iOS APIs, undocumented system-level audio interception, automatic wallpaper changes or unsupported GPU access; test any requested platform capability against current public documentation.
- Apply least-privilege permission prompts, with useful demo/offline behavior for denied permissions. Document Photos, Files, microphone or audio rights only where that app actually needs them.
- Maintain licenses for ANGLE, VisualCore, ProjectM reference code and all bundled shaders, meshes, textures, fonts, datasets, sound and educational copy. Do not assume upstream assets may be redistributed.
- Use clear scientific/educational caveats wherever simulations or graphics are illustrative. Do not market a toy visualization as an instrument, diagnostic tool or accurate predictive model.
- Validate imported data formats, sizes, paths and schema versions; avoid executing untrusted user code except in the specifically constrained Shader Studio design.

### Content and App Store review checklist
- Document why each permission is necessary and the exact UI path requesting it.
- Provide privacy policy and required app data disclosures based on actual telemetry/storage behavior, not sample text.
- Check all media and code redistribution rights, attribution and trademark rules before the storefront submission.
- Keep claims in marketing and screenshots aligned to implemented working features and measured/attributed facts.

## 14. Xcode project, build, and CI commands

After selecting XcodeGen and writing a real `project.yml` during Phase 0/1, these are executable examples **from this app repo**. Scheme and target names must be confirmed with `xcodebuild -list`; do not assume VisualCore has a particular SPM product name.

```bash
# Use XcodeGen only if project.yml was adopted and reviewed
xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -list -project GraphicsBenchmarkLab.xcodeproj
xcodebuild -project GraphicsBenchmarkLab.xcodeproj -scheme GraphicsBenchmarkLab -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
xcrun simctl list devices available
SIMULATOR_UDID="$(python3 scripts/select_simulator.py)"
test -n "$SIMULATOR_UDID" || { echo "No available simulator"; exit 1; }
xcodebuild -project GraphicsBenchmarkLab.xcodeproj -scheme GraphicsBenchmarkLab -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIMULATOR_UDID" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test
python3 scripts/check_repo.py
```

If the repo uses an `.xcworkspace`, SwiftPM-generated project or a different scheme, inspect it and replace these paths; the test commands above do not constitute successful execution here. Build/sign/archive and test native ANGLE/Metal rendering on macOS with Xcode and a physical device.

### Minimal Python repository audit script

Create `scripts/check_repo.py` during the first phase. It should verify presence of essential architecture documents and app-owned shaders, then print the pinned VisualCore version using an actual resolved dependency file. Do not automatically download code or modify an upstream checkout.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import sys
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
required = ["CLAUDE.md", "docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md"]
missing = [name for name in required if not (root / name).is_file()]
for path in missing:
    print(f"MISSING: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
if missing:
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("Repository guidance and integration contract are present")
```

### Portable Python 3 simulator selection helper

Save as `scripts/select_simulator.py`; it reads `xcrun simctl` JSON and chooses a booted iOS simulator first, otherwise an available iPhone simulator. This helper does not create or boot a device; select/boot one manually if no compatible runtime is installed.

```python
import json
import subprocess
import sys
output = subprocess.check_output(
    ["xcrun", "simctl", "list", "devices", "available", "-j"], text=True)
data = json.loads(output)
devices = [device for runtime, group in data.get("devices", {}).items()
           if "iOS" in runtime for device in group
           if device.get("isAvailable", True) and "iPhone" in device.get("name", "")]
device = next((d for d in devices if d.get("state") == "Booted"),
              devices[0] if devices else None)
if device is None:
    sys.exit("No available iPhone simulator. Check Xcode runtimes.")
print(device["udid"])
```

### Minimal XcodeGen target layout

For a fresh repo, an initial `project.yml` can be generated with the following app-only starter; replace deployment target and bundle ID with validated project values, then add local package products only after the VisualCore audit.

```yaml
name: GraphicsBenchmarkLab
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.example.visualcore
targets:
  GraphicsBenchmarkLab:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    deploymentTarget: "17.0"   # proposal, verify supported OS
    sources:
      - Apps/GraphicsBenchmarkLab
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.visualcore.graphics-benchmark-lab
```

Install XcodeGen through its official distribution if not already available, verify `xcodegen --version`, and run `xcodegen generate` only after this file and target source exist. Avoid storing unreviewed private package tokens in `project.yml` or CI.

### Suggested macOS GitHub Actions job (create after actual build validation)

```yaml
name: iOS CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Verify Python and repository artifacts
        run: python3 scripts/check_repo.py
      - name: Inspect Xcode and app schemes
        run: xcodebuild -list -project GraphicsBenchmarkLab.xcodeproj
      - name: Build simulator target
        run: xcodebuild -project GraphicsBenchmarkLab.xcodeproj -scheme GraphicsBenchmarkLab -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Pin CI action revisions and the Xcode version according to your organization’s supply-chain rules; add simulator unit tests and any authenticated VisualCore package fetch only after configuration is proven to work. CI on macOS does not substitute for physical GPU regression testing.

## 15. Acceptance criteria and definition of done

A first-release candidate is acceptable only when **all** of the following can be demonstrated:

- [ ] MVP-01: Repeatable baseline scenes: textured quads, shader ALU stress and particles.
- [ ] MVP-02: Warmup, controlled measurement and cooldown phases.
- [ ] MVP-03: Frame-time percentile, CPU submit time and optional supported GPU timer metrics.
- [ ] MVP-04: Device/OS/build/quality/thermal-context report with provenance.
- [ ] MVP-05: Results export as versioned JSON or CSV.
- [ ] MVP-06: In-app explanation of benchmark limits and variability.
- [ ] Standalone app uses public audited VisualCore APIs and shared ANGLE/Metal path, not ProjectM-specific engine internals.
- [ ] Render-state serializations are versioned, validated, and safe after background/resume and renderer reset.
- [ ] Native UI is usable with accessibility features; reduced motion and quality controls behave as stated.
- [ ] Domain and integration test cases in §11 pass; unresolved errors are documented, not marked passing.
- [ ] At least one physical device run with recorded build/OS/device metadata validates actual GPU behavior.
- [ ] No unsupported privacy, scientific or platform capability claims remain in the product UI or listing.
- [ ] Bundled third-party code, shaders, assets, educational facts and sounds have reviewed license/source records.
- [ ] Build from a clean macOS checkout succeeds and the final PR contains exact verification commands and results.
- [ ] Any VisualCore changes have their own upstream PR plus before/after ProjectM reference regression evidence.

## 16. Ordered next actions

1. Create a new `GraphicsBenchmarkLab` app repo and initialize the Claude/Spec Kit Python variant (commands in §7).
2. Perform read-only VisualCore package/render-host inspection; resolve actual public APIs and upstream gaps.
3. Save the constitution and app-specific design decisions in reviewed repository artifacts.
4. Run Phase 00 through all eight quality gates; complete any upstream VisualCore feature as a separate, reviewed change.
5. Implement Phase 01 measurement methodology and fixture statistics as the smallest testable vertical slice.
6. Continue the remaining phases one by one; compare every release claim against the acceptance matrix.
7. Archive evidence from physical device validation and review the release privacy/license checklist.

# Effects Composer
## iOS application architecture and Spec Kit + Claude Code implementation manual

**Concept #25 of 25** | **Category:** Developer and creator tools | **Proposed app/repository target:** `EffectsComposer`
**Planning status:** proposed implementation guide; not proof of an existing application or released VisualCore package. **Source:** `AppsBrainstorm.md` catalog item 25; `README.md` VisualCore architecture and Spec Kit strategy.
**Rendering invariant:** reuse the existing ProjectM-proven OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal infrastructure exposed by VisualCore. Never create a duplicate EGL/ANGLE backend or link ProjectM engine internals into this independent app.

---

## 1. Executive summary and source traceability

A visual effects-chain editor for building, previewing and exporting reusable shader looks.

### Original brainstorm concept

> A mobile effects editor where users combine shaders, color grading, distortion, blur, particles, and compositing effects.

**VisualCore capabilities listed in the brainstorm:**
- Render graph
- Framebuffer pipelines
- Shader library
- Effect parameters
- Preset serialization
- Offscreen rendering and export

**Original product opportunity:** A creative visual-effects application with reusable effect chains and shareable looks.

**Brainstorm initial ranking:** #10 of 25. This is a strategic first-pass judgment, not measured App Store demand or revenue.

**Recommended product hypothesis:** A carefully scoped, offline-capable first release can demonstrate a distinct graphics workload and validate reusable VisualCore APIs. Test this hypothesis with a functioning vertical slice before expanding content or monetization.

## 2. Product contract and scope

### Primary audiences
- Creative users modifying images and backgrounds
- Motion designers prototyping looks
- Developers testing render-pass composition

### End-to-end user journeys
1. **Journey 1:** Open built-in test image.
2. **Journey 2:** Add Blur → Color Grade → Distortion, reorder effects.
3. **Journey 3:** Adjust parameters, compare before/after and export a processed still.

### Version 0.1 feature contract
1. **Feature 01:** Linear chain editor with five built-in effects and bounded parameters. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
2. **Feature 02:** Editable reorder, enable/disable and immediate preview. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
3. **Feature 03:** Before/after compare and preset saves. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
4. **Feature 04:** Local image import via system picker with scoped access. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
5. **Feature 05:** Still export with dimension/format validation. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.
6. **Feature 06:** Controlled render target pooling and shader compile diagnostics. Acceptance requires an implemented behavior and a test or documented manual verification—not a screenshot mock.

### Explicit non-goals
- General video non-linear editor
- Arbitrary custom feedback loops or user code in MVP
- Batch importing cloud libraries without consent

### Later-stage ideas, not MVP commitments
- DAG editor with branches/masks and feedback semantics
- Supported video export and animated effects
- Export effects as validated VisualCore presets

## 3. UX blueprint

The first launch should reach a meaningful working graphic or educational interaction without requiring an account. Use SwiftUI for navigation, settings, labels and accessibility; host VisualCore rendering in a verified UIView/UIViewRepresentable integration that owns no duplicate GPU lifecycle.

**Proposed screen inventory** (adapt to the app-specific flows above):
| Screen | Responsibility | Concrete behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Home / gallery | Start without setup | Curated Effects Composer example, recent scene and explicit entry point |
| Interactive scene | Primary VisualCore rendering surface | Touch and app-state changes mapped into validated domain commands |
| Inspector | Controls and explanations | Show effective parameter values, reset and valid ranges |
| Library / files | Persistence where relevant | Open, duplicate, save, import/export only via permitted system APIs |
| Settings / help | Quality, accessibility, privacy | Explain input permissions, limitations, credits and renderer fallback |

**Interaction design rules:** screen gestures must have a deterministic domain meaning; rendering can interpolate but cannot silently change persisted state. State-affecting controls should be testable independent of the GPU. All critical feedback must remain legible without bloom, color alone, or animation.

### State transitions to implement
```text
uninitialized → loading-assets → ready → active
                                  ↔ paused / backgrounded
                                  ↘ editing / exporting (if supported)
any GPU state → renderer-lost → recover-resources → ready
any document state → validation-error → recoverable-message
```

Do not upload application/scene state to a server by default. If future features introduce accounts, cloud sync or sharing, write a new privacy and threat-model spec before implementation.

## 4. Architecture: VisualCore consumer, not renderer fork

```text
EffectsComposer SwiftUI app (navigation, accessibility, preferences)
    ↓ commands / immutable snapshots
EffectsComposerCore (domain rules, models, persistence schemas, validation)
    ↓ render-state snapshot; never raw SwiftUI bindings
EffectsComposerRendering (scene adapter, shaders, asset IDs, pass descriptions)
    ↓ public APIs discovered in the real VisualCore checkout
VisualCore runtime, shaders, effects, scenes, inputs, diagnostics
    ↓ shared EGL/context/render host as audited
Existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal implementation
    ↓
iOS device GPU and display
```

**Ownership policy:** The app owns its content, mathematical rules, domain schema, UI and business logic. VisualCore owns generic graphics infrastructure. `Coastrnaut/projectm-ios` remains VisualCore's pinned reference submodule, not an app dependency. Any VisualCore API needed but not present must be proposed upstream with a test and an API contract; do not stub an imaginary package into production.

### Contracts and threading
- A domain coordinator produces immutable render snapshots or bounded commands; presentation does not mutate simulation truth.
- The VisualCore render host controls the EGL context, resource lifetime, presentation and the required render thread/queue; all GL work obeys that ownership.
- Native SwiftUI overlays remain separate from shader drawing where legibility, hit-testing and VoiceOver need native controls.
- On scene resize, background, memory warning or renderer reset, reallocate GPU resources from versioned CPU state rather than persisting raw GL handles.
- Shaders are treated as bundled, versioned assets unless the specific product explicitly supports user-authored GLSL with additional guards.

### Application-specific components
- **`EffectChain.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`EffectRegistry.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`RenderPlanCompiler.swift`**: renderer-facing render orchestration and GPU pass bindings; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`ImageImportCoordinator.swift`**: data storage, schema validation, assets or export; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`EffectParameterEditor.swift`**: pure domain algorithms and behavior, covered by CPU unit fixtures; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`EffectsComposerRenderer.swift`**: renderer-facing render orchestration and GPU pass bindings; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
- **`ExportCoordinator.swift`**: data storage, schema validation, assets or export; implement the specific rules in §6 and make dependencies explicit.
