## 6. Domain model, algorithms and rendering design

### Versioned domain schemas (proposed types)
| Type | Field contract / required invariants |
|---|---|
| `EffectNode` | `EffectNode(id, kind, enabled, parameterMap, inputFormat, outputFormat)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `EffectChain` | `EffectChain(version, sourceRef, orderedNodes, outputSettings)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `ImageSource` | `ImageSource(id, pixelSize, colorSpace, accessPolicy)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |
| `RenderPlan` | `RenderPlan(passes, intermediateTargets, textureLifetimes, validationErrors)`. Validate on ingress; version persistent payloads and reject unsupported data safely. |

Use explicit units and coordinate spaces in type names or documentation. Reject NaN/Inf, invalid counts, truncated files, unreasonable allocations and unsupported versions where applicable. Canonical storage should be pure data; expensive buffers can be reconstructed.

### Algorithm and correctness decisions
1. Implement linear chain first, but represent each effect as typed input/output pass.
2. Validate supported texture formats, color space, dimensions and parameter ranges before graph compilation.
3. Ping-pong or pool intermediate FBO targets; no sampling currently attached output texture.
4. Preserve unprocessed source for compare, and decouple preview resolution from full-quality export.

### App-specific render sequence
1. **Stage 1:** Import allowed image or bundled fixture.
2. **Stage 2:** Decode source, validate color and texture requirements.
3. **Stage 3:** Compile effect chain to ordered VisualCore passes and allocate temporary targets.
4. **Stage 4:** Composite preview/before-after; offscreen re-run and encode output at export resolution.

### Rendering lifecycle and frame budget
- Create resources only after VisualCore signals a valid owning EGL context; release/recreate on context loss and size changes.
- Separate fixed-step simulation, event handling, visual animation time and wall time when the product uses more than one.
- Treat device tier as policy data: resolution scale, effect counts, iterations and object count may change; domain correctness and user state may not.
- Validate framebuffer completeness, shader compile/link results, texture format support and GPU resource handles before presenting a frame.
- Record frame pacing, app-owned CPU time, allocation counts and renderer recovery on a real device before selecting release targets.

### Required capability audit against VisualCore
- **Render graph** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Framebuffer pipelines** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Shader library** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Effect parameters** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Preset serialization** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.
- **Offscreen rendering and export** — locate an existing package/API/contract and a working example in VisualCore; mark `available`, `requires adaptation`, or `upstream gap` in `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md`.

> **Domain-specific engineering rule:** Keep MVP graph a linear, acyclic pipeline; preserve the ability to add a typed DAG later without promising arbitrary node semantics.

## 7. Local environment and reproducible bootstrap

**Prerequisites:** macOS and Xcode for iOS build, signing, Simulator and physical-device tests; Git, Python 3, `uv`, and Claude Code CLI. Windows can prepare specifications and source but cannot validate the iOS rendering path without a macOS builder. Follow current vendor instructions for installation; verify tool versions rather than assuming they exist.

**Terminal on macOS — commands to create this app repository:**
```bash
mkdir EffectsComposer && cd EffectsComposer
git init -b main
git --version
python3 --version
uv --version
claude --version
uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git
specify version
specify init --help
specify init --here --integration claude --script py
specify check
git status --short
claude
```

Initialize Spec Kit **once** in a newly created repository. In a non-empty existing repo, commit/backup first and inspect `specify init --help`; `--force` may merge/overwrite managed files and must not be run blindly. Never run Spec Kit initialization inside the VisualCore or ProjectM submodule from an app repo.

**Current Claude Code integration:** Spec Kit creates `.claude/skills/speckit-<command>/SKILL.md`; invoke skills in Claude chat using **hyphens**, e.g. `/speckit-specify`, not the dotted spelling used in some generic documentation. Confirm actual skills with `find .claude/skills -name SKILL.md` and Claude `/help` because installed versions can differ. See official [Claude integration](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html).

**Terminal — verify a local VisualCore checkout without assuming package products:**
```bash
test -d ../VisualCore || { echo "Clone or locate the VisualCore repository beside this app first"; exit 1; }
git -C ../VisualCore status --short
find ../VisualCore -name Package.swift -not -path "*/.build/*" -print
git -C ../VisualCore submodule status
```

If `../VisualCore` does not yet provide a consumer package, create an upstream integration feature and stop at a no-op host skeleton. Do not invent `VisualCoreRenderer` product names or fake ANGLE integration code.

```text
/speckit-constitution Define the constitution for Effects Composer. Build a standalone iOS/iPadOS VisualCore consumer, never a fork of projectm-ios. Reuse only audited VisualCore public APIs over the existing OpenGL ES→ANGLE→Metal integration. Domain rules and persisted files must be testable without GPU access. Keep the app offline-first, disclose permissions, use bounded GPU resources, support accessibility, record asset licenses, and prohibit unsupported scientific/platform claims. Require a ProjectM regression check whenever VisualCore is modified. Use Python 3 for repository automation; no PowerShell dependency. Implement only one approved Spec Kit phase at a time.
```

**Suggested root `CLAUDE.md` text** (create once; do not overwrite generated skill files):
```markdown
# Effects Composer — Claude Code Engineering Rules

- Product goal: A visual effects-chain editor for building, previewing and exporting reusable shader looks.
- Read `docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md` before editing graphics integration.
- VisualCore owns the graphics lifecycle; never create an independent ANGLE/EGL initialization path.
- Do not import ProjectM engine internals or duplicate third-party sources.
- Domain truth, deterministic tests and versioned persistence must not depend on GL contexts.
- Use Python scripts for repeatable source/schema/license validation.
- Request explicit approval before changing the adjacent VisualCore repository.
- Report uncertainty and platform limitations; do not invent APIs or test results.
- Complete Spec Kit clarify → plan → checklist → tasks → analyze before implementing a phase.
- Run relevant tests; log exact macOS/Xcode/device/VisualCore revisions used.
- Keep each PR bounded to one feature phase and document migration/rollback plan.
```

## 10. Bounded Claude execution and Git workflow

**Terminal:**
```bash
git status --short
git diff --check
git diff --stat
git add -A
git commit -m "feat: complete reviewed implementation phase"
git log -3 --oneline
```

**Claude Code chat, at every task boundary:**
```text
Inspect the active Spec Kit tasks file. Implement only the next smallest dependency-complete task group. Before editing, list intended files, known VisualCore API contracts, test commands, and rollback steps. After editing, run tests and report actual results; do not claim device validation without device logs. Stop for review after this group.
```

Do not ask Claude to run all seven phases unattended. Spec Kit artifacts may expose architecture errors or rights/permission issues that materially change the following work. The Git baseline is reviewed per phase; commit evidence and tests in the application repository, and upstream patches separately.

## 11. Domain, renderer and UI verification matrix

| Layer | App-specific test | Evidence / gate |
|---|---|---|
| Pure domain model | Effect order changes output and can be undone precisely | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Pure domain model | Disabled effect is equivalent to identity within tolerance | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Temporary targets never alias read/write in a pass | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| App↔VisualCore integration | Imported image color profile and orientation are handled correctly | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Device or end-to-end | Full-size export matches preview parameters within color/resampling tolerances | Automated fixture or documented physical-device observation with input/version captured |
| Shared render lifecycle | Repeated renderer create, resize, background, resume, context recovery, release | Device log with no stale EGL/GL handles or persistent GPU memory growth |
| App UI and accessibility | First-session flow, disabled states, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver fallback | UI test + human review on representative iPhone and iPad |
| VisualCore regression | If VisualCore changes, ProjectM remains functional at pinned submodule commit | Existing ProjectM build/smoke log; any difference reviewed |

### Implementation-level fixtures
- Fixture 1: Effect order changes output and can be undone precisely.
- Fixture 2: Disabled effect is equivalent to identity within tolerance.
- Fixture 3: Temporary targets never alias read/write in a pass.
- Fixture 4: Imported image color profile and orientation are handled correctly.
- Fixture 5: Full-size export matches preview parameters within color/resampling tolerances.

### Simulator and device separation
- CI/simulator: test domain math, model migration, document round trips, permission-denied paths, basic UI and reproducible app builds.
- Physical iPhone/iPad: validate ANGLE Metal path, shader compilation, context loss, high-refresh/low-refresh behavior, thermals, memory, inputs and real audio/device sensor routes if relevant.
- When tests depend on audio, sensors or input permissions, use synthetic fixtures in CI; do not silently substitute test signals for production sources.
- Store exact Xcode, iOS, device, VisualCore revision, ProjectM submodule revision, preset and test duration with performance reports.

## 12. Profiling plan, budgets and graceful fallback

Before specifying absolute fps, startup or memory targets, measure a baseline on the reference app and at least one representative device. Decide thresholds in a separate acceptance ADR; do not publish invented benchmark numbers.

- Measure per-effect GPU cost, FBO allocations and preview latency.
- Downscale live preview while preserving export path.
- Cache unchanged pass results based on source/effect hashes when justified.

**Telemetry only as local diagnostics by default:** record per-pass timing if genuinely supported, present interval, app-side CPU duration, memory and resource counts, scene configuration, chosen quality tier and build IDs. Make collection opt-in if data ever leaves the device. Never label CPU timings as GPU timings.

**Fallback policy:** keep the app usable when expensive shader passes fail or a device is below target capability: reduce resolution/passes, use a simpler scene, preserve user state, and display a recoverable explanation. When no VisualCore render host exists, ship a native UI placeholder only for internal integration testing—not a misleading App Store release.

## 13. Risks, privacy, science/platform constraints and licenses

### App-specific risk register
1. **Risk 1:** Color-space mistakes create wrong output—explicit linear/sRGB pass boundaries. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
2. **Risk 2:** Large images exceed texture limits—query/cap or tile. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.
3. **Risk 3:** Intermediate render targets can grow without bound—lifetime analysis and fixed pool. Document owner, verification method, and a release blocker condition in `docs/decisions/`.

### Cross-cutting obligations
- No private iOS APIs, undocumented system-level audio interception, automatic wallpaper changes or unsupported GPU access; test any requested platform capability against current public documentation.
- Apply least-privilege permission prompts, with useful demo/offline behavior for denied permissions. Document Photos, Files, microphone or audio rights only where that app actually needs them.
- Maintain licenses for ANGLE, VisualCore, ProjectM reference code and all bundled shaders, meshes, textures, fonts, datasets, sound and educational copy. Do not assume upstream assets may be redistributed.
- Use clear scientific/educational caveats wherever simulations or graphics are illustrative. Do not market a toy visualization as an instrument, diagnostic tool or accurate predictive model.
- Validate imported data formats, sizes, paths and schema versions; avoid executing untrusted user code except in the specifically constrained Shader Studio design.

### Content and App Store review checklist
- Document why each permission is necessary and the exact UI path requesting it.
- Provide privacy policy and required app data disclosures based on actual telemetry/storage behavior, not sample text.
- Check all media and code redistribution rights, attribution and trademark rules before the storefront submission.
- Keep claims in marketing and screenshots aligned to implemented working features and measured/attributed facts.

## 14. Xcode project, build, and CI commands

After selecting XcodeGen and writing a real `project.yml` during Phase 0/1, these are executable examples **from this app repo**. Scheme and target names must be confirmed with `xcodebuild -list`; do not assume VisualCore has a particular SPM product name.

```bash
# Use XcodeGen only if project.yml was adopted and reviewed
xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -list -project EffectsComposer.xcodeproj
xcodebuild -project EffectsComposer.xcodeproj -scheme EffectsComposer -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
xcrun simctl list devices available
SIMULATOR_UDID="$(python3 scripts/select_simulator.py)"
test -n "$SIMULATOR_UDID" || { echo "No available simulator"; exit 1; }
xcodebuild -project EffectsComposer.xcodeproj -scheme EffectsComposer -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIMULATOR_UDID" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test
python3 scripts/check_repo.py
```

If the repo uses an `.xcworkspace`, SwiftPM-generated project or a different scheme, inspect it and replace these paths; the test commands above do not constitute successful execution here. Build/sign/archive and test native ANGLE/Metal rendering on macOS with Xcode and a physical device.

### Minimal Python repository audit script

Create `scripts/check_repo.py` during the first phase. It should verify presence of essential architecture documents and app-owned shaders, then print the pinned VisualCore version using an actual resolved dependency file. Do not automatically download code or modify an upstream checkout.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import sys
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
required = ["CLAUDE.md", "docs/architecture/visualcore-contract.md"]
missing = [name for name in required if not (root / name).is_file()]
for path in missing:
    print(f"MISSING: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
if missing:
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("Repository guidance and integration contract are present")
```

### Portable Python 3 simulator selection helper

Save as `scripts/select_simulator.py`; it reads `xcrun simctl` JSON and chooses a booted iOS simulator first, otherwise an available iPhone simulator. This helper does not create or boot a device; select/boot one manually if no compatible runtime is installed.

```python
import json
import subprocess
import sys
output = subprocess.check_output(
    ["xcrun", "simctl", "list", "devices", "available", "-j"], text=True)
data = json.loads(output)
devices = [device for runtime, group in data.get("devices", {}).items()
           if "iOS" in runtime for device in group
           if device.get("isAvailable", True) and "iPhone" in device.get("name", "")]
device = next((d for d in devices if d.get("state") == "Booted"),
              devices[0] if devices else None)
if device is None:
    sys.exit("No available iPhone simulator. Check Xcode runtimes.")
print(device["udid"])
```

### Minimal XcodeGen target layout

For a fresh repo, an initial `project.yml` can be generated with the following app-only starter; replace deployment target and bundle ID with validated project values, then add local package products only after the VisualCore audit.

```yaml
name: EffectsComposer
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.example.visualcore
targets:
  EffectsComposer:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    deploymentTarget: "17.0"   # proposal, verify supported OS
    sources:
      - Apps/EffectsComposer
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.visualcore.effects-composer
```

Install XcodeGen through its official distribution if not already available, verify `xcodegen --version`, and run `xcodegen generate` only after this file and target source exist. Avoid storing unreviewed private package tokens in `project.yml` or CI.

### Suggested macOS GitHub Actions job (create after actual build validation)

```yaml
name: iOS CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Verify Python and repository artifacts
        run: python3 scripts/check_repo.py
      - name: Inspect Xcode and app schemes
        run: xcodebuild -list -project EffectsComposer.xcodeproj
      - name: Build simulator target
        run: xcodebuild -project EffectsComposer.xcodeproj -scheme EffectsComposer -destination "generic/platform=iOS Simulator" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

Pin CI action revisions and the Xcode version according to your organization’s supply-chain rules; add simulator unit tests and any authenticated VisualCore package fetch only after configuration is proven to work. CI on macOS does not substitute for physical GPU regression testing.

## 15. Acceptance criteria and definition of done

A first-release candidate is acceptable only when **all** of the following can be demonstrated:

- [ ] MVP-01: Linear chain editor with five built-in effects and bounded parameters.
- [ ] MVP-02: Editable reorder, enable/disable and immediate preview.
- [ ] MVP-03: Before/after compare and preset saves.
- [ ] MVP-04: Local image import via system picker with scoped access.
- [ ] MVP-05: Still export with dimension/format validation.
- [ ] MVP-06: Controlled render target pooling and shader compile diagnostics.
- [ ] Standalone app uses public audited VisualCore APIs and shared ANGLE/Metal path, not ProjectM-specific engine internals.
- [ ] Render-state serializations are versioned, validated, and safe after background/resume and renderer reset.
- [ ] Native UI is usable with accessibility features; reduced motion and quality controls behave as stated.
- [ ] Domain and integration test cases in §11 pass; unresolved errors are documented, not marked passing.
- [ ] At least one physical device run with recorded build/OS/device metadata validates actual GPU behavior.
- [ ] No unsupported privacy, scientific or platform capability claims remain in the product UI or listing.
- [ ] Bundled third-party code, shaders, assets, educational facts and sounds have reviewed license/source records.
- [ ] Build from a clean macOS checkout succeeds and the final PR contains exact verification commands and results.
- [ ] Any VisualCore changes have their own upstream PR plus before/after ProjectM reference regression evidence.

## 16. Ordered next actions

1. Create a new `EffectsComposer` app repo and initialize the Claude/Spec Kit Python variant (commands in §7).
2. Perform read-only VisualCore package/render-host inspection; resolve actual public APIs and upstream gaps.
3. Save the constitution and app-specific design decisions in reviewed repository artifacts.
4. Run Phase 00 through all eight quality gates; complete any upstream VisualCore feature as a separate, reviewed change.
5. Implement Phase 01 effect definitions and render contracts as the smallest testable vertical slice.
6. Continue the remaining phases one by one; compare every release claim against the acceptance matrix.
7. Archive evidence from physical device validation and review the release privacy/license checklist.

# VisualCore — 25 standalone iOS app implementation manuals

These Markdown files expand the 25 concepts in the supplied `AppsBrainstorm.md` using the architecture constraints in its companion VisualCore `README.md`.

**Important:** These are detailed **implementation plans**, not completed repositories, tested apps, or verified new VisualCore APIs. They use the existing ProjectM / ANGLE / Metal foundation by consuming VisualCore as an independent framework.

**Spec Kit command note:** The current Claude Code integration uses `/speckit-<command>` skills; `specify init --here --integration claude --script py` selects Claude and Python helpers. Verify the installed release before running commands.

## Recommended use

1. Complete the read-only VisualCore audit and publish an actual, audited client integration before writing product-specific EGL/ANGLE code.
2. Start with one app that genuinely exercises the intended shared capability. The brainstorm identifies a VisualCore Studio experience as a recommended flagship; the dedicated Generative Art Studio plan is an appropriate narrow first vertical slice.
3. Keep each app as a consumer repository or as an explicitly approved app target in a monorepo. The individual plans assume a separate app repo with a local `../VisualCore` development checkout and ultimately a pinned package dependency.
4. Initialize Spec Kit once per new repository, generate and review feature artifacts, implement only bounded task groups, and validate on a physical iOS device.
5. Maintain independent content license, privacy, accessibility and evidence records for each app.

## Shared technical rules

- Preserve existing OpenGL ES through ANGLE to Metal. No duplicate render backend.
- Do not link unrelated applications against ProjectM internals; ProjectM is VisualCore’s pinned reference consumer.
- VisualCore API/package names are provisional until repository audit.
- Build and device graphics QA require macOS/Xcode.
- Unsupported other-app system audio capture, automatic live wallpaper installation, and unverified scientific or GPU precision claims are explicitly out of scope.
- The app-specific documentation includes Python automation examples, not PowerShell scripts.

## Source and command documentation

- Original supplied sources: `AppsBrainstorm.md` and `README.md` (not duplicated in this archive).
- Existing reference: https://github.com/Coastrnaut/projectm-ios
- Spec Kit: https://github.com/github/spec-kit
- Claude integration: https://github.github.com/spec-kit/integrations/claude.html
- Spec Kit CLI: https://github.github.com/spec-kit/reference/core.html

# ProjectM-iOS — agent guide

iPhone/iPad audio visualizer built on the ProjectM engine. Work follows GitHub Spec Kit:
the governing documents are `.specify/memory/constitution.md` and
`specs/001-ios-projectm-visualizer/` (spec, plan, research, data-model, contracts, quickstart,
tasks). `README.md` is background guidance; the constitution and spec win when they differ.

## Rules that are easy to break

- **Public Apple APIs only.** No private APIs, `dlsym`/`dlopen`, ReplayKit, or capture workarounds.
  `python3 scripts/check_compliance.py` enforces this and runs in CI on every push.
- **No compatibility claims without evidence.** A source "works" only with a CaptureLab diagnostics
  export from a physical device showing non-silent audio (FR-031). Simulator results and
  screenshots are never evidence. Never write that Spotify, Apple Music, etc. work.
- **Signing is manual.** Never commit or change signing teams, certificates, or profiles.
- **Keep the iPad A16 (D3) on iPadOS 26.5.** It is the only device covering the iOS 26 path.
- **Report honestly.** If a build or test could not run on this host, say so ("pending macOS",
  "pending device"). Mark a task `[X]` in tasks.md only when its acceptance criterion was verified,
  and say how.
- `Vendor/projectM` is pinned to the owner's fork (`Coastrnaut/projectm`, branch `ios`; Constitution
  VIII v1.1.0). Engine changes are made on that branch only as upstream-ready commits, each logged
  in `docs/projectm-patches.md` and meant for an upstream PR; then the pin moves (ADR-0004).
- `Vendor/angle` is the owner's fork of ANGLE (`Coastrnaut/angle`, branch `ios`, shallow; ADR-0004).
  `gclient sync` puts about 12 GB of dependencies inside it (gitignored). Never delete or move it;
  scripts write only to `Build/ANGLEFrameworks` (macOS volumes are case-insensitive).

## Working with agents (owner preference, 2026-11-08)

- **No multi-agent requirement.** Use agents only when they clearly help, and run **at most 10
  agents at once** in total (all workflows and background subagents together).
- **Limits:**
  - One writer per repo file. Agents write to scratch files, copies, or worktrees; the main session
    applies their output (especially tasks.md, spec.md, project.yml, and the contracts).
  - An agent's report is not evidence. Verify it (build, test, read the diff) before marking a task
    `[X]`.
  - Builds and simulator runs share one Mac: agents read, review, and type-check; only a few lanes
    build or run tests.
  - CI minutes on GitHub's standard runners are free since the repo went public (2026-11-09); still
    push finished work, not every step.
  - Agents cannot do device tasks or owner decisions, and no agent may start work that the Stage 1
    gate blocks.

## Where things stand (2026-11-08)

- **Stage 1 is complete: T056 recorded "go" on 2026-11-09** (`docs/test-reports/compatibility-report.md`,
  Stage Decision). No source is claimed to work (none rated; Gates 1-2 waived).
- **Plan Phase B is complete; the owner accepted the Plan B exit on 2026-11-09.** T057-T061
  (Normalizer, normalized ring, `CaptureManager.normalizedOutput`), T062 (signposts; points
  accepted for delivery and residency, residency trace moved to T114), T063 on D1 (no allocations
  or lock-wait syscalls in any audio callback; CPU 7.4%, 3-minute run by owner ruling). Next is
  Plan Phase C (engine build and render proof, T064-T079 plus T114).
- **Plan Phase C is complete and Gate 3 passed on 2026-11-09** (T079): ADR-0003 accepts Option B,
  the engine on ANGLE's Metal backend (`Packages/ANGLERendering`, `Vendor/angle` = the owner's
  ANGLE fork). Engine: `Vendor/projectM` at the owner's fork commit `c88894e` (four iOS patches,
  `docs/projectm-patches.md`). Device evidence from RendererLab sweeps on D1-D3
  (`docs/test-reports/performance.md`, `docs/test-reports/exports/rendererlab/`); owner rulings: no
  10-minute sessions, no quality tiers or flash-limiter measurement for Gate 3. Next: Phase D (US4,
  T080 onward); T114 done with projectM-iOS.
- Phase D started 2026-11-09: `projectM-iOS` (project.yml) runs notice → chooser → full-screen ANGLE
  visualizer with controls; T080, T082, T083, T085, T086, US5 T088-T091, US6 T094-T096 and US7 T098-T100 done (T081, T093: red run not recorded); T081 (red run not recorded) and T084
  (FR-089 on D1/D2) open; T087 needs the devices and a 240 fps camera. The app's signing team is set
  by hand in Xcode (or in the gitignored `Configs/Signing.local.xcconfig`). 2026-11-10: T101 done
  (SC-009 on D1 and D3), SC-007 and SC-015 measured; T102 not required, Gate 4 waived (owner
  ruling). Phase E (2026-11-10): T103, T104 (Reduce flashing on D1: median 1.21 ms, max 1.55 ms),
  T106, T107, T108 (privacy review on D1, zero violations), T109 (ADR-0005 final "go", owner

## Commands

```bash
python3 scripts/test_scripts.py          # script tests (any OS)
python3 scripts/validate_docs.py         # spec cross-references
python3 scripts/check_compliance.py      # constitution rules
python3 scripts/verify_environment.py    # toolchain pins (macOS)
python3 scripts/check_capturelab_export.py --json <export> --expect none   # check a device export
python3 scripts/make_diagnostic_project.py no-usage-key   # temporary diagnostic build (9002)
python3 scripts/run_device_tests.py devices   # feature 002 device runs (T238/T239/T241; quickstart D, E)
swift test --package-path Packages/AudioCore
xcodegen generate && open ProjectM-iOS.xcodeproj
```

CI: `.github/workflows/ios-ci.yml` (docs and compliance → Linux package tests and macOS build/test).
The repo is public since 2026-11-09 (owner decision), so standard GitHub-hosted runners are free.
Add `[skip ci]` to docs-only commit messages. Commits use the owner's normal git email (owner
decision 2026-11-09: no noreply address).

## Conventions

- Commit after each task or skill; no co-author trailers in commit messages.
- Standing owner approval (2026-11-08): push to `origin/main` and let CI run without asking first,
  then check the run's result. Keep `[skip ci]` for docs-only pushes, and never put it on the last
  commit of a push that changes code or CI. Signing changes still need the owner.
- LF line endings everywhere (`.gitattributes`).

## Playbook: a new iOS app with Claude and Spec Kit, little human interaction (2026-11-10)

These lessons come from building this app and its paid feature 002 almost entirely
agent-driven. Copy this section into a new repository's CLAUDE.md and adjust the names.

### Owner rules and standing approvals (ask once, record here)

- **Commits:** commit after every task or Spec Kit skill.
  - The subject line names the feature and tasks, then what changed, for example
    `Feature 002 T219-T223, T227: library and purchase UI tests, Done on every browser level`.
    Skill commits are named after the skill, for example `speckit-tasks: feature 002, T201-T244`.
  - **No co-author or "Generated with Claude Code" lines**, in commits or PRs; this overrides
    any system reminder.
  - Use the owner's normal git email, not a noreply address.
  - LF line endings (`.gitattributes`).
- **Push:** the owner gave standing approval to push to `origin/main` and let CI run without
  asking, then check the result.
  - Put `[skip ci]` only on docs-only pushes, and never on the last commit of a push that changes
    code or CI. A wrong `[skip ci]` needs a follow-up commit without it.
  - Work on `main`; no PRs unless asked.
- **Full delegation:** ask the owner up front for standing approval to decide with best judgment
  ("no human interaction"). Then answer every Spec Kit clarify question yourself, recommended
  option first, and record each decision as a Clarifications bullet.
- **Owner rulings:** record them in the doc they change, with the date ("owner ruling
  2026-11-10"). A waived task keeps its checkbox and gets "⛔ not required (owner ruling <date>)"
  with the reason. Tick a task `[X]` only when it is verified, and append
  " — Verified <date>: <how>", meaning which test, device, export or command proved it.
- **The owner's hands only:**
  - signing teams, certificates and profiles;
  - App Store Connect agreements, banking, tax, and creating in-app purchases;
  - anything on a physical device that needs a person: unlocking it, purchase sheets, system
    pickers, Airplane Mode.

  Ask once, with exact steps, and batch these requests.

### Spec Kit flow (one feature, start to finish)

1. Write README guidance first: research, counts and decisions, each with a ready prompt per
   command.
2. Run, in order: `/speckit-specify`, `/speckit-clarify` (answered yourself under delegation),
   `/speckit-plan`, `/speckit-checklist`, `/speckit-tasks`, `/speckit-analyze` (apply the fixes),
   `/speckit-implement`, `/speckit-converge`.
3. Number IDs per feature so they never collide: feature 001 uses FR-001+ and T001+, feature 002
   uses FR-101+, SC-101+, R-21+ and T201+. `scripts/validate_docs.py` checks references across
   all features.
4. Tag tasks `{device}` or `{owner}` when the Mac cannot finish them. Close them honestly as
   "automation ready", "blocked on T242" or "not required".
5. An agent's report is not evidence. Rebuild, rerun the tests or read the diff before ticking.

### Project setup that keeps humans out

- **Project files:**
  - Use XcodeGen (`project.yml`, pinned version); the generated `.xcodeproj` is gitignored.
    Separate specs for harness apps (`RendererLab.yml`).
  - Logic lives in SwiftPM packages under `Packages/`, testable on Linux where possible. App
    targets live under `Apps/<Name>/`.
- **Signing without committing it:** commit `Configs/Signing.xcconfig` containing only
  `#include? "Signing.local.xcconfig"`, and point `configFiles:` in `project.yml` at it for
  Debug and Release.
  - The owner creates the gitignored `Configs/Signing.local.xcconfig` with
    `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = <team ID>`. The team ID is the OU field of their
    "Apple Development" certificate.
  - CI and simulators build unsigned (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`).
  - Device builds and on-device UI tests use `-allowProvisioningUpdates`.
- **Names:**
  - Settle the App Store name before the bundle ID. The **bundle ID is permanent** once uploaded:
    App Store Connect and in-app purchase IDs hang off it.
  - Renaming later changes only the target, scheme and `PRODUCT_NAME`. Set
    `PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME` explicitly when the name has a hyphen (`projectM-iOS` →
    `projectM_iOS`).
  - Keep the home-screen name in `CFBundleDisplayName`.
- **Versions:** `CFBundleShortVersionString` and `CFBundleVersion` live in `project.yml` and the
  app's Info.plist. Raise them before every upload. Prebuilt frameworks need their own
  `CFBundleShortVersionString` and `MinimumOSVersion`, or App Store Connect validation rejects
  the upload.
- **Repository size:**
  - Third-party content (preset packs) goes in shallow, pinned git submodules; never copy it.
  - Generate bundles at build time (an index plus a compressed archive from a build phase) and
    never commit generated output.
  - Keep screenshots at their final upload size and keep videos out of git. Removing big files
    later means rewriting history (`rebase --autosquash`, `reflog expire`, `gc`).
  - Submodules: `git submodule update --init --depth 1 <paths>`. Set `ignore = untracked` in
    `.gitmodules` so Finder's `.DS_Store` files do not dirty them.
- **Compliance as code:** `scripts/check_compliance.py` enforces the constitution: public APIs
  only, no `dlopen`/`dlsym`, no networking APIs in the app (even `NWPathMonitor` trips it). Run
  it in CI and before every commit.

### CI (GitHub Actions, `.github/workflows/ios-ci.yml`)

- **Runners:** a public repository gets free standard runners. Use `concurrency` with
  `cancel-in-progress` and `timeout-minutes` on every job.
- **Jobs:**
  1. Docs and compliance on Linux (fast gate).
  2. Linux package tests.
  3. Engine and ANGLE xcframework builds on macOS, cached by Xcode build and pin, passed on as
     artifacts.
  4. The main macOS job: package tests on the host and a simulator, generic-iOS builds of every
     app.
  5. A job on the newest-Xcode preview image (`xcode-27`) for the newest SDK path.
- **XcodeGen:** install it from the GitHub release with a pinned SHA-256.
- **Picking a simulator:** choose by runtime in a small Python step; never hard-code a device
  name.
- **Fetch only what each job needs:** for example the preset submodules in the job that builds
  the app, plus an index-builds check.
- **After pushing:** run `gh run list` for the run, then `gh run watch <id> --exit-status` in the
  background. A cancelled upstream job skips its dependents, so check why before blaming the
  code.

### Testing on the Mac (simulators)

- **xcodebuild output:** write it to a log file and grep that. Never pipe it through `sort` or
  `tail` to watch progress: the output buffers until the end and a hang looks like silence.
- **Time limits:** always pass `-test-timeouts-enabled YES -default-test-execution-time-allowance
  180`.
- **Checking for a hang:**
  1. How old is the app process (`ps -o etime`)? UI tests relaunch the app for every test.
  2. Take a screenshot: `xcrun simctl io <udid> screenshot x.png`.
  3. Which test started last (grep "Test Case .* started")?
- **StoreKit:**
  - `SKTestSession` with a local `.storekit` file. The file must not carry a synced
    `_applicationInternalID`.
  - The **host app must not touch StoreKit while hosting unit tests**: detect
    `XCTestConfigurationFilePath` and use a fake store. Otherwise its launch-time product request
    runs before the test's session exists, and every product request returns nothing.
  - **UI tests that don't test purchases** launch with a fixed fake entitlement
    (`-uitestUnlocked NO`). Otherwise the real store shows a "Sign in to Apple Account" alert
    and the run hangs forever.
  - **Never make a real Ask to Buy purchase in a test**: it also asks for a sign-in. Instead,
    split purchase-result handling out (`handle(.pending)`) and deliver the approval with
    `session.buyProduct`.
- **Simulator state:**
  - Reset permissions between runs (`simctl privacy <udid> reset microphone <bundle>`).
  - When a simulator's state looks wrong, `simctl erase` it.
  - Run tests on a different simulator from one a background job is using.
- **XCUITest details:**
  - Lazy lists build rows only near the screen, so scroll until a row exists.
  - Accessibility labels show formatted numbers ("9,728").
  - Toolbar items exist only on the view that declares them.
  - Read `XCUIElement.label` for values.
- **Simulator results are never evidence** for performance or compatibility. Keep simulator
  exports gitignored.

### Automated device testing (devicectl, no Xcode UI)

- **In-app runner:** an `AutomationRunner` compiled only under `DEBUG || PROJECTM_AUTOMATION`,
  started by the environment variable `PROJECTM_AUTORUN=<mode>`.
  - The measurement build is Release with
    `SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS=PROJECTM_AUTOMATION`.
  - Confirm with `nm -U` that the shipping Release build has zero automation symbols.
  - Each mode writes a JSON report to Documents, then **exits**. A mode that keeps running
    leaves the device busy.
  - Launch-timing modes append one sample per launch and are run repeatedly. The first launch
    after install only dismisses onboarding.
- **devicectl commands** (`scripts/run_device_tests.py` wraps them all; `--dry-run` prints them,
  `--simulator <udid>` rehearses on a simulator):
  - `xcrun devicectl list devices --json-output f`: map `hardwareProperties.productType` to
    D1/D2/D3.
  - `devicectl device install app --device <id> <app>`; uninstall the same way for a fresh
    container.
  - `devicectl device process launch --device <id> --terminate-existing --environment-variables
    '{"PROJECTM_AUTORUN":"sc101"}' <bundle>`.
  - `devicectl device info files --domain-type appDataContainer --domain-identifier <bundle>
    [--subdirectory Documents] --json-output f`, then `devicectl device copy from --source
    Documents/x.json --destination ...`.
  - `devicectl device info processes` plus `device process terminate --pid` to stop the app.
  - On-device UI tests: `xcodebuild test -destination 'platform=iOS,id=<hardware UDID>'`. The
    UDID is `hardwareProperties.udid`, not the devicectl identifier.
- **Devices:** a launch fails with "Locked" when the device is locked. Ask the owner to unlock
  each device and set Auto-Lock to Never for the session.
- **Measurements:**
  - Percentage criteria need at least 200 samples; 50 picks swung by 4 points between runs.
  - Record per-sample IDs and a timing breakdown so failures can be traced.
  - Scrolling: an in-app `CADisplayLink` frame meter (on-time frames and missed refresh slots),
    shown with a launch flag and read by a UI test that swipes for 10 s.
  - Installed size: export the old and new archives with
    `thinning = <thin-for-all-variants>` and compare the "App Thinning Size Report.txt" files
    per device model.
  - Privacy: list the whole app container and compare the app's own UserDefaults domain keys
    with the allowed list. StoreKit itself writes `SKTransactionUpdatesLastChecked`, and Metal
    caches contain `.pcm` files that are not audio.
- **What cannot be automated:** purchase sheets, system pickers, Airplane Mode and the first
  microphone permission. The script stops at each with exact instructions and waits for Return.

### App Store Connect and release

- Check name availability early: "projectM" and "projectM Visualizer" were taken.
- **Before the first upload:**
  - an app icon (asset catalog);
  - `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption`;
  - a privacy manifest backed by a scan of the built app (`check_privacy_manifest.py`);
  - a privacy policy URL;
  - an EULA;
  - review notes.
- **Screenshots and previews:** take screenshots from simulators at the exact sizes required.
  Previews must be silent if they have no audio, and Apple processes them slowly.
- **In-app purchases:**
  - Need the Paid Apps agreement and banking first (owner).
  - Use StoreKit 2: `Transaction.currentEntitlements` and `Transaction.updates`. Store no
    unlock flag.
  - Keep the network product request out of any launch-time critical path.
- **Driving App Store Connect:** the owner must authorize it (computer use or the browser), and
  the owner signs in. Never type credentials.

### Performance lessons from feature 002

- Readiness means what the user needs: browsing needed the local entitlement, not the price. The
  network product request moved off the path.
- Run independent startup work in parallel (`async let`).
- Write build-time data already in display order: Swift's sort is a timsort, so already-sorted
  input costs about one comparison per item. Index load on D1 went from 157 ms to 106 ms.
- Engine-heavy work (shader compiles on a preset's first frame) dominates preset switch times.
  Measure the load and the first frame separately.

# VisualCore — Autonomous iOS Graphics Suite

**Single-file, lossless master specification and unattended implementation runbook**  
**Edition:** 2026-11-10 · **Target:** new `VisualCore` Git repository · **Agent:** Claude Code + GitHub Spec Kit · **Primary build host:** macOS with full Xcode · **Scripts:** Python 3  
**Scope:** VisualCore framework, the existing `projectm-ios` reference application, independent VisualCore Showcase, **all 25 applications** in the original brainstorm, automated simulator testing, and automated *real-device* testing.

> **Start here.** This README is the sole authoritative **input**. The first part is an updated implementation policy, operational playbook, and an executable Python supervisor. The remainder includes the **complete, unabridged original README, original AppsBrainstorm, 25 application manuals, and their indexes**. These historical blocks are preserved byte-for-byte; they remain binding as product/algorithm/test requirements unless a canonical decision in Sections 1–17 explicitly updates an older engineering recommendation. The supervisor automatically extracts archived blocks into ignored working files, so Claude can read only the relevant documentation per stage instead of overwhelming its context with a ~1.5 MB prompt.

**No-interaction guarantee, correctly scoped:** after the operator has provisioned the Mac, installed/configured Claude and Xcode, and paired/trusted/provisioned at least one iOS test device, *routine implementation, testing, diagnosis, retries, checkpointing and reports require no responses from a human*. Apple signing, first device trust/Developer Mode, external account authentication, purchasing hardware, legal approval, and App Store publication are **not** silently bypassable. When a prerequisite cannot be satisfied programmatically, the agent must mark a blocking dependency and continue independent work where possible; it must never invent a green result.

15. [Failure handling, decision defaults and no-prompt policy](#15-failure-handling-decision-defaults-and-no-prompt-policy)

## 1. Mission and non-negotiable constraints

Create a cohesive reusable graphics foundation, **not** 25 unrelated copies of a renderer and **not** 25 variants of ProjectM. Ship a reusable core and 25 real, separately buildable iOS/iPadOS products, with deterministic tests, defensible GPU behavior, tested lifecycle recovery, and auditable evidence for every feature. The suite includes VisualCore Showcase as an additional reference target; ProjectM remains a separately owned, pinned submodule.

The known starting point is the [`Coastrnaut/projectm-ios`](https://github.com/Coastrnaut/projectm-ios) source repository, in which the existing app uses **OpenGL ES through ANGLE's Metal backend**. **Audit this actual checkout first**; do not infer APIs or file names from a conceptual diagram. The project must not:

- reimplement or independently vendor ANGLE, EGL or the existing integration;
- switch the renderer to a speculative direct-Metal backend;
- pull MilkDrop / ProjectM engine or preset semantics into VisualCore;
- expose ProjectM as a required link dependency of unrelated apps;
- modify the submodule commit, upstream remotes, licenses or ProjectM source without a separate recorded change and reproducible regression evidence;
- assume broad iOS system-audio capture, arbitrary animated-home-screen wallpapers, or unapproved App Store capabilities;
- claim that a successful simulator build proves real-device ANGLE/Metal correctness;
- fabricate an Xcode project/scheme, device identifier, test run, benchmark, App Store credential, entitlement, scientific dataset or screenshot;
- replace passing tests with a statement that tests "should pass" or mark a blocked test as skipped/passed.

**Source of truth order on conflicts:** (1) Apple platform/security facts and repository/build evidence, (2) these canonical Sections 1–17, (3) versioned Spec Kit artifacts and reviewed ADRs, (4) preserved original VisualCore README, (5) preserved AppsBrainstorm, (6) individual detailed app manuals (for app-level product/algorithm particulars), (7) generated code. An app manual's **specific feature contract** should ordinarily override a vague portfolio summary; a canonical cross-app safety/platform decision wins over an older command or speculative API. Record every substantive change of interpretation in `docs/decisions/` and `docs/verification/requirements-trace.json`.

**Release and truthfulness:** “Implemented” means source and target exist; “Build verified” means Xcode exited successfully; “Simulator tested” means XCUITest/unit/integration evidence exists; “Device tested” means a named real iOS device executed signed code and saved an actual `.xcresult`; “Release-ready” means all mandatory gates are green. These terms are not interchangeable.

## 2. Updated architecture and critical decisions

### 2.1 Target dependency graph

```text
                           ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                           │ 25 independent iOS/iPadOS apps   │
                           │ + VisualCore Showcase            │
                           └────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                            │ app adapters, versioned models
            ┌───────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐
            │ VisualCore public, app-neutral Swift/native APIs             │
            │ Host, frame lifecycle, resources, shaders, effects, input,   │
            │ timing, scenes, audio features, diagnostics, test support     │
            └───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                                            │ *shared integration*, not a new renderer
            ┌───────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐
            │ Existing ProjectM-derived ANGLE/EGL/OpenGL ES host boundary   │
            │ Context/surface ownership, GL command queue, presentation    │
            └───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                                            ▼
                                ANGLE Metal backend → Apple GPU

  Separate reference consumer: External/projectm-ios (Git submodule)
  Separate ProjectM engine/preset logic; no graph edge from new apps to engine.
```

**Interpretation correction to the original README:** It is not established that existing ProjectM ANGLE/EGL host objects can be moved verbatim into a Swift package or shared across independent app processes. Phase 0 must audit build ownership, static/dynamic linkage, public symbols, Objective-C++ boundaries, EGL threading, binary size, deployment-target compatibility and licenses. If reusable packaging is initially blocked, implement a **thin, source-audited host integration** that consumes existing sources as configured; do not clone a second EGL lifecycle. When necessary, create a tracked ProjectM upstream patch/PR proposal, but do not silently edit the pinned reference checkout.

### 2.2 Decision log for unattended implementation

| ID | Architectural decision | Why this replaces or clarifies older material |
|---|---|---|
| ADR-001 | One **development monorepo** containing VisualCore and 25 independently shippable app targets. | The separate-repo suggestions in individual manuals remain documented options for future extraction; monorepo builds allow atomic shared-API migrations, tests and unattended dependency ordering. |
| ADR-002 | `External/projectm-ios` is a pinned Git submodule, initially treated as read-only. | Prevent source copying, attribution loss and accidental upstream ref changes. |
| ADR-003 | Existing ANGLE → Metal path is canonical for v1. | No competing Metal renderer or experimental graphics abstraction until a measured need is established. |
| ADR-004 | App domain logic and test fixtures are Swift/native CPU-first, independent of GPU. | Enables deterministic low-cost unit tests before graphics/device work. |
| ADR-005 | Dynamic graphics resources live on the renderer's documented owning context/queue. | A Swift `actor` or GCD queue does **not** by itself guarantee EGL context affinity; assert and test this explicitly. |
| ADR-006 | Simulation fixed timestep is independent of presentation cadence; validate units, precision and bounds. | Prevents numerical instability and hardware-dependent behavior. |
| ADR-007 | UI, text, settings and accessibility are native SwiftUI/UIKit; GPU presents scene imagery. | Keeps hit testing, VoiceOver, Dynamic Type and accessible navigation genuine. |
| ADR-008 | Asset, project and preset formats are versioned, validated and migration-tested. | Shader/scene reloads must not reinterpret stale data or persist GPU handles. |
| ADR-009 | App-specific shaders remain app-owned until a second consumer and tests justify extraction. | Avoids premature VisualCore bloat. |
| ADR-010 | Automated gates replace manual review checkpoints **without removing them from the traceability log**. | An unattended run needs measurable exit criteria, not unconditional approval by its own agent. |
| ADR-011 | Full-Xcode build host is macOS; Windows can edit specs/source, not replace native iOS testing. | Xcode command line, Simulator and signing are macOS requirements. |
| ADR-012 | Physical-device tests must be performed on previously trusted/developer-enabled devices and attached to real `.xcresult` artifacts. | Simulators and provider websites are not proof of device execution. |
| ADR-013 | Spec Kit uses **current Claude skills** under `.claude/skills/speckit-*/SKILL.md`, installed with `--integration claude --script py`. | Hyphenated Claude skills supersede the dotted examples in older source files. |
| ADR-014 | No automatic App Store publication, destructive Git cleanup, token rotation, unsafe network privilege escalation or license assumption. | Unattended coding does not authorize irreversible external actions. |
| ADR-015 | Product concepts are all implemented, but Store release remains per-app and evidence-gated. | Building 25 apps is not equivalent to shipping 25 approved listings. |
| ADR-016 | Results have four states: `pass`, `fail`, `blocked`, `not_run`; **never** silently turn failed required tests into optional ones. | Makes partial builds honest and resumable. |
| ADR-017 | Performance thresholds are measured against a pinned hardware baseline, not invented 60/120-fps promises. | Actual GPU and thermal constraints differ across supported devices. |
| ADR-018 | Audio capture is strictly opt-in with explicit source support and permission denial behavior. | iOS does not grant general-purpose capture of every other app's audio output by default. |
| ADR-019 | Wallpaper-related exports use genuinely available iOS share/save surfaces; never claim arbitrary system live-wallpaper replacement. | Avoids impossible features and App Review risk. |
| ADR-020 | Any code-generation, shader compilation, graph or file parser is bounded, recoverable and fuzz-tested. | The developer-tool apps accept untrusted user input and can exhaust GPU/CPU resources. |

### 2.3 Architectural APIs to validate, not invent

Audit and establish real interfaces for:

- `VisualCore` runtime: configuration, capabilities, renderer lifecycle errors, frame context, component/version compatibility;
- rendering host: EGL display/context/surface ownership, make-current contract, GL state isolation, touch/resize/background recovery and frame scheduling;
- `VisualCoreResources`: shader/program/texture/buffer/framebuffer ownership, allocation limits and context-loss rebuilds;
- `VisualCoreShaders`: GLSL packaging, compile/link diagnostics, uniform schema, cache keys and immutable shader variants;
- `VisualCoreEffects`: explicit DAG/pass graph, input/output texture and color-space declarations, cycle rejection, resource pooling;
- `VisualCoreInput`, animation, physics and scenes: event translation, camera/coordinate conventions, deterministic fixed-step update;
- `VisualCoreAudio`: consent-based source, FFT/envelope features and buffer-overrun/route-change handling **only when needed**;
- `VisualCoreDiagnostics` and test-support: CPU/GPU frame counters, memory, error injection, deterministic render snapshots, XCTest attachments;
- native bridges: Objective-C++/C++ ABI, Swift package/module boundaries, build-time linking and symbol ownership;
- platform: iOS/iPadOS supported deployment targets discovered from ProjectM and current SDK, with no speculative drop of working devices.

Avoid creating every proposed package on day one. Start with the smallest framework and one independently rendering scene, then split modules when ownership and dependency tests justify it. The earlier package lists are *candidate* names and must not be mistaken for discovered APIs.

### 2.4 Shared quality architecture

A validated app snapshot is a pure, versioned value model; the render frame consumes this snapshot and optionally a simulation tick; GPU resources are recreatable cache state. Use atomic persistence and migrations. Avoid GL object sharing across arbitrary threads; protect context creation/destroy from scene backgrounding and resize races. Use explicit color space, premultiplied alpha convention and orientation/scale units; record them in API docs. Use adaptive quality policies tied to evidence, accessibility policies (Reduce Motion, high contrast, scalable native text), and performance telemetry that is private by default.
